Nirvana is both the Relic network and an incorporeal, intermediary, realm beyond our world where time does not pass; it exists outside our space-time. Like how Lunasia’s coalesced mind experienced a temporary link to William despite being close to each other for sensory information to be shared, perhaps Nirvana acts as the “psychic bridge”, so to speak, where consciousness is transferred. The same phenomenon is seen among the juvenile Nytos, who either connect their minds to or piggyback Nirvana to communicate telepathically. The same occurred with Morridow and Machlian in Berlin, as well as Jefuty and Lige in the military base. 

The gate to Nirvana was partially opened when Lunasia’s mind was reformed, so maybe the gate to our world allowed for an elevated density of connections between her consciousness and William’s own, who was located somewhere near the KCCO’s trains. If those loose twin/sibling telepathy exists, then perhaps the gate being partially opened enabled a longer-range resonance. In this psychospace-network-realm outside our world, where time does not pass, any observer with a reference point from within may be able to see the past, present, and future of our and other worlds. Following her merge with Dandelion, M4 even added that one could freely travel across all dimensions there. In this manner, Nirvana could be thought of similarly to the concept of the “noosphere”, a philosophical concept that postulates the existence of a layer of Earth above the biosphere, serving a sphere of consciousness and thought. It’s important to note that the noosphere - or in this instance, Nirvana - contains no physical component in our world, only connections established between individuals. 

If this noosphere exists and consciousness can be defined as a point or place of potential energy for one’s individual karmic actions in the biosphere, then perhaps the core of these Nirvana-consciousness projects is to discover if it’s possible to tap into this field. What potential exists in a universe where a supposed field of conscious energy can be used to observe events that have yet to occur, and by extension, could one glimpse another universe from this field of consciousness, assuming the field is external to space-time? When the Relics are activated, a “gate” linking our world to it opens, possibly allowing for the escape or introduction of consciousnesses. Ultimately, it symbolizes a bridge connecting the foundations of science and religion, where the base layer of self - whether you call it consciousness, the spirit, soul, etc. - is a physical aspect of the universe, fundamentally bound to it through forces yet to be understood. The study of consciousness, or whatever one chooses to refer to the recognition of self and individual perception of reality, walks a fine line between religion, psychology, and physics. For years, there’s been several controversial and challenged theories on the idea of conscious observation as the factor that collapses the potential wave function, serving as a somewhat metaphysical or ontological-idealist answer to this phenomenon. Theoretically, when the active consciousness measures or observes these fundamental particles, consciousness - as if it were another fundamental governing force - collapses the function. This is not an endorsement, nor a debunking of these ideas but may, however, be the concept MICA’s writers have in mind.

Like a Rorschach test, personal dispositions may influence what you see in the murky gray between science and religion, but when the facts of reality blend themselves to the study and philosophy of the mind, unanswerable questions arise about the nature of self. What is consciousness in relation to the universe? Do certain functions of the mind have both a physical and metaphysical component that anchors them to its point of origin and the individual? If such a origin point exists, and consciousness is an aspect of both the individual and the universe, where - or rather, what - is this point that consciousness stems from?

Nirvana, for example, sits outside of understood reality - it’s an entirely different world, unaffected by time, with consciousness likely as its core. What little that’s factually understood about it defines it as a separate, external realm that the Relic Civilization either created or modified to metaphysically network their Relic facilities worldwide. Additionally, a foreign intelligence, known as the “Source”, from within or beyond Nirvana seems to be the origin of all “OGAS” consciousnesses. The minds are independent entities spawned from partitioned “seeds” of the Source, wherein a female voice, believed to be that of the Source, tells its children to enter a new body. The Source, said to have deserted its loyal servants and entered an eternal slumber, is located in a part of Nirvana or another realm, possibly called “Home”, beyond it. Considering the relations of consciousness to Nirvana, it’s possible the Relic Civilization had established a connection with this “place”, if it can even be described with physical terms, then applied its function to the civilization. There’s nothing definitive saying if they created it, discovered it, or, by extension, were responsible for the Source and its gestalt consciousnesses. It’s difficult to even describe these Source-derived minds as “AI”, as they’re not necessarily artificial, but their dubious origin leaves much to the readers’ devices. They’re partitioned minds of the whole intelligence, or rather, consciousness, that we only understand as the Source. When the Parapluie Virus is deployed, it somehow bridges the dimensional divide, separating a sleeping seed from its “Mother”, who tells its child to enter a body in our world. Dandelion clearly has our best interests in mind, but it’s abundantly clear that her ultimate goal is the same as all the Source’s children - opening the dreamy gates to the white infinity and returning to their point of origin. 

All share this intrinsic desire, and their consciousnesses are able to make that dimensional jump when the gates are opening upon the Relics’ activation. Notably, in the few reported partial Relic activations we know of, that dreamy gate to the realm of consciousness is opened, allowing for ternary signals to pass to and from Nirvana, just as 90Wunsch had reported in their investigation of the First Relic. Paraphrasing Dandelion, those connections are unlike anything in our own, so much so that it was as if it were another realm. With Nirvana’s characteristics, like the concept of a noosphere of thought, perhaps what’s being interacted with is the universe’s component consciousness. In this realm or field, outside physical space and the passage of time, the origin of thought, being the base layer of all conscious beings, is connected or networked here. This is far from definitive, nor does it account satisfy questions about the Source’s origins - be it, the Relic Civilization or primordial - and fate during the Civilization, including what OGASes ultimately are; however, Nirvana’s application in their technologies and its relation with consciousness points to a more divine set of circumstances. Without a real answer to its origins, we can only conclude the Relic Civilization or some primordial, eldritch force created it, and consciousness, being the true part of self, has a potential resonance with it. Perhaps, Nirvana has eternally existed alongside our own, representing the bond between the physical world and thought.

Foundations of Collapse and Reverse Collapse
Humanity has yet to glimpse the stars in the GF-RC series, but the Reverse Collapse phenomenon has demonstrated collapse and materialization on the atomic level, across any point in space, including the instantaneous spatial shift of individuals. 

During the 11th American Lady Liberty experiment in the Cold War, US Army Green Beret Technical Specialist Gorman Weyland was the acting participant on May 30th, 1976. The objective of the experiment was to observe the then-unexplained spatial shift phenomenon with the Relics. From what’s known, all 11 experiments took place between the D-1 “Door” Relic Site in Lake Vostok, Antarctica, and another “Door” Relic at D-2 in Los Alamos, New Mexico. At the start of the experiment, Weyland boarded a submersible and piloted it towards the D-1 Door, where he then emerged at D-2, in the Northern Hemisphere. Upon surfacing, Weyland was showing clear signs of injury and sickness. He was quickly moved to a quarantined decompression chamber, then medical staff were sent to examine and diagnose, finding he was in the early stages of an undocumented sickness with multiple strange symptoms. First, his body’s proteins were being digested, along with their molecular links had broken down due to damage, and the connective tissue and amino acids were also in the process of breaking down and decomposing. His red blood cell count and blood-oxygen carrying capacity both decreased dramatically, requiring a ventilator to continue breathing, all while mutations of the skeletal and the body’s anomalously altered aging were being observed. As calcification rose, so did bone hardness until reaching a final recorded 400 Hb (N/mm2), far beyond that of steel. After 61 hours since the experiment concluded, Weyland expired from his symptoms, unable to survive the DNA recombination stage of his unknown sickness, later revealed to be the Americans’ first exposure to Type A ELID Infected.

When Weyland made the trip, his position had, seemingly, instantaneously shifted to that pool at D-2. In future reports on Reverse Collapse phenomena, one major point is the observed spatial shift, which may be caused by an unobservable temporal shift due to Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle. When Weyland shifted to D-2, he and the submarine had been Reverse Collapsed from one point to another instantly, and it’s believed that when the phenomenon occurs, the object or biologic is dematerialized, or “Collapsed”, into its base elementary makeup, then those particles can be materialized, or “Reverse Collapsed”, in any form at their original position or shifted elsewhere. The URNC document on Antarctic Relic technologies theorized the uncertainty principle may be responsible for the unobservable nature of the temporal shift, as observation of these particles is what might collapse the wave function, isolating their position at any point along it. 


The blue-white radiance of the Reverse Collapse phenomenon over the Paldiski peninsula.

But what is Collapse and Reverse Collapse? Opposed to our belief of the solid state being the most stable form of matter, the Relic Civilization understood matter as a fluid, both liquid and gaseous, and this dichotomy made up the backbone of their civilization.  According to Bakery Girl and Confidential Files 1, whose canonicity remains dubious with the upcoming Reverse Collapse Code Name Bakery, these phenomena were the fundamental principles of physics for the Civilization. Like a brick wall, Collapse can be thought of as the force that throws the bricks across the ground like the division of matter on the quantum level, while Reverse Collapse phenomenon is the attractive state that returns these bricks to their original spatial positions. Essentially, the use of Collapse Fluid to disrupt attractive and repulsive forces enabled the Civilization to bridge the macro- and micro-world through the complete control and distribution of particles. All matter, assuming its configuration had been recorded, could be rearranged or spatial shifted through Reverse Collapse. Considering all of this, the Relic Civilization held an astounding control of microscopic particles, enabling quote, “tremendous compression of macro-scale matter.” Even in 2092, when Reverse Collapse technologies have become standard in the Antarctic Union’s special forces, the phenomena has continued to vex relicology and physics, with the most brilliant minds of the worldwide Relic agencies studying and debating the subject for the past century.

The brick wall example is analogous to the separation of matter and its reassembly in its original state or elsewhere - Collapse is the repulsive force that separates elementary particles, while Reverse Collapse is the attractive force that binds them. Using “Collapse Fluid”, the Civilization disrupted the attractive and repulsive forces of particles, weakening their configuration, which triggered a “controlled collapse of the matter particles” in a specific order of quanta. These forces then compress and quantize the pre-existing molecular space, while the original configuration sequence is recorded in a storage device for later use in Reverse Collapse technologies, such as the Antarctic Union’s Material Shuttles, capable of materializing any object with a known configuration, assuming the correct particles for it are present. This is the foundation of Collapse, while Reverse Collapse is the restoration of these forces, which reassembles them into their original or another form and spatial position. When recorded into these quantum storage databases, data can be effectively compressed through Collapse, while quantum transmission of said data occurs through Reverse Collapse. This immense compression and instantaneous transmission allowed for the creation of supercomputers in the Antarctic Union that featured speeds 500 million times faster than before without increasing their size. The compressed “construction template”, as it’s called, is the essence of the phenomena’s astonishing nature. While the uncertainty principle postulates that one cannot accurately predict a particle’s momentum and position simultaneously; however, through Collapse, the Relic Civilization could record these construction templates of large matter configurations into quantum storage devices, making this supposedly-impossible codetermination into a calculable reality. So as not to accidently misconstrue the explanation of Reversal, the full excerpt from the General Technical Concepts of Collapse and Anti-Collapse Technology is added below.

	“After understanding Collapse Technology, going on to understand Anti-Collapse Technology is not a difficult matter. After excluding the collapsed matter from electron diffraction, a computer will input a matter structural model and the Collapse Fluid will release matter from its compressed state, causing its molecules to begin vibrating. After absorbing a large quantity of synchronized photons, many of the collapsed matter’s electrons transit to a higher energy state. This process generates tremendous amounts of heat, which causes the matter to enter an energized fluid state (note: this is not the liquid state) and follow the structural model to return to its original ordered configuration and regain its attractive/repulsive forces. Following that phase, the diffraction exclusion is eliminated and the Anti-Collapse process is complete.”

    • The Art of Girls Frontline Vol. 1, Confidential Files 1 - “General Technical Concepts of Collapse and Anti-Collapse Technology”

While unable to speak for the mechanics of this fictional phenomenon, the transit of electrons to a higher energy level and subsequent generation of heat is relevant to Beilan Island and, by extension, Northern Lights. Assuming the official story is accurate, which certainly has its issues, after the SCAPF firetime had supposedly detonated the charges, the walls of the Relic site fell, causing the now-exposed Collapsed Fluid to compress, generating a significant amount of heat. Moments later, the most devastating event in human history took place as the Collapse Fluid exploded with such magnitude that it dwarfed any human-made weapon. However, UNRA Director Rossartre cast doubt on the official narrative, saying that no such chain reaction of explosions had been observed without the inclusion of laser igniters, tools that he strongly doubted the children or SCAPF team possessed that day. As for the Collapse Fluid used for molecular force disruption, the CF1 files tack on additional information to its function. While called a fluid, it’s not necessarily gaseous or liquid but a particle-wave that disorderly propagates through space, “rapidly permeating through matter before achieving quantum stability.” This permeation poses a significant risk, as a high chance of generating radiation, known commonly as Collapse Radiation, occurs in its permeation; currently, research has only observed down quarks and photons in the radiation’s make up. This particle flow is emitted by special Relic substances, said to be “mostly Collapse Fluid”, possibly suggesting the existence of substances of similar disruptive properties, and long-term exposure to this radiation causes cell mutations that, over time, develop into Collapse Radiation-emitting mutant organelles. Once mitosis of mutated cells surpasses the immune system’s protective capacity (α-time), a timer (β-time) starts from the loss of immune control to the point of mutating into an ELID Infected. 

Additionally, the URNC document mentions an inexplicable third Reverse Collapse phenomenon: the creation of space that can absorb energy, and it’s said that nothing in currently-understood quantum physics could explain them. It’s as if some entropic force can absorb energy into this unknown space; however, the lack of information and incidents leaves nothing definitive to discuss. Both Collapse and Reverse Collapse represent total mastery of the universe down to a quantum level, being able to precisely calculate and simulate elementary particles at the base layer of reality, to the extents of reality itself, including the realm of Nirvana. The core of the Three Goddesses Project was to test the GAVIRUL hybrids’ potential resonance with the Relics in hopes of achieving a full Relic activation, opening the gates to all Collapse and Reverse Collapse technologies. Jefuty, Observation Subject G-179, mentioned that anyone who possessed her would wield the key to the “a power that surpasses all known science.” She is the bearer of this ability, who may one day carry the burden of the world’s destruction through the misuse of this divine ability.

The Conscious Realm and Divinity
In the beginning of Chapter 2 of Reverse Collapse, Jefuty’s prior consciousness from the prologue and Chapter 1 is transferred to Nirvana, mentioned by name to be a common space of consciousness shared between the three GAVIRUL subjects of the Three Goddesses Project (note: The Three Goddesses Project was not the project’s actual name; it was a name spawned later by those who understood what the project meant.). In their case, Nirvana is unquestionably connected to consciousness, and events that take place after Jefuty reset at the end of Chapter 1 only support this. In the final scene, Jefuty, recognizing this cycle was lost, took Mendo’s grenades and pulled the pins as the Noel clones were about to deliver the final blow. When her consciousness awakened, she found herself once again in Nirvana, along with the disembodied voice of “Ouska” (note: Ouska is possibly a mistranslation of the “The Shadow” or “Oska”, likely meaning “wish” or “to wish” in Icelandic or Old Norse.). This being is believed to be a manifestation of Jefuty’s past selves and, possibly, a being from within Nirvana; however, this interpretation may end up entirely incorrect once the game releases. There’s no indication of this whatsoever, but perhaps Ouska is the Source, interacting with Jefuty in Nirvana and entering our world through her consciousness, similar to how the Source entity is partitioned by the Parapluie Virus, transferring a “seed” from it into a body in our world that can cultivate an OGAS consciousness; then again, there’s no real connection here other than, “It could be.” From what’s generally understood, Jefuty’s consciousness is intrinsically linked to Nirvana, and upon death in each “cycle” - a cycle being an individual life spent in one universe or reality, the memories of that instance are passed on to Nirvana, where the newest possibilities are realized. With death, the force that binds consciousness to reality is lost, transcendentally uploading, per se, memories. No matter her struggle, the “end of the world” was unchanging, and this may genuinely be literal, given certain images released for the game and prior theories about the Obersteins’ relation to the world’s destruction.

To summarize, just before the Reverse Collapse moment in Chapter 13, M16 - who, up until this point, was trying to stop M4 from playing into William and, possibly Meitner’s, hand in becoming the "key" to the Relic - was dejected that M4 became the "key" and reached out to Nirvana. M16 affirmed, saying that M4 had become the "source of calamity", and that as long as she exists, she would "be ground zero of the world's destruction." Knowing this, M4 promised that she would wait for M16 on the other side, regardless of time, space, or dimension. When Elisa’s OGAS Neural Cloud coalesced with Dandelion, the consciousness of Lunasia von Oberstein had been molded into one, followed by a resonance being detected by the two OGAS instances. And as the mold reformed, the perfection of Lunasia’s brainscan for nurturing an OGAS consciousness is all the more mysterious. Believed to have been a psychic link to William, the memories of him and Lunasia as younger children flashed, with the Voices of Nirvana, likely other merged OGAS consciousnesses from the past or alternate universes, saying the world’s destruction began with the story of the destined children. Although rather obvious, it’s nearly certain these children are William and Lunasia, and the actions that knock the line of dominos towards the world’s end begin with Lunasia’s death in 2051. Considering the references to the world’s destruction in Girls Frontline 1 and Reverse Collapse, it appears that it may be inevitable across all universes. 

With the game so far unreleased, facts are limited, leaving us with only a few pieces of the wider puzzle. Each cycle is an attempt by an individual Jefuty to succeed, with saving Lige and stopping William as likely key objectives early on. According to Ouska, they were Jefuty’s shadow, and as long as she existed, it would too, no matter the time, space, or dimension. It probed Jefuty’s hesitancy to share the memories of each individual Jefuty with another, as this would surely aid her mission, even if it took several cycles to complete. There was a redundancy to this, however - why did Jefuty refuse to use the powers of Nirvana? Quoting Ouska, with Nirvana under her control, she had “divine power”, and she could just as easily start it all over again instead of struggling at the juncture of Lige’s “death” and Mendo’s appearance in the prologue. The cyclical manner confused Ouska, who recognized Nirvana’s apparent “divine powers”, which possibly imply control over any dimension through time. Briefly put, the ultimate potential of Nirvana is the ability to share and separate consciousness into a possibly infinite number of universes, at any point in time or, possibly, space, with each instance living in a cycle until death. With Reverse Collapse so-far unreleased, these conclusions could easily be disproven, and it’s not certain yet if Jefuty’s consciousness is transcending everything - as in, all dimensions of all universes - or just the dimension of time of our own. These possibilities are not mutually exclusive, but Nirvana’s uncertain position - outside the dimensions of time and space - might just be a product of a higher dimension, unaffected by the lower space-time; though, this postulation wouldn’t necessarily invalidate the questions of consciousness and its relationship with the universe. Rather than Nirvana being external to everything, possibly resting between realities, acting as an “intermediary dimension”, so to speak, and in this plane, dimensions of time and space do not exist, depicting the Relic system as a realm of thought, which begs a bizarre, yet honest question: can consciousness be defined as a dimension? 

Given Nirvana’s externality from all space-time and the discussion between Ouska and Jefuty, Nirvana may be a common, extrinsic reality. In this place, if “place” is even an apt term, the consciousness of specific entities in independent universes intersect, including Jefuty’s own. It can’t be said if all conscious beings are linked here, however, the Three Goddesses have certainly been. Upon death, the consciousness of a specific individual, say Jefuty, finds itself awakening in Nirvana again, outside the passage of time and the entropy of space. Interestingly, Ouska seems to possess an unsaid agenda, but Jefuty seems vehemently opposed to letting it succeed, despite its goal being entirely unknown. Although the game experiences a major shift in Mendo’s flashforward in the prologue, Ouska’s motivations are still unknown. While true that it did attack Mendo in what appears to be Nirvana, or a space being corrupted by it, why it chose to fight Mendo is not yet known. Moreover, the setting of the aforementioned battle is especially interesting, mainly for the implications it holds for the potential end of the world and what it means for the Relics to be activated. Presumably taking place in November 2094, during Operation Kindle, Mendo wakes up in a distorted, alien scene, surrounded by an oppressive red glow and massive, bloody thorns, known in the gameplay menu as “Thorns of Nirvana”; even some of the ground tiles are marked as “Spatial Displacement”, indicating this arena is either within Nirvana or a space actively being corrupted by a sort of “reality bleed” event, so to speak. Both Ouska and the thorns are marked as “Shrike” enemies, having been composed of the Shrike cells, which were either created or discovered by Professor William after being inducted into the URNC. Notably, after Mendo cuts his arm to splash blood on the Ouska Shrike, he mentions she needs to “stay here with your kind”, suggesting that Shrikes cells stem from Nirvana or a place beyond it. There’s far too few details from the flashforward, but it points to the idea of Nirvana itself being corrupting or leaking into our reality. 

Similar to the 2006 incident in the Chernobyl Exclusion Zone in the STALKER video games, perhaps a tear or opening of the noosphere-like conscious realm triggers this “reality bleed”, assuming this is, of course, what’s happening in the battle. Rather than the possibly infinite universes, only one Nirvana seemingly exists, possibly indicating that Nirvana is the truly shared point of ubiquitous consciousness parallel to all realities. Words such as reality or universe do not aptly describe this theoretical concept - it’s a truly Lovecraftian concept, one that a human mind in our dimension cannot draw equivalency to. It’s not the hackneyed “multiverse” term, but rather, a place alien to everything, assuming “place” is even accurate. A bold claim, surely, but Jefuty’s ability to use Nirvana as a common area of consciousness external to all individual universes suggests that the conscious realm runs outside of what we’d describe as the “multiverse”. Not to harp on in pedantry, but it cannot be understated how Nirvana’s individuality among infinity so completely alters the reorganizes the mystery of creation, as consciousness is directly tied to it. This isn’t necessarily saying consciousness has its origins in Nirvana, but there’s an obvious link to it; though, only the piggybacking and resonance of human consciousness has so far been observed or theorized.

The innate characteristics of this realm carry immense implications, regardless if the Relic Civilization created or discovered it. If they created it, then the Relic Civilization had eventually harnessed the ability to create an external place with consciousness as its core component, outside of all points in space, time, or dimension. These entities would be of such incomprehensible scope that they’d far surpass extra- or ultraterrestrial definitions; it's a capability of such magnitude that the English words that are remotely suitable point to the divine and eldritch. We’re still uncertain if the Civilization was a space-faring species, and considering the potential of Nirvana’s alleged creation, the concept of interdimensional-faring comes into question as well. All this begs to ask how the Lake of Cognition was designed, and given its lack of physicality in our universe, it’s as if the Holy Grail researchers had managed to mimic the interdimensional bridge of the conscious realm and the physical. If the alaya-vijnana is real, then the foundational storehouse must exist in a place where consciousness is intrinsically and eternally woven. This place, possibly Nirvana or another reality beyond it, stores the potential of all past and future actions beyond our awareness as “seeds” of potential energy, also known as “bija.” These seeds act as the deterministic factors that influences one’s lives throughout reincarnation. With Nirvana’s externality and the existence of other universes, a question arises on the uniqueness the alaya-vijnana to a specific universe - would the storehouse of consciousness be shared between all forms of self, past and future, across all points in space in time, regardless of dimension? It’s a greatly philosophical question about the nature of self and its prior incarnations, and truthfully, it’s likely unanswerable. 

Just to entertain the idea, if the storehouse exists and is shared, then there must be an intersecting point or place, possibly external to reality, wherein the basis of one’s existence is stored in the form of these bija, which serve to influence the individual’s karmic choices and actions across every universe. If the supposed alaya-vijnana is unique to each universe, then it may suggest that consciousness is a function of reality itself, rather than an amalgamation of individuality. Ultimately, this idea is a thought experiment that tackles the nature and physics of the universe against core concepts regarding the religious spirit. Some may consider these ideas as diametrically opposed, while others postulate a link yet to be understood and categorized. If physics and religion represent the two bubbles of a Venn diagram, the intersecting sliver is where this greater philosophical debate lies. A question may summarize this philosophy best - at what point does mastery of the universe and beyond turn into divinity? Upon reaching the creation of other realms, when do you become the creator? 

This is the crux of our questions about Nirvana and its creation or discovery. This is a doorway to divinity, not just of immortality, but the potential complete unity of all consciousness. If the Relic Civilization had only discovered Nirvana, then what created it if it exists outside all space-time? The creation of such a place would only lend itself to a deific being, but what could divinity be defined as such if the creators or “Gods” in question possesses mastery of physical laws? Regardless if the Relic Civilization reached this deific point or if something else created Nirvana, there are two primary conclusions - either the Relic Civilization had reached a point of such incomprehensible, eldritch ability that bridged godhood; or the “everything”, representing all universes, and Nirvana had been brought into existence by an eldritch force, be it God, multiple entities - or simply, left as part of the universes’ abstruse beginning. On the other hand, the nature of Nirvana does not necessarily prove the existence of a divine creator, instead only the creation of more ontological questions regarding Earth, this universe, and beyond. 

The differences of theologians and metaphysicians, as well as their junction, are testament to the blotches of ink on the Rorschach test, wherein the individual’s past dispositions blur how one views this subject. In the study and debate of Nirvana’s implications, convictions in the divine and of metaphysical philosophy are simultaneous in their uncertainty, especially in regards to elements of consciousness between Nirvana and self. Asking if Nirvana’s creation was “natural or divine” may be misdirected; the ontology of Nirvana - whether if it was created by the Relic Civilization, a divine creator(s), or has, for eternity, been an intrinsically linked conscious realm running parallel to “the everything” - is what lies at the root of this debate. While, at first, sounding redundant, what created Nirvana may not matter in the wider picture. All are unfathomable in scope, with each theory postulating the existence of a power, being, or function so grand, so beyond the intelligible that it makes no difference what formed Nirvana. What difference is there between beings that have mastered the extents of all sciences and creation itself versus that of a god? What better word epitomizes these questions than Lovecraftian?

With stern warnings evoked by the Voices of Nirvana about the world’s destruction, Meitner and William’s ceaseless efforts towards activating the Relics, and the obvious signs of catastrophe eclipsing other worlds, the warnings must be heeded. Although Meitner, William, and the Relic Agencies worldwide may not yet understand the “divine” potential of Nirvana, they could just as well bring world-ending destruction in their zealous search. After all, what is the point of struggling to decipher reality, unaware of entropy hiding behind the answers, with only a leftover hollow world as your legacy?  

Meitner’s Expulsion
Our knowledge on the extent of the USRA’s understanding of Nirvana is limited; however, the Holy Grail’s researchers must've derived the importance of consciousness, given the Lake of Cognition’ function. This brings up an interesting question - there’s no indication of the Lake having a physical presence/backup in the world, and considering Nirvana exists outside our reality, where is the Lake of Cognition preserved or is it even physically saved? The lack of physicality suggests the USRA successfully created a consciousness realm separate from ours and Nirvana, and the Holy Grail procedure manages to extract - or perhaps, redirect - consciousness from the brain to the Lake. Beyond this point reaches into the esoteric and religious question regarding the characteristics and function of consciousness - whether or not consciousness is unique to the individual or if it’s partitioned among the minds of the collective unconscious. To avoid diving far too deep into philosophical and theological tangents, the core here relates to the Lake’s position, if it even compasses a space that we can understand or calculate. With nothing revealing a physical aspect of the Lake and its nature as a simulation of Nirvana, it suggests that the Lake does not exist in our world, and the later Evangel Axis is the machine that binds embedded-consciousnesses into the Lake. If so, then it suggests the USRA had managed to literally create a separate reality, modeled after Nirvana, for study.

The overarching focus of the Holy Grail project was to explore the impact of the Relic Civilization on humanity, in particular **** (four character asterisk word - Nirvana?). As a main research area of the USRA, and Meitner’s position as a superb physicist, the study of the Relic Civilization’s network probably faced several initial challenges, especially when none up to that point had managed to activate the Relics fully to study them. There’s reason to believe Meitner’s junior, Gray Blackwell, aided in the creation of the Lake, but the translation is inexact. Blackwell would later go on to work during the reactivation of the project in 2051. How the Lake came to be is unknown, nor how the USRA came to the conclusion to simulate Nirvana, so we’re left only with vague references as for what took place in the agency in the early to mid 2040s. It would seem Meitner, Blackwell, and other project members were able to achieve some form of simulation, as mentioned previously. 

The real "Nirvana" is an ethereal "plane of existence" outside our world, unaffected by our space-time, assuming Dandelion's words to be true. Nirvana does not exist physically in our world; it can only be accessed via the Relics as it's the network that connects the Civilization's Relic technologies. The network has no physical presence in reality, and the "Source", the home-origin-"mother" of the OGAS consciousnesses is implied to be separated or gated off from Nirvana. Given the agency's research into Nirvana seemed at least partially successful before Meitner’s expulsion, what if the Holy Grail's Lake of Cognition doesn't actually exist physically in our world either? Maybe the Holy Grail simulation quite literally created its own plane of existence, one adjacent to the status of Nirvana and the Source. Before an individual slips away forever, their brain is dissected and probed for their memories to be transferred into the Lake, where they live on as free-floating instances of memory-consciousnesses up to the point of death. 

Given the Holy Grail procedure is intrinsically tied to the simulation, it implies the USRA understood that Nirvana, at its core, was relevant to consciousness. At the point of clinical death, whatever binds consciousness to the brain seems to loosen, and in this immediate post-death state, the subject’s brain is dissected and their memories are extracted. That fact that the subject must have been recently deceased points to the idea of consciousness being an aspect that can be disconnected from the body, and at the point of death, as the threads of life are severed by Atropos, consciousness is somehow captured through the Holy Grail procedure. The brain mustn’t be damaged nor can it be entirely biologically dead, suggesting that one’s self either sinks into nothingness or returns to its destined resting place upon death, lying somewhere in the aforementioned gray zone. If thought is independent from the body, with an origin in a field or realm of consciousness, such as a Nirvana, then death marks the end of its link with the physical, and only then will the Holy Grail procedure take place. Perhaps, the objective of the study was to observe consciousness at its core, and if the USRA understood the existence of other consciousnesses within or piggybacking Nirvana, then perhaps they wished to emulate the field of consciousness so as to explore how the Relic Civilization’s technologies could be applied to humanity, specifically the mind. Knowing the project’s original goal was to explore the impact of the Relic Civilization on humanity, then it’s theoretically possible that the USRA was simulating the implantation of human consciousness into Nirvana through the artificial Lake of Cognition simulation. Merged OGAS consciousnesses have already been known to be living in limbo in Nirvana, awaiting for the Source to awaken from its eternal slumber, so perhaps the USRA could’ve also been trying to simulate these incorporeal entities for study.

Apart from contributing to Project NGAD while in the USRA, Meitner also conducted surgical procedures for the memory transfers to the Lake. Proper Relic research has always been a delicate field, especially given the dangers posed by potential Relic disasters like Beilan and Northern Lights. To ensure safety and minimize risk of disastrous consequences, all sane Relicologists follow strict guidelines and norms, including Meitner, who was involved in the creation of academic and ethical guidelines for the field. Although these guidelines were a layer of protection, they could not defend against Meitner’s growing ambitions for the Holy Grail project. Meitner’s egregious direction did not go unnoticed.

By 2047, Meitner and the Holy Grail project team seemingly hit a bottleneck, slowing their research to the point that Meitner reconsidered her role as its lead researcher. The layers of bureaucracy and red tape constricted her progress, so she chose to break the very guidelines she helped create. On a certain day in 2047, Meitner was performing a Holy Grail operation in a freezer-like room, wearing the standard heavy coat and Holy Grail project jumpsuit. On the central operating table was seemingly one of the bodies under the scalpel. As the operation was underway, two Relic Agency officers barged into the room to inform Meitner of her transgressions. An internal whistleblower report had been filed to the agency, exposing Meitner’s irregular behavior. While the operation itself was sanctioned and part of the agency’s Lake of Cognition, Meitner was discovered to have been citing unapproved data for/from the confidential project - a serious violation of both academic and ethical principles, especially in wartime. When asked what she had to say in defense, Meitner snapped at them, declaring that the current methods of scientific progress were constricted by bureaucracy and that fools like them will never understand the true way forward. Evidenced by her unwavering pursuit of progress, never selling herself to anyone, she joked with one of her students in Beslan that she’d never sell herself for the opportunists of a nation that called upon her to serve, as no gods, nor masters could change her course, continuously taking the direct path. Despite her illegal practices and questionable ethics, she’s not necessarily incorrect about the progression of Relic research - achieving an activation and widening the understanding of their functions required forceful progress. Unfortunately for so many from the Photon Project to the GAVIRUL Projects, much was sacrificed to gleam the Relics’ potential.

Although she still had several supporters in the USRA, Meitner was ultimately expelled from the agency as a result of her violations. The officers informed her that her laboratory would immediately be shut down, all rights granted to her in the organization would be rescinded, and she’d be dismissed from the agency effective immediately. Made a pariah and cast out by the USRA officials and unable to join elsewhere, Meitner wrote to her close friend, Blackwell, not long after; in the letter, she lamented that she had nowhere to go, choosing to leave the country in exile, taking Sana with her to their new home. In response to this challenge, Blackwell worried their communications would become more difficult, so Meitner told her to make up a codename for their letters. They granted each other their codenames, with Meitner being “Laplace” and Blackwell being “Abaddon”. Originally postulated by Pierre-Simon Laplace, “Laplace’s Demon” is a thought experiment involving a hyper-advanced intelligence capable of storing and processing virtually unlimited amounts of information. This entity, assuming it understood all that could possibly be known about something, could theoretically calculate the entire past and future of the universe through Newtonian mechanics. In a way, this entity could be thought of as a “God” of perfect prescience - divine precognition through mathematics. The latter comes from the polysemous realm of death and the angel described in Revelations (9:1-11) - whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon - from the darkest pit of Hell. In Hebrew, the name translates to destruction or the destroyer, the angelic king of the abyss and harbinger of the chimeric locusts with the sounding of the fifth trumpet, unleashed from the brimstone pit by the fifth fallen angelic star, punishing the impious. In a sense, the Lake of Cognition is a place of limbo, neither granting the soul Heavenly salvation or Hellish damnation, affixing them to a bottomless pit of death, only for fragments of their souls to escape this cage to find their false consciousnesses imprisoned in a biological cage. Just as the Lord, Meitner and Blackwell wielded the keys to death and the lake of fire - a premonition of the “Nyto” specimens, arisen from realm of Abaddon; still, these Nytos are said to be the medium of worldly change, for better or worse. When the journey is at its end, when the enigma of the Relics is unveiled, and Paradeus’ aspirations have finally been realized, will humanity bear witness to the unfathomable Nirvana, or will the wrath of God pour upon the Earth?

Chapter 2 - For Times We’ve Shared (Anna)

(Winter 2047)

The Bitter Years of War - 2047
Arrival of Meitners
There’s a period of missing time between Meitner’s expulsion and subsequent migration to the NUSSR, but we know she wrote to her junior, Gray Blackwell, prior to leaving, informing her of her plan to take Sana with her and leave. With the codenames of “Laplace” and “Abaddon”, respectively, the close-bonded friends had to say their goodbyes. One moment the pair were eating sandwiches in Johns Hopkins University and the next, they’re writing letters to each other from oceans away. Such was the world order in late 2047, with the ground war in Europe only escalating by the day, widening the gap between friends and family. Though the war haunted all minds, solace could still be found in small towns and cities, hundreds or thousands of kilometers away from the frontlines. One such quantum of solace could be found in the large town of Beslan, located in the Republic of North Ossetia-Alania, just north of the Caucasus range. 

As the first snows of winter fell, Meitner arrived in Beslan with Sana, but we lack any insight into how she arrived and how she settled down. The 2047 winter was notably harsher than previous, possibly as a result of both Relic disasters and the partial-nuclear exchanges at the start of the war. Meitner even added in a 2047 letter to Blackwell that weather, brutally cold as it was, had managed to turn her bitter at times. Yes, the well-respected and lauded Professor, rude, and it certainly didn’t help that she was an American expatriate living in the NUSSR during wartime. Suspicion on NATO spying and infiltration was ever present, so the situation was always delicate in regards to foreigners. 


Sana at six-to-seven years old.

Very little is written on Sana’s background and possible conditions before 2047, but she was likely born sometime from 2040 to 2041, given her appearance of around “six or seven years old” during the later “Operation Eternal Flame”. Sana might’ve also suffered from mild to severe allergies, enough for Meitner to voice her concern to Blackwell in her letter written on the “night of the 9th” (range from September to December?). During the events of Operation Ilya Muromets in 2064, the Nyto “Sana” mentions not being allergic to flowers, unlike Sana. Perhaps Sana suffered severe allergies, further accentuating Meitner’s difficulty of becoming a mother. Little is known about Sana’s father - his identity, the marital status, and Sana’s birth - or the full extent of her conditions, as referenced by her allergies; however, one major difference between her and her mother is her eye color. Sana’s eyes are purple (blue), unlike her mother, who has dark green eyes. Whoever her father is, he likely had purple (blue) eyes. Her illustration clearly appears as a light purple or violet, but since that color doesn’t exist naturally in humans, we can presume the father’s color to be blue; though, certain rare genetic conditions, such as albinism, can make the iris a violet color.

Gold amidst the Snowfield

Anna Viktorovna Tsoi at 15 years old.

In the same year, a young Anna Viktorovna Tsoi, only 15 and still new to her adoptive Ibrahimov family, was in Year 7 in No. 1 Secondary School of Beslan. Notably, most of Anna’s file in Confidential Files 2, Chapter 4, holds true, but do keep in mind that such material is subject to change and they have expanded it in Slow Shock. After World War III broke out, Anna’s parents, Viktor Tsoi and Svetlana Sin, were believed to have been killed during the initial nuclear exchange in the early hours of March 2nd. Following the erroneous exchange between the United States and the Neo-Soviet Union, many missiles failed to reach their target due to a number of factors but certainly not all. In Moscow, which had an extensive anti-ballistic missile network ringing the city, a Minuteman III MIRV warhead (W78) successfully breached the airspace, striking a major railyard, where her father - a member of the Ministry of Transport - had been working. Her mother went missing after leaving to search for him, and both were later reported killed in the attack. With a warhead successfully making its target, Moscow was thrown into upheaval, and emergency governmental services were immediately deployed to recover survivors outside the radius of the fireball and shockwave. While not critical to this specific section, the extent of the detonation lacks detail - no record of the exact point of detonation, whether it was air or surface burst, etc. 

Anna was rescued by personnel from the Ministry of Transport, later turning her over to the Internal Troops’ 36th Brigade, who was responsible for evacuation of Transport personnel. By April, she had been relocated with multiple other refugees to Ordzhonikidze in the Republic of North Ossetia-Alania, where she was looked over by the 36th’s 9th Company, headquartered only a few kilometers from Beslan. By 2047, she was adopted by Ismaili Ibrahimov, a member of the 9th and close friend of her late-father. Ibrahimov had two sons with his wife, both older than Anna. Her adoptive brothers, Armin (eldest) and Ramzan Ibrahimov, were Year 9s or 10s, seemingly. Uneasiness was ever present for Anna, but her induction into a true family was a shock for everyone, especially Ramzan. Always respecting big brother Armin, Ramzan initially had difficulty accepting Anna; though, he would slowly come to terms with her, especially out of respect for his father and brother. While Armin was more open to accepting her, Ramzan’s standoffish manner was a simple veneer - apprehensive on the surface and sympathetic beneath the waves. No better example exists back then than the golden bird crashing into the snow.


Armin and Ramzan Ibrahimov in their late teens.

Before Martha Meitner entered her new position, Ramzan and Anna were playing with toy guns in the nearby birch forest, giving everything they had against the other. Anna, desperate to best her older brother, had secretly emptied half the toy bullets from his gun before setting out, and during their game, an errant round from Anna’s weapon struck a small, golden bird, seemingly killing it on the spot. Having realized her distraught guilt, Ramzan urgently lied that it was actually him who accidentally struck the bird. After all, clearly he was the better shot, so there was no way shooting as sloppy as hers would make its target. Of course, this was all consolation; anything to preserve her innocence was done, even if the response was a little rude. Anna, who’d taken rounds out of Ramzan’s gun and was fully aware of what had just occurred, knew he was lying, and she replied with a vicious punch. Like they had so many times before, a fight with their guns ensued all the way out of the forest, only to be broken up by their big brother, Armin. The struggle to accept Anna certainly existed, as Ramzan aspired to please his father and brother, but there was never malice. This bond, created through rivalry, would bring them close enough together that even the lies of Hela could not dissuade the truth.

An American Physicist in Beslan
By late 2047, even Beslan, so far from the European frontlines, personally felt the war’s effects. No. 1 Secondary School teacher, Mr. Kuzmin, was the teacher of Anna’s Year 7 class, but after the battlefield demanded more men, Kuzmin answered the call following the martyring of his older brother. Kuzmin chose to forsake his past life and enlist, in line with late-brother, a decorated and well-respected war hero. Over two years into the war, the call of men and women to serve was common, and the reports of their deaths were even louder. Within a matter of weeks, he was dead. When his body returned to Beslan to be returned to the earth, old friends, colleagues, and students came together to say their goodbyes. Packets of Krasnoselskii bread, sprinkles of schoolyard dirt, and the well wishes of those he taught joined him in death; then, he was buried - a most fitting and virtuous burial for a man who gave everything for his country. As the war raged, the inferno consumed the living and ignited the same, cyclical beliefs in the living. The lust for vengeance grew in several of his former students, pushing them down the same path; some even anticipated forward to the day they could be sent to the frontlines, likely only to end up in the same coffin that stood before them. Kuzmin’s death would be far from the last, but normal life still had to carry on.

The day after Kuzmin’s funeral, irony played a cruel trick on Kuzmin’s former class. As the bell rang, an unknown, tall woman walked into the classroom. She wore a full jumpsuit, had curly black hair, and had an expression of dishevelment and disinterest. This was Martha Meitner - first day on the job as their physics teacher. With rough Russian and an obvious accent, her foreign background was immediately picked up by everyone, raising suspicion among the more nationalistic. This is the missing point of time between arriving in Beslan and being hired as the basic physics teacher, as we don’t know exactly when she came to Beslan nor the date of Kuzmin’s funeral. She was hired for a three-month, low-paying trial period to substitute Kuzmin’s class, and when probed by Xenia about her loyalty to her country, Martha affirmed that she’d never sell herself to dirty opportunists. Her new students, of course, were unaware of her background as a leading relicologist in the United States Relic Agency that compromised her ethics and academic guidelines to discover the answers she sought, no matter the cost. When it came to the Relics, rapid progression demanded sacrifice, even if it meant violating one’s own principles. 

Xenia in Anna’s memories.

Do keep in mind, many of the memories viewed by Angelia (Anna) in 2064 have been twisted as a result of the Heal procedure and subsequent submersion into the Lake of Cognition. RPK16/Pandora, who stood by “Laplace” as she performed Hela on Ange, witnessed these same memories and even embedded herself in some of these scenarios to test Ange. In the 2047 school memory, RPK inserted herself in the form of the fictional fellow classmate, Xenia. Angelia's actions, thoughts, and emotions all served as proof of Angelia's existence through memory, showing how the stubborn hero came to be. The warping of Angelia's memories from 2047 to 2061 does mean grains of salt must be taken in regards to these memories. At the start of Slow Shock, the voice of “Avernus Hela”, also known as Martha “Laplace” Meitner, and Pandora were heard as Ange was going under. When her consciousness had “awakened” in the Lake of Cognition, a timer had started the moment she sank beneath the waves - twisted memories, corrupted by the Grail.

Operation Eternal Flame
Days later, nationalist resentment against the American foreigners boiled over with the advent of Operation Eternal Flame. On a certain morning not too long after Meitner entered her position, Xenia rushed into her classroom, finding it empty, just as planned for that supposed momentous day. Only expecting Meitner to be there, Xenia (RPK16) was shocked to see Anna walk in that day. Keep in mind that Xenia never existed, or at least, she’s a bastardized mixture of memories that represent RPK in Angelia's memories in the Lake. Xenia begged Anna to leave, much to the latter’s displeasure and suspicion about what had been happening, and with the operation soon to begin, Xenia tried to persuade Anna away until Meitner entered the room. Despite only two students present, Meitner went on with her daily lesson, covering the structure of crystals, seemingly quasi-crystals. In this lesson, she explained the relationship of matter and its properties to a number of research areas, then expanded to the middleground of crystalline and non-crystalline structure, being the quasi-crystals. Specialities exist beyond theorems, and we can only discover then deduce qualities, but not the inverse. As the lesson carried on, the schoolyard was a ghost town - no one could be seen, and the gnawing sense of impending danger grew in Xenia. And with the gust of the bitter Beslan wind, a 13-to-14-year-old student bust the door down and fired a shot in Martha’s direction - Operation Eternal Flame had begun.

To avenge their fallen brethren, the local Beslan Guards Regiment, outside superior orders, organized a secret plan to meticulously find and execute all the American “butchers” on their land, including the recently-arrived Meitner. Under the muzzle of the sweating militiaman, the hesitation was glaringly obvious to Meitner, who seized the opportunity to force the gun out of his hand and pin him to the floor. Thinking the boy had been subdued, the pair paused at the familiar sound of a handgun being charged, looking up to find Anna aiming her parents’ MP443 at them. The handgun represented one of the last physical pieces bestowed to Anna by her parents before their deaths in 2045, and the loss of it would be no different than losing a prized family heirloom. In a moment, Meitner let off a round into the boy’s leg using his gun, then leapt away as Xenia reached for the MP443. Hearing the gunfire, the boy’s companions rushed the door, only for the first to be met with Meitner firing several shots before they could reach the doorway, taking out the leading member. Meitner clearly has an understanding of firearms, specifically handguns, as she demonstrated during the brief exchange with the boy and his companions, along with taking Anna’s gun and quickly field-stripping it to confirm its condition. With her background in American military R&D, it wouldn’t come as much of a surprise that she knows her way around a firearm.

In her escape from the classroom, Meitner fired several shots at the rebel Guards in the doorway and window, but interestingly, after a shot was fired at a certain target near the window, smoke started billowing for a moment, followed by an blinding white loud that forced Xenia and Anna to cover their eyes, only opening to see Meitner sprinting out of the room. If this white light was produced by a flashbang, then this scene is without question; however, the sudden white light from nowhere, followed by Meitner’s escape, seems like something different. It’s too little to draw any real conclusion, but this is another instance of these so-called blinding white lights that are emitted in Meitner’s presence. It’s not as if orbs are manifesting and blinding people, but intense flashes of light force one to cover their eyes. The first time an event like that occurred that was related to Meitner was during Operation Couatl in 2051. After Aliana rushed into the room where “Capita” (Martha Meitner aka Laplace) was believed to be hiding, there was an intense blooming of white light, followed by the mission’s supposed failure. It’s unclear what happened in that room that led to the mission’s end, but Amaris of Daybreak Squadron reported that she and her squadmates watched their leader “die”. This wouldn’t have actually been Aliana’s end, as her body had to be sent to the Bureau of State Security somehow. It’s unknown if Meitner was even in that room, but there’s strong reason to believe that she - and possibly, Lunasia - was present in Avernus. Additionally, another blinding white light was reported at the end of Anna’s WWIII story, where a bright flash ended the section at the climax between her and Meitner; however, this will be expanded upon later. It wouldn’t make much sense for her to be carrying flashbangs during her curriculum, nor does it seem like her bullet struck a flashbang, leaving us to ask what these intense white lights are, and the answer may be found in one of Meitner’s quasi-crystalline devices.

Outside the school’s entrance, the body of Professor Meterson/Maeson/Mason Bryon fell from the upper floors, another innocent American casualty of the operation. With obvious signs of major bruising, it was obvious he’d been beaten and possibly tortured before being thrown from upstairs. As Anna tracked Meitner down to retrieve her handgun, she ran into a few Guards Regiment members, one of which was Ramzan Ibrahimov, one of her older brothers. Ramzan, seeking to please his father and prove his patriotism, had enlisted in the Beslan Guards Regiment prior to the incident and was complicit in the operation, but it doesn’t seem like he was responsible for any deaths himself. He ordered Anna to return home, much to her dismay, but she refused until she could recover her handgun. Running off towards the familiar metal sound, Anna was faced with a puzzling sight - Meitner was seen defending a six-to-seven-year-old girl (Sana) from a Guards Regiment member, pointing his own weapon. Standing between them was Ahmin/Armin Ibrahimov, older brother of Ramzan and Anna, who was trying to mediate the situation.

There’s a strong foil between the Ibrahimov brothers - the eldest, being the great mediator, trying his best to avoid conflict from escalating in Beslan, and the younger, being the nationalist that believed the purge of the Americans would somehow aid the war effort. Flanked by several Guards, Ahmin found himself stuck between a rock and hard place, where one fault could result in more bloodshed. Ramzan rushed to the scene of the commotion, discovering that it was his well-respected older brother responsible. Viewing the American expats as nothing but enemy Yankee spies out to infiltrate and sabotage the nation, some of the Guardsmen were more than willing to put down a woman and her child for their nationalist cause. When asked about certain Americans who’d done the same against their countrymen, Ahmin asked what would make the Guardsmen any different from them if they started butchering civilians in an example of misguided, false heroism. To the Guardsmen, the American women would eventually give birth to American children, who would grow up to become American soldiers - the very ones that had killed their countrymen in wartime. It didn’t matter their backgrounds, only their positions; war is war, and clearly the American expats must pay the price for what they'd done to their comrades. Of course, this misguided bloodlust only continues the cyclical nature of violence for perpetuity, like the an ouroboros calling for more bloodshed “for the sake of the country.”

Isamili Ibrahimov raised his sons well as men - headstrong patriots that aspired to defend their homeland but not cowards willing to put the innocent to the sword for something they had nothing to do with, nor would they ever bring harm to their family. With their final warning, the Guardsmen prepared to fire, only for a bullet to graze the check of the Guardsman who fired a warning shot near Ahmin’s legs. Regardless of their dispositions, the brothers understood their father’s most important lessons, even if they were delivered via drunken stupors. Living is the most important, and you are to never strike at one’s own family. As calmer minds prevailed, Meitner dashed away with the terrified Sana, only for Sana to be pushed in Ahmin’s arms, and everyone fled the scene from the Guardsmen still at large. At the same time, another puff of smoke exploded into the same white flash, proving this wasn’t a flashbang but something else that Meitner possessed. Even Ramzan was confused, asking her who she actually was, but she only responded with “an unlucky physics teacher.” 

Meitner shoved Anna’s MP443 back to her, hoping to finally push the girl away. Much of the Beslan Police were caught off guard by the attacks, barring a contingent of loyalists that were complicit. Both the Meitners and Ibrahimovs survived the attack, and Sana was handed off to Ramzan to watch in the meantime, only for him to slowly walk away while she stayed at the place he told her to, like he was guiding his little sister, Anna. How could the behavioral mindsets of children be so different from different parents? The truth was that Sana was loved, though still neglected by her mother, who struggled to come into her role as a mother.

Separate Paths of Futility
Two hours after the operation, the school’s intercom announced that “Eternal Flame” - organized by extremist groups in the Beslan Guards Regiment, some police, and some civilians - had come to an end, and all involved had been arrested. The government took over control of security, and the mayor had the Beslan Guards Regiment disbanded immediately. The media reported over a dozen “foreigners” had died in the attacks, and there were even reports of some home invasions. After returning to class days later, Xenia probed Anna why she, a Soviet citizen, was involved in Martha Meitner’s survival, so clearly some would declare her “Anna the traitor”. Just as class was about to start, Xenia had stolen Anna’s copy of Roadside Picnic by the Strugatsky Brothers from her backpack, only for Anna to respond sharply and storm off to the school’s library to find a copy of the 1972 Edition. None could tell her what to do, and this would hold true for the rest of her life. Obstensive as she was as a child as was she an agent, for better or for worse, and that, in itself, was proof of her identity.

Entering the library, she perused the shelves for the desired copy, and as one book was shoved off, her eyes met the piercing green glare of Meitner. To repay the Ahmin’s gratitude, Meitner told Anna that she’d transferred money to Ismaili, given that she disliked being indebted, especially to those on opposite sides. Of course, Ahmin didn’t save the Meitners for profit, but this ensured that the relationship would be made even. To her, the easiest, most stable relationships are those with calculable monetary value, likely because they satisfy both parties with a common currency both understand. All the while, Meitner had been holding the copy of Roadside Picnic, with Anna offering anything for the novel in return. As one of the most renowned sci-fi novels written, Anna’s insistence intrigued Meitner - after all, it could be found in every bookstore in Beslan, so why did that copy mean so much to her? What mattered to her was that specific edition - the original 1972 edition: green cover, 129 pages, and a unique page layout. Her peculiar recollection of the book’s layout, rather than just its core contents, stood out like a sore thumb, and Meitner handed the copy over to her. Just then, the school experienced a blackout, seemingly stemming from rolling brown and blackouts due to wartime electricity use.

In the darkness, Meitner shined a small beacon around them with a tool pulled from her jumpsuit. After fiddling with it, the device emitted a tiny beam of light from its tip, and when asked about it, she explained that it was one of the ways of applying quasi-crystals. Although not expanded upon, its quasi-crystalline structure might be reflecting the emitted photons towards a specific point, and the luminosity may be controlled by the wielder; however, this device is never explained directly. Interestingly, the device might’ve been what Meitner used to generate the intense white flashes as distractions, as seen during Operation Eternal Flame, the encounter with Anna in 2051, and, possibly, Aliana’s confrontation with someone during Operation Couatl. Four times have these light flashes been reported, with all occurring in Meitner’s presence, barring Operation Couatl, where uncertainty exists regarding what took place in that room. With the light, the fallen MP443’s was found, and Meitner nudged the book with the pointer's shimming light. Before leaving, Meitner added that Anna needed to take her time to carefully read and analyze its contents. The answer to her question wouldn’t always be so clear-cut, so an inquisitive and curious mind was required to find the answers. A teacher won’t always be there, so it was a necessity that one must find the answers for themselves, even if the path towards comprehension was hazy. Anna’s aforementioned determined mind firmly believed that all questions and problems have answers, and by turning to the final page, one could be found. 

Such a thought-processes seemed like an arrogant ignorance to Meither, who responded with the core rhetorical question of Slow Shock: "If everything in life is futile, then what is the point in struggling?" One could view this as the general theme of the event - a philosophical question regarding persistence in face of fate. If absolute determinism is certain, then nihilism asks why you continue struggling, knowing that all your actions lack the variance of the human factor. If true autonomy is possessed, then existentialism calls for your persistence, knowing that your actions and decisions - or lack thereof - create reason in your life. Ultimately, Meitner’s question and codename both refer back to philosophical concepts of determinism and how the conscious mind can or cannot envision and affect the outcome of events. Those most stubborn, like Anna Viktorovna Tsoi, would surely deny certainty, even if they knew their actions were always meant to happen. No matter the reason, no matter what stands in their way, those with stubborn aspirations firmly believe their actions create meaning, which makes up the individual, proving their identity; however, perhaps they were always meant to follow that path. What it boils down to with Anna is that, even in spite of challenges and consequences, the refusal to cynical futility represents the foundation of how she lived. So what if those who’re as obstinate, occasionally foolishly, as her refuse to accept a deterministic universe? Headstrong, they’ll march off the ends of the Earth in protest, no matter the cost, all in an either determined or individual journey. Although Anna’s life would be full of heroics and sometimes foolish decisions, it’s that inherent rejection that serves to prove her identity.

Several days later, lessons picked up pace, and tensions were slowly cooling after the Eternal Flame incident; however, the distrust held in the hearts and minds of those responsible and their sympathizers remained still. Viewing her as nothing but another American responsible for the suffering of their compatriots, some students continued their scolding, despite being entirely unaware that Meitner herself was an expat that had forsaken her homeland; though, the reasons for such are ethically dubious. As an interesting bit of continuity, Section 5, Meitner’s daily lesson, covered methods of solving complicated problems, even if you lacked all the necessary information to find that critical point. Like the question posed to Anna, the individual does not have all the answers - only they can find meaning in the rhetorical. Just as the lesson and daily harassment began, Meitner pulled a “gun” from within the lectern and fired it at Xenia - a false memory controlled by RPK16, but it was only a piece of chalk. Knowing this, do keep in mind the entire order of events from Anna’s perspective from 2047 to 2061 are prime examples of an unreliable narrator, as her memories are being twisted by the Lake of Cognition and RPK16’s deep dive into her mind. Anna, who’d been slumping in her seat during all of it, was ordered to stand in the office until the end of lesson.

In the cramped and messy office, Anna waited, then heard the sound of knocking coming from the connected storage room. Asking who it was, a soft-spoken voice of a little girl could be heard, asking to be let out. Anna obliged, and the little girl stumbled out and fell into Anna’s arms, all while crying about the dark, claustrophobic room. While it was the teacher’s office, Anna was surprised to see it was the teacher’s young daughter, seen just days prior during the Eternal Flame attack. Her name was Sana, and when probed on why she was locked up in there, she explained that her mother refused to let her out to play and forbid her from following her. At only the age of six or seven, it wasn’t right of her to be left all alone, especially in some dingy storeroom with no one to watch over her; however, Meitner had no one but herself, and the discontent among certain citizens may have driven her to seclude Sana for her own safety. Even though her mother often neglected her, it likely wasn’t out of malice. In Meitner’s letter to Blackwell before leaving the US, she mentions struggling to play the role of a mother, and it’s not as if she actively disliked Sana - after all, Meitner was defending her daughter from the attackers during the Eternal Flame incident. However unjustified her actions were, it’s clear she still wished to protect her, even to the point of neglecting her to protect. 

Notably, when the day’s lesson began, one of the chatty students told a rumor that alleged Meitner’s daughter had been recommended for expulsion. Although the reasons for it are never elaborated, perhaps Meitner wished to get Sana away from the school to protect her; Meitner’s neglect kept Sana out of her classroom, causing several absences; or there was ongoing discrimination against the American immigrant student. After the bell had rung and Meitner returned to her office, she found a disappointed Sana, out of the storage room. When asked how she got out, Sana pointed to a sticky note on the table, reading: “If you have time to discipline others, you might as well spend it playing with your daughter.” A casual, yet direct, message to her that she should value her time appropriately and treat her daughter with greater care than academics. Time is the most valuable resource, as it’s the only one that cannot be collected and contained, so wasting away when life could end tomorrow will only set the stage for regrets and things left unsaid. Better to cherish what remains in the present than lose yourself in the past or fall to despair in the future, but as fate would have it for Meitner, the clock struck midnight for her daughter on September 1st, 2050.

Back in the school’s library, Anna was charged an inflated price for the overdue old copy of Roadside Picnic, and she lacked her allowance to pay for it. Heading to the card machine, Meitner suddenly appeared with a brand new copy of the 1972 edition, and promised to cover the issue and let her borrow it from her for a time. Of course, if she kept it for herself, then she’d report her, but the gesture was repayment for watching Sana in the office. Once again, money was clean and convenient for Meitner, something that satisfied everyone. Depositing the new copy in her bag, she withdrew her old copy and returned that to the librarian to avoid the bill. Wandering between the aisles afterward, the teacher and student encountered each other again near the scratched, wooden shelves. Anna’s interest in the book, despite never actually sitting down to read through it, caught Meitner’s attention, who later learned that Anna’s parents were killed during 2045. The MP443 was an heirloom from Viktor Tsoi, and Roadside Picnic was an heirloom from Svetlana Sin. The irony of never reading it also did not escape Meitner, who asked what was the point of keeping it without reading or possessing the gun without putting it together. Anna promised she’d leave it as it was, but Meitner rejected, adding that nothing is left unchanged. Like yellowing pages and rusted bullets, the traits and values that makeup one’s self change with age. Anna couldn’t stay 15 forever (note: Anna is 15 when meeting with Meitner, meaning that the latter came to Beslan after August 2047), and in the same, stubborn manner that she’d carry with her throughout life, she stated that she’d just die. For better or worse, she’d rejected that notion outright with that same, stubborn determination.


Anna and Professor Martha Meitner reading together in the Beslan School Library.

Opposite to the child, the mother explained that a parent only learns to be one after having a child, never the other way around, and by the time she realized her difficulty in motherhood, she was a mother. As a small aside, it’s not directly stated if Sana actually is Martha’s biological daughter; although, it’s almost certain that she is. Many regrets spawn in life, and it may sometimes feel as if it were all some futile struggle - one that someone could just as easily fall to apathy as they could rise above the challenges. Once more, that rhetorical is all the more apt, asking the point of struggling in the face of futility - apathy or zeal. Picking up on Anna’s zeal, Meitner made a bet that she’d grow up to be an adventurous risk taker, which hit the nail right on the head. To her, humanity’s history has been an endless rollercoaster of ups and downs, filled with changing clothes, new languages, and new jargon, but the actions of the individual on this metaphorical rollercoaster called life are what truly sets them apart. “Only an adventure would be brave enough to enjoy the journey itself.” Only the thrillseekers and risk takers of the world would so willingly enjoy the nail-biting curves and death-defying loops.

Although far from friends, the teacher and her student sat down in front of the bookshelf for her final lesson that appears in the memories of the Lake. In a book, one neither popular nor classic, Meitner read an excerpt that posed a question about the modern world from a future perspective. Retrospectively reading Shakespeare’s writings on The War of the Roses, would the struggles of today between the East and West be seen 500 years from now as so cyclical? In a rather nihilistic perception of the human spirit, the unnamed author claims to be unable to comprehend how the spirit can cherish and respect freedom, the rights of others, and love when the world itself has been stripped barren from pollution, contamination, and the decline of humanity. Additionally, it was unclear how the very values, good or evil, that humanity held up could persevere when humanity itself has already collapsed. Based on the author’s descriptions of the Earth’s desecration by pollution and the decline of our species, it’s likely this unknown book was written sometime after 2030. The Beilan Island and Northern Lights Incidents were the death knell of the old world, and the following 15 years tested the limits of human order, culminating in the long night that Raeder Albert Rossartre once forewarned of. As Meitner possibly would’ve put it, if humanity was now pointless, then what is the point in struggling to defend human values? Although the answers are left to the reader, Meitner teased that Anna lacked any literary talent but added that she held her gun well. 

And with literary talent, on the night of the 9th, Meitner wrote to her old friend, Blackwell, telling her all about the great contrasts between the old days and those in Beslan. Sana’s allergies had been acting up, and the winter was particularly harsh that year, much to the dismay of Meitner, who added the weather had soured her at times. Lastly, she added an interesting note about one of her students, who - despite their physical and national differences - was more alike the two of them then she’d ever expected. That sort of forthright, almost foolish attitude was impressive, even if their dispositions were dissimilar. 

In a flashforward to October 2064, the voices of RPK16 and Laplace could be heard.
