There’s only a few lines in Slow Shock that point towards this collective unconscious, so any speculation on its purpose would be nothing more than just that. A complete lack of context leaves the door wide open for debate on the USRA’s project goal; though, it’s entirely possible the three-level system was designed in 2051, while just the Lake was of USRA origion. While admittedly theoretical, perhaps what the USRA, Meitner, Blackwell, and Oberstein had all collectively created over the years was a partial-alaya-vijnana, external to our world and, possibly, in line with Nirvana. Notwithstanding the theoretical differences between the Lake and Nirvana, an important aspect of the system that’s not yet understood is how consciousness is extracted from the Holy Grail-Hela subject.

The Surgical Procedure and Potential Memory-Upload Technology
Said to have been created by Gray Blackwell, the Holy Grail-Hela surgical procedure is an invasive brain surgery, directed at the dissection, extraction, and transfer of the patient’s memories into the Lake of Cognition. In Angelia's case, RO635 envisioned the brutal operation in her neural cloud after discovering many used surgical instruments - scalpels, retractors, saws, and drills - laid on an operating table. As the body biologically dies, the conscious begins disassociating from the body, allowing for the capture of memory-fragments in the Holy Grail-Hela procedure. The thought of Angelia's skull being drilled, probed, and dissected, layer by layer, consumed her mind; the ambiguity of the procedure is, perhaps, the most important part to the overall mystery of the system. There’s nothing elaborating how these memory-fragments are extracted from the brain, then implanted into the Lake, but an answer may be found in Oberstein and Meitner’s cooperation agreement. While Oberstein’s role is indistinct, maybe the memories were extracted through a primitive form of the mind-upload technologies employed by Ultimate Life Holdings, 42Lab, and Paradeus. Again, the following is mere theory, and the fact that the USRA were simulating the Lake before 2047 throws a wrench into this whole concept, unless the USRA had already achieved a similar mind-upload technology.


POV of the Commander in UltiLife’s Consciousness Digitization Interface, preparing to enter the Magrasea Backup server on September 23rd, 2063.

The Lake of Cognition seemingly exists outside of our world, with no obvious physical backups, but the USRA and the two friends must’ve uploaded minds into this space somehow - but how? The procedure’s general ambiguity past the point of dissection is the most peculiar, with such a dark zone of information on how consciousness is inserted into the Lake. One possibility could stem from UltiLife’s Consciousness Digitization Interface, or some early similar prototype produced back in 2051. While UL is, seemingly, not the sole enterprise to research mind-uploading, they have the most prominence in the lore for such. Before Project Neural Cloud in 2060, a “Minister” representing UltiLife emailed a Director from Cyber Media, hoping to initiate negotiations for a potential cooperation agreement with UL’s experimental mind-upload technology. Prior, CM recognized the flaws of UL’s projects and had a negative view of the proposition, knowing that UL’s technology hadn’t yet matured, lacking necessary academic and clinical trial data; therefore, CM’s hesitancy wasn’t without basis. Moreover, while CM HQ was grateful for the relevant data provided by the Minister, they refused, saying that clinical trials wouldn’t take place until the technology’s flaws were addressed. In a follow-up email, the Minister forwarded the relevant research paper and materials to CM’s technical department but added that UL R&D struggled to realize the human-consciousness upload experiment; despite this setback, the Minister had spoken to UL’s superiors, they were willing to cover 70% of the potential cooperation plan’s funding. Nevertheless, the CM Director refused again, but they did thank the Minister for their support of UltiLife’s research projects. With CM’s rejection, UL needed a major corporate partner, and their saving grace came in the form of 42Lab and its Project Neural Cloud.


Logo of Ultimate Life Holdings.

As a relatively new company of ten years, UltiLife has a history of collaboration and research agreements with a number of prestigious institutes and companies - including 42Lab, which has granted them opportunities for AI, “digital genetic” technologies, and most prominently, Project Neural Cloud in 2060. From what little we understand, the UL human-consciousness upload cooperation plan was outlined in the “Project UltiLife: Mind-Uploading Clinical Trial Agreement”, found in Neural Cloud’s opening animated cutscene. While appearing for only moments, there’s a few stand-out snippets. The project was: funded by UL, but the subject’s name is redacted from the record; and its investigator was Dr. Tessier Winter, presumably one of UL’s principal researchers. Nothing is known about this person, apart from this fact; though, if there’s anyone who holds the answers to what’s truly happening beyond this project’s veil, it’s them. Interestingly, “Tessier” is a derivative of the Old French “tissier” - literally meaning, “to weave”, as in a weaver or one who weaves. Weaving is intrinsic to the stories of the Greek Moirai - Clotho, Lachesis, and Atropos - who weave the fates of humanity from life until death. This is probably an over-analysis of the name, admittedly, but MICA’s naming schemes are often deliberate, such as Professor Samantha Shaw’s Wolf Pack.

In the lead-up to PNC, UL agreed to collaborate with 42Lab for what is evidently a simultaneous test of PNC and UL’s mind-upload technology. Known as the Consciousness Digitization Interface, this machine is used to digitize and upload consciousness into Magrasea - 42Lab’s super cloud server, first activated in 2057. When a human subject is connected, their mind is converted into Neural data, similar to the Dolls of PNC. Notably, the Holy Grail procedure captures memory fragments from one’s dying body, as the mind disassociates from the physical body, and these fragments could be structured similarly to Neural data, similar to the CDI’s function. The story hasn’t yet expanded upon the original UL project, nor their likely collaboration with 42Lab, but the CDI is most likely the result or a prototype of the mind-uploading technology. Before the Commander on September 23rd, 2063, the only other human to digitally access Magrasea was PNC’s chief researcher, Professor Irida, in 2060. The circumstances of her own upload, medical emergency, and subsequent disappearance have been subject to significant scrutiny, given a forcible human upload may have been part of the trial; however, all of this is only tangential to UL and the “Minister”. Having existed for around ten-odd years, the company’s origins are shrouded in uncertainty, yet sparing information on UL’s age, their Minister representative, and the nature of their project possibly hints at the UL representative being Minister Rudolf von Oberstein.

Divergent Magrasean Minds
Related to the CDI, the theory of consciousness duplication is a hot topic among the community, more specifically, whether or not the mind’s rationality and self-awareness is omnipresent. In layman’s terms, when a mind is perfectly duplicated, is that copy its own independent mind or will the two souls be entangled on a metaphysical level? From what’s shown in Girls Frontline so far, the former has proven right in the case of Doll backups and the Nytos; however, there’s precedence for the latter, given the Commander’s background in Neural Cloud’s Clukay character event. Before the official start of the current Magrasea investigation, the Commander and 416 were uploaded together in a testbed, who found themselves in a Magrasea unlike the one we’re accustomed to in the main Neural Cloud story. During the initial investigation, the Commander and 416’s consciousnesses must’ve been separate from their bodies; though, this seems to have not formed two separate conscious entities between them, indicating their minds had genuinely shifted to a different space, being Magrasea. 

Those familiar with the video game SOMA would certainly recall the dishonest “coin toss” analogy, wherein it’s explained that, during consciousness upload and duplication, there will be a “coin toss” that decides the mind’s “host”. So as not to spoil the game too much, nor depart too far from the subject, think of mind duplication in terms of two potentials: the coin toss, a scenario in which the conscious mind will transfer to a new host through chance; and the independent minds, another scenario in which a duplicated consciousness will become two independent entities, with the duplicated instance using the original as a deterministic seed of future actions, unless this instance becomes tampered in some way. All of this is to say: play SOMA, it’s an unforgettable 7-to-10-hour psychological-horror and philosophical journey that’ll leave you asking more questions, rather than true scares, and provides an intriguing and, admittedly, haunting perspective on this subject. It’s almost impossible to say which is correct, as we’ve apparently seen both occur in multiple instances - human, Doll, or Nyto; though, the circumstances of the Dolls of Project Neural Cloud and the Commander may offer some leads.

The Dolls of PNC that also appear in Girls Frontline are our Dolls. They may be of a mass-produced series, but only they partook in the project in mid to late 2060. When these Dolls entered the server, they were uploaded to 42Lab's Neural Cloud Sector, a sector specially designed to host and carry out the functions of PNC. Sometime before, during, or after the Wipeoff Incident, the Magrasea Server was backed up to an external backup server, which ran independently for over three years without human intervention. This disconnection was likely intentional, possibly related to an experiment conducted by Professor Irida of 42Lab, but that's just theory tangentially related to this explanation. When the Magrasea Backup was created, all information (and consciousness) saved at the moment was copied into the backup, serving as the setting for the Neural Cloud game, set in September 2063. The "actual" Dolls of PNC - as in, the Dolls uploaded from reality to Magrasea - were seemingly released after Project Neural Cloud was announced to be a success in late 2060; although, their backups were still "living" in the backup server. Simply put, there are two versions of these Dolls - one in real life, some of which are now in G&K; and one in the backup server, having been abandoned from humanity for what has equated to eons. 

This is what leads to the ultimate question about Neural Cloud’s conclusion and the Exiles’ odyssey: who is the "real" among them? It's very much a SOMA-esque question, wherein the copied consciousnesses - having co-existed for years, albeit, in their Neural Cocoons after the Wipeoff Incident - have fair, equal arguments for being the "real" self, but there remains but a single self in reality. So, does that invalidate the life and experience of the one in the backup? It's up to you to decide, but the ending of Neural Cloud, assuming we are indeed successful in saving the Exiles, holds worrying potential about the friends we’ve made in the server and in reality. When the day comes, what happens to the backup server’s minds? Project Neural Cloud was already completed three years earlier, with all the original Dolls, seemingly, having been released, but what happens when their ghosts, who may not even be the same individuals anymore, manifest from a time-lost grave? After the Commander and 416 exited the testbed for the true investigation, the log-out triggered temporary memory-loss, however, they would slowly return over time, as shown in Clukay’s character event, where the Commander describes to Willow, with some possible exaggeration, the journey with 416. All of this points to the Commander’s mind shifting to Magrasea when uploaded, which may align with Professor Irida’s coma and unusual brainwave activity recorded on September 30th, 2063, following an emergency surgery in an UltiLife Medical Facility. There was no divergence of minds that we know of, only the consciousness being uploaded as Neural data, then transferred back, only for the memories of their experiences in Magrasea to slowly return to them. But what’ll happen when the Exiles find the avenue of escape? Will their minds inexplicably coalesce with themselves in reality, or will there be permanent divergent consciousnesses? Currently, it’s an unsolvable question, one tangentially related to questions about the function of individual consciousness when copied.

Only two humans have ever glimpsed Magrasea through the CDI, the Commander and Professor Irida. It’s believed Irida still remains in a coma, her mind still stuck in Magrasea, as evidenced by the unusual brainwave activity recorded by UL staff after her surgery, unless she’s already passed since 2060. The Commander’s memories gradually returned upon exiting the server, but Irida’s fate is much more dubious. We don’t know when Irida uploaded herself, assuming it was voluntary on her part, so it cannot be said if it occurred before or after backup disconnection, suggesting the possibility of Irida’s consciousness being duplicated from the original server to the backup, like the Dolls of PNC. On the other hand, Magrasea’s disconnection was almost certainly planned as an isolated testbed, likely for Irida’s research into 3rd generation neural clouds; however, this isn’t directly tied to the study of human consciousness, but part of her experiment did involve a 3~ year waiting period, generations in Magrasea, for the mental models of Black Box Evolution Theory to take shape. Assuming the alaya-vijnana is a tangible concept with basis in Nirvana or another realm, then would a divergent mind, split into multiple entities, share the same foundation? Do the seeds of an imitation carry over, or does a new space open for the new instance? When Irida was uploaded, it’s as if her mind had been locked, trapping her in a virtual prison, unless that was the plan all along to guide her evolution theory, which does, somewhat, seem to be the case, given Entropy’s evolution. The CDI enabled the Commander’s entire mind to be quantized and uploaded, then reformed and implanted back into their body upon exit, no independent conscious or rogue intelligence to speak of.

Unlike the Lake of Cognition, the minds processed by the CDI seem to shift consciousness, rather than copy it, to its desired destination. When Blackwell was testing the Lake in early 2051, she copied her memories and embedded them as a test, thus creating the Gray Blackwell of the Lake that Angelia met in 2064; however, there was one core difference: Blackwell’s mind didn’t shift, it was individually copied and transplanted. This throws a wrench into the CDI theory, but there are several caveats, as we lack significant information on how consciousness is uploaded to Magrasea versus the Lake. First, there’s nothing stating the CDI in 2063 was incapable of scanning the host, copying the memories as Neural data, then storing them in a database, while the host maintains self-awareness in their organic body; it’s just that there’s only a two-person precedent set, both having consciously shifted into Magrasea. Second, there’s still nothing definitive on how Meitner and Blackwell successfully captured memory fragments, hence the entire theory of a precursor to the CDI, and with such a lack of descriptions on this 2051 technology, most theories are built upon unsteady ground. Simply put, the CDI is the best lead we have, but its demonstration with the Commander and Irida conflict with how Blackwell’s copy was embedded in the Lake. Then again, the Lake and Magrasea are drastically different environments, so the rules of one may not dictate the other. It’s a bland, generalized statement, but we genuinely need to wait for more information from either game.

Furthermore, in Zangyin’s event in Neural Cloud, she mentions rumors of a mind-copy technology, with few having ever made use of it, likely stemming from cultural and religious traditions that fear and revere death. The reach of mind-upload technologies in the academic and scientific spheres is unknown, but Zangyin’s acknowledgement points to its gradual inception, prominently enough that a folklorist Doll to learn of it. Then again, Zangyin and the other Dolls of Project Neural Cloud were uploaded via the CDI, so it’s feasible that’s where she learned of it, with Irida’s upload possibly tangentially related. As a folklorist, traditions and beliefs about death are plentiful, and the introduction of a technology that essentially enables the human consciousness or “soul” to be transferred, allowing it to live forever, external to the mortal body, no doubt raises ethical and cultural questions. Life and death is the natural cycle of all things, spawning questions since time immemorial, but only with the Lake and CDI does humanity have the means to transgress death, bypassing the understood principles held by so many in both spheres of thought. Perhaps the introduction of UL’s CDI, or an earlier prototype, was the public’s first insight into this field of immortality. The respect for death is strong, and many would view it as a violation of the natural order, a dangerous and unethical potential, or an insult to God, even in the 2060s.

Oberstein’s Colleagues
Acknowledging UL’s potential connection to those responsible, yes, it’s feasible that it’s someone else; though, the subject matter and UL’s existing life span align with Oberstein’s background, so the idea can’t necessarily be discarded outright. What may discount this theory is the mere existence of the Lake during the Holy Grail, wherein the USRA must’ve realized a method or technology to capture consciousness, then affix it to the waves. This isn’t to say Blackwell and Meitner couldn’t have employed a precursor UL technology - backed by Oberstein, who entered a prominent position near or after the end of WWIII, possibly the Minister of Science and Technology and UL’s representative - to aid them in Sana’s resurrection. Lastly, none of this provides an answer to who Oberstein was working with when he poached Meitner, and the only known suspects are: 90wish, namely a group of researchers loyal to Oberstein and deeply intrigued with Relic technology; remnants of the UNRA, most of whom either refused, rejected, or were denied entry to Antarctica; the unknown tertiary Relic Department related to the development of secondary Relic weapon technology in 2050; Paradeus, if it already existed, which may be related to a compartmentalized 90wish faction; or an entirely independent group yet to be fully revealed. If we wish to reach into true esotericism, maybe the former anti-Relic terror group, Pandora, wasn’t fully dismantled in the 1990s - something incredibly speculative and, most likely, not the case. After Lunasia’s death in 2051, “William” vowed to deliver vengeance to an unstated group murderous madmen, and it’s later revealed that Oberstein sacrificed her for a “necessary” cause, adding that, “*** (Lunasia), someday you will understand my meaning.” Although we’re yet to learn of Lunasia’s fate after being abducted from the manor, it’s evident that a group of researchers - namely, Oberstein, Meitner, and other, unknown individuals - were linked to her death.

The rejection of fate only served to irreversibly change its course for the next 40 years. In the beginning, the procedure was conducted on Sana’s brain, which hadn’t yet entered total, biological death, likely thanks to Meitner’s freezer box. Although Sana was a victim of countless many in Beslan, she would be the first sacrifice to what later would become Paradeus’ Lake of Cognition, the bottom layer of consciousness and origin of instincts for all Nytos. Sana’s soul was successfully transferred, but the results were insufficient. Reiterating, it’s unclear if these layers of Nyto Consciousness were created by the USRA or Gray and Meitner, so we can’t say for certain who was responsible for certain functions of the system. Due to Meitner’s rather unsuccessful research venture, a roadblock came in the form of memory-fragment locomotion between layers, preventing any chance of Sana’s memories being contained to simulate her. The fragments traveled to and from the Lake, unable to be controlled, so Blackwell came up with a revolutionary idea: the creation of a device that confined consciousness in desired layers, preventing the leakage of memories from the Lake to the rest of the mind.

Four Days in the Grave
Developed by Blackwell, the Evangel Axis is a unique device meant to “immobilize” consciousness in the system. When activated, it consumes a significant amount of energy to generate an “ice sheet” between the Lake of Cognition and one’s Virtual Cognition Image, and as more memory fragments are implanted into the Lake, the Gospel’s “ice sheet” expands over the Lake’s surface. By now, this ice sheet has grown into a full iceberg, preventing all memory travel between layers. From within the Lake, the soon-to-be-twisted consciousnesses may glimpse a shimmering rainbow refracted through the ice, explained as the optical phase interference phenomenon - a beautiful, eternal prison for the imprisoned consciousnesses. There is one major caveat to this design, however - the Evangel Axis’ energy consumption cannot be satiated through simple means. Blackwell used the example of plant growth lights to explain its consumption, mentioning that, like how growth lights simulate the Sun for photosynthesis but require electrical energy in the process, the Evangel Axis must consume bioenergy/biofuel as a side effect of the Holy Grail’s simulation of “Nirvana”. Although an incomplete understanding, Paradeus’ kidnapping and Nyto experiments were directed towards a false immortality - an intention to sacrifice individuals to the Lake and the Holy Grail, wherein the remnants of their minds are molded into an amalgamated artificial consciousness.

The reasoning behind the necessity of bioenergy remains indeterminate, as there’s nothing yet showing why this must be done, leaving us rather little to go on. Nevertheless, there was still promise in the design. It’s not as if electricity was unavailable in Berlin or Avernus, so what makes bioenergy unique? Perhaps there’s something on a biological or conscious level that fulfills this quota, something adjacent to the true origin of self. The Evangel Axis, the Lake, and Nirvana all share a common factor: consciousness, and more specifically, its interactions with humanity. If there is a legitimate link between the human mind and Nirvana, similar to the noosphere concept, then perhaps what enables consciousness to potentially resonate with the other side, rather it be an internal biological process or an imperceptible sense, is harvested from recently-deceased bodies, manifesting as the bioenergy. According to Persica’s hypothesis on Machlian and Morridow’s compatibility, their bodies, although not entirely human, still biologically function the same. Information is communicated through the body in two ways: chemical reactions and potential differences, however, both involve the “generation of various chemical elements or electrical charges within a cell.” When identical twins stand side-by-side, a temporary resonance is feasibly opened, increasing sensitivity to each other’s biological information transmissions - simply put, a telepathic connection between individuals of the exact same genetics. In response, the Commander asked if the memory fragments in Machlian’s VCI originated from Morridow’s electromagnetic field, which allowed the consciousness information transfer between the twins, theoretically. Additionally, a “sensory induction” phenomenon had been observed between the Isomers of Tallinn that allowed them to share their senses, regardless of physical distance. Persicaria added that this phenomenon was incapable of stably transferring large HD data packets; however, it was, theoretically, enough to enable portions of memories to be transmitted.

If bioenergy is a must for the Gospel’s operation, then perhaps it’s the bioelectricity in cells that is most relevant. When twins are in immediate proximity, heightened sensitivities allow their electromagnetic fields, generated by their biological functions, to potentially resonate, interfering or reproducing similar effects in each other’s bodies. Additionally, while entirely Persica’s hypothesis, she suggests that Morridow’s memories could’ve telepathically transferred to Machlian’s VCI through this electromagnetic field resonance, possibly indicating that memory fragments are, in some aspect, linked to the conscious. Of course, brains possess a measurable voltage, but if bioenergy is paramount to the Gospel, then it begs to ask if these naturally-generated EM fields from transmissions are related. Sure, it doesn’t necessarily explain the Gospel’s input requirement, but there’s nothing else in the story that unites biology, electricity, and consciousness so neatly. However, this could all be simply discarded with additional information, and nothing yet has directly linked the Gospel to Persica’s theory, apart from the aforementioned subjects’ conjunction.


Machlian’s vision of the Baptism of Berlin through the Cocoon Plan.

Not to tread too far from the subject, but interestingly, Machlian also seemed to possess memories of events yet to occur, along with fragments of Morridow’s own memories, one of which was even from Morridow’s perspective in the future. In an implanted, false memory - or perhaps, a vision of an alternative universe or time, the Cocoon Plan was successfully carried out in Berlin, with Morridow, Gray, and Narciss watching the chaos unfold in the prison and the quarantine wall. None of this transpired in our timeline, and Machlian does mention the Commander was an outside factor in all of them, never appearing in any vision except for our own. If we are to believe these future visions are real, then maybe the transmission of memory fragments is not exclusive to just an individual consciousness in an individual universe, unless one’s alaya-vijnana is shared across spacetime, outside the bounds of our perceived dimensions. A similar - albeit, less consequential - event occurred with the Commander, wherein they witnessed a vision of the S09 Base being attacked by Carter’s men before learning of the attack from Khaybar as it was happening.

When Blackwell successfully fixed consciousness in place in the Lake, she began simulating Sana’s consciousness. In the Lake system, consciousness can be simulated using the memories of those who underwent the Holy Grail procedure, and through the Evangel Axis’ application, it isolated the memory fragments from Sana’s Virtual Cognition Image. Back then, Blackwell was only ever willing to harvest the bioenergy of animals to sustain the Gospel, but Sana’s body could only nod and shake her head. Blackwell synthesized Sana’s consciousness but was ultimately unsuccessful, as the consciousness generated was always incomplete, so she attempted many more times, none of which achieved the desired results. Over time, the Gospel’s “ice sheet” gradually thickened, where it now stands as a true “iceberg”, preventing any and all potential memories from escaping into the VCIs of those controlled by it. No matter how many times she synthesized or mixed up the order, the desired result never came. In her words, “what was generated… was not Sana.” This mixture of memories in a puppet body likely would’ve never become the Sana they knew, for this is the unfortunate revelation of the Lake and Gospel system. Although initially successful in fixing Sana’s consciousness to the VCI, “Sana” could do nothing more than shift her head somewhat, effectively nothing more than a zombie.

In a follow-up, Blackwell wrote to Meitner, explaining the project’s failure and the immense energy demands of the Holy Grail, which exceeded the laboratory’s capacity, restricting the Gospel in the process. For the latter, more power was needed, no matter the cost. During Blackwell’s explanation to Ange in the Lake, she mentioned that human uniqueness and creativity were impossible to replicate; the personalities synthesized from the Lake were mockeries - simple selections and recombinations of memory fragments, fused into a bastardized mind. Humans were incapable of simulating God, and like a machine generating countless words through recombinations, they could never create the 27th letter. During the original Holy Grail, the project members set out to study Nirvana through an artificial simulation, unable to ever match its anomalous intrigue. Whatever, wherever, or whoever birthed the universe and consciousness remain above. By simulating Nirvana, they had unknowingly created a mockery, wherein the traits of consciousness are nothing but a million bubbles of one’s life. The creation of consciousness in reality, regardless of origin, is incompatible with the stolen souls in the Lake, as Lake-synthesized minds are molded into a desired form, but never one of new memories. In a way, the Lake-Evangel System could be seen as an allegory for a program or machine that’ll never equate to human creativity, as the mind is the birthplace of unique thought - nothing can be created from the Lake, only generated through selection and recombination of implanted memory fragments. Viewing it from a religious perspective, the Lake could be viewed as mankind’s rejection of fate and aspiration of God’s capacity - an omnipotence that crude imitation was incapable of. From the creative vision, one may view it as an allegory for human creativity versus the abilities of machines - a great source of debate, especially in recent times.

Despite all its glory, the immortality the Lake of Cognition posed was nothing more than an artificial dream built upon foundations of grief, nihilism, and bloodshed. Through a failed endeavor towards a false-immortality, Blackwell had inadvertently set the course for manufactured divinity, wherein the true self was lost in the churning deep of the Lake. In a twisted sense, the Lake and Gospel are a two-part system that could’ve been the answer to immortality; however, none of Blackwell’s experiments achieved this goal. Nothing new is created, only the collapse and reassembly of consciousness, dooming the lost soul to an eternity of isolation, division, and recombination. As long as the human consciousness lives on in the Lake, the body does not matter, but she did elaborate, saying it wouldn’t be true immortality, given that Lake consciousnesses wouldn’t know what the real human self thinks; they’re programmed drones, constricted by the Lake’s innate inability to simulate individuality and imagination. There are only pre-existing inputs, leaving everything birthed of the mind to fade away into the countless rising bubbles. The temptation of the technology, however, would surely enthrall science and theology alike, as even Blackwell herself chose to scan her consciousness and implant that snapshot into the Lake in 2051 after the Evangel’s activation. The last “real” thing the Blackwell of the Lake remembers was delivering Martha the honest truth of the experiment: humans cannot emulate the Creator, as the cost of human artifice to realize this deluded fantasy risked eroding their humanity; apparently thereafter, her snapshot was implanted in the Lake, though it’s unclear how this was achieved, nor is it necessarily sensical for Blackwell to exploit the Lake-Evangel System right after renouncing it.

Laplace’s Demon

Professor Martha “Laplace’s Demon” Meitner, aka Hela, in 2051.

Although the lab lacked sufficient bioenergy input, potential remained. To Meitner and whoever else was working with them, perhaps the increase of input was a necessary prerequisite to realize their goal. Despite their best efforts back then, they had failed, but Martha refused to accept this end. After all, if life is nothing but a futile journey that ends in death, then what’s the point of struggling? The timeframe isn’t certain, but it’s known Martha went to extreme ends, violating all ethical and moral principles, to carry on the project. The harvesting of bioenergy from animals could not suffice, so she crossed all lines of morality, turning to harvesting human bioenergy. The specifics are not stated, but Gray declared Martha a demonic servant of the Devil for the crimes she committed, sacrificing her own students to satiate the Evangel Axis. Gray - who looked up to her senior classmate dearly, seeing her as a shining, brilliant mind - recognized her for who she had become. Martha's drive to save her daughter, someone who she may have never truly loved, corrupted her soul into something unrecognizable to her junior. Gray immediately cut all ties with her, the project, and the Evangel Axis. By opening Pandora’s Box, Gray had unknowingly played her role in a chain of events that may bring the world’s destruction. Truthfully, you could mark any single point along the timeline as the beginning of these events, but a true watershed moment is the relationship between Martha Meitner and Gray Blackwell. When Sana died, what was left of Martha’s humanity died with her. Had Sana not been killed in the attack, Martha’s interest in reactivating the Holy Grail may’ve been avoided, stopping her from coming to Berlin to meet with Gray to discuss and plan out the new project. Gray would’ve never recommended Oberstein as their collaborator, meaning the “sacrifice” of Lunasia and the development of the Evangel Axis system wouldn’t happen. And from there, all of history would be altered all the way to Reverse Collapse, where Jefuty, Noel, and Lunasia may have never been born in the first place for the Three Goddesses Project. Even the Commander likely would’ve never been standout as they are, as all the events which led to the Butterfly Incident no longer occurred.

Gray Blackwell was a doctor of ethics, someone who staunchly opposes the violations of morality, of the Hippocratic Oath. In her final letter to Martha in 2051, she exclaimed that her senior’s actions and objectives were nothing more than an ideal built upon a foundation of slaughter. In 2051, Gray viewed their experiment as an unrealistic fantasy, but when Ange met Lake Gray, the success was revealed. In the Lake, Ange told Gray a comforting lie about the latter’s fate, saying that she died long before 2064, and her students held a wonderful funeral in her honor. In opposition to Martha’s lesson from Roadside Picnic, Gray’s favorite motto was about the inevitability of death and the inevitability of life. While Martha may rhetorically ask what is the purpose of human struggles, Gray accepts life and death for what they are, and this natural order shouldn’t be violated by those of greedy eyes and desperate minds. The subject of the Holy Grail project is something all of science would view as a momentous miracle of Relicology, immortality in its closest viable form. This feat would be both a miracle and a deadly temptation, as the power of the Holy Grail would become a subject of desire to all. Even so, the project’s success still emboldened her, knowing that her theory was ultimately correct, even if she was not the one to prove it. However, her morality and ethics did not sway her from personal ideals; the results of the Holy Grail are inherently unethical and only bring disorder to the natural world. Her guilt was stronger than her curiosity - not something that can be said by many researchers in the Girls Frontline universe. The Evangel Axis had taken so many who underwent the procedure through its internal circulation system, all of which Gray was forced to watch. Having been betrayed by the woman she respected most; her project becoming nothing more than a cycle of slaughter; and most of all, watching the final deaths of countless souls in the Lake drove her to help Ange. 

In 2051, after Gray walked away from the project, Martha and Rudolf seemed to strengthen their cooperation, where the former Holy Grail project was renamed to the “Hel/Hela Project”. Under the pseudonym of the same name, Hela was the lead researcher of the Hela Project, acting under the codename “Laplace”, which she had used in writings with Gray. As the war was reaching its zenith, Laplace continued gathering and harvesting bioenergy for the Gospel, with Oberstein seemingly supporting her work. On that deplorable day in Neu-Tempelhof, a black limousine arrived at the gates of the Oberstein manor’s garden. The serene scene would’ve been otherwise beautiful if not for the events taking place that day. The vehicle stopped, then Oberstein and a bodyguard stepped out. The bodyguard was sent into the mansion, and moments later, Lunasia was dragged out, wearing a serious and resentful expression when looking at her father. Obestein said little but promised this was all a necessary sacrifice; obviously, Lunasia - or alternatively, William and Nemhran - sharply rejected it, declaring that he was nothing but selfish and self-serving, tormenting his daughter for his own benefit. In his last words, he explained that she’d one day come to understand his pain and reasons, possibly alluding to Lunasia’s future as the destined child whose soul was splintered into so many pieces. Upon a wave of his hand, the bodyguard pushed her into the car, and Lunasia begged her father, even using his first name, that he shouldn’t carry through with it. Why she was taken and what happened to her remains unanswered, but it seems Lunasia was a victim of the Hela Project under Meitner and Oberstein. In scattered notes, a picture of a girl who appeared remarkably similar to Nemhran was found, but due to the image being partially burnt, her features couldn’t be made out. 

Typhonic Revelation - Spring 2051 
In the months following Blackwell’s denouncement of Meitner as a servant an evil, having allegedly sacrificed a student to the Lake or the Evangel, Meitner had been fully integrated into Paradeus as the lead researcher of the now-called “Hela Project”, referring to the eponymous Norse realm and Goddess of Death, from which Meitner had taken up her new name - “Hela”, codenamed Laplace’s Demon.


CG of C.M. Kirov Command Academy?

After Anna graduated from the No. 2 Secondary School of Beslan the same year, she entered the C.M. Kirov Command Academy, a Minister of the Interior-ran officer academy in Ordzhonikidze, training to become an officer. The incident in Beslan left great scars on all, and through her connection to Zelinsky, along with Ramzan’s similar pursuit of an officer’s career after the Beslan Guards Regiment had been dismantled, Anna entered the academy in the last year of the war. In winter of 2047, many of her fellow, more disillusioned classmates were desperate for a chance to enlist, unaware of the harsh realities and trepidations beyond their rose-colored lenses. The Ibrahimovs’ graduations occur offscreen, leaving the life paths of the siblings to the imagination, but Ramzan entered the service, followed thereafter by Anna in 2051, who encountered her older brother in the courtyard of the Command College. Ramzan, desperately trying to preserve her life after losing their brother several months earlier, strictly prohibited Anna from enlisting, but upon their chance encounter, he erupted at the chick who long since left the nest, asking why she’d so willingly jump into the abyss like him. Echoing life-long tenacity, Anna simply told him he has “no right to interfere with my life”, promptly saluting and leaving his presence in moments. Much like their older brother who kept the rambunctious trio together, Ramzan sighed, eventually realizing Anna’s choice was not for him to decide, yet he must stand by her side, supporting family like Armin always had. Sometime later, Anna strolled down the fourth floor corridor, where various portraits of renowned figures in the NUSSR were hung, including Meitner’s, commemorating her “ international fame for her groundbreaking achievements in Relic technology research.” As the chief researcher of the Holy Grail Project, and an instrumental figurehead of academic ethical standards on Relic research, it’s still peculiar why her portrait was mounted in a Soviet Command College; however, from Meitner’s letters to Blackwell after Sana’s death, she must’ve made her way to Moscow, probably seeking job opportunities in the capital, immediately contributing to the Soviet Relic Department. 



Hearing the ramblings in the hall, Anna turned to find two cadets defacing Meitner’s portraits, gleefully denouncing her nationality in the process, with Anna taking obvious offense. She rushed one of them, delivering a jab squarely in the face, initiating a two-one-one brawl, only to be broken up by the statute-esque form of Instructor Ramzan, scaring the other two off. Before Anna strode off, Ramzan shouted her name, ordering her to remove Meitner’s portrait. Responding to Anna’s rhetorical on the cowardice of defacing portraits, far away from the front lines, Ramzan - hesitant of the former American teacher and Anna deploying to war - wished for Anna to prove her worth in uniform, because if she couldn’t even “know which side they’re on”, she wasn’t worthy of the cadet armband. In an overboard scathe, Anna’s statement about him not wanting her on the battlefield was lambasted, asking why it was Armin, not her, who perished in Beslan, likely initiating an offscreen brawl or vows of silence for a time between them.

Anna’s Deployment & The Dead Sea
By the seventh year of war, desperation set in on its belligerents, with protracted campaigns only resolved with technological breakthroughs or an eventual peace agreement. Resource and arms loss meant weapons and technical equipment were reserved exclusively for specialized echelons of the militaries, with much of Anna’s platoon using decades-outdated communications equipment, while Captain Ramzan’s detachment possessed the latest combat Dolls in his squadrons, though some of these may have resulted from twisted memories of the Lake and RPK16's interactions with Angelia’s consciousness. In Spring 2051, the war’s end was well in sight, and Anna, now a Junior Lieutenant, was made commander of the 3rd Infantry Platoon of the 57th Guards Division, allegedly stationed on “Island P” in the “Southwest Pacific”; however, given the depicted events in the Jr. Lt. section, as well as the fact that the real-life 57th Guards Motorized Rifle Division saw combat across the Eastern Front of World War II to Berlin, it’s more than likely the case that Anna and Ramzan’s operation was set in the Contaminated Zones outside Berlin, with these so-called “islands” as hot-spots of radiation. Because nothing can be created - only formatted - in the Lake, perhaps Anna once was deployed to Southeast Asia, with the Lake or RPK16 and Meitner’s tweaks gnarling the memories of the 2051 operation and her overseas deployment. However, there is the possibility of Avernus ascending whole, rising with an island in the Southwest Pacific, somehow discreetly flown or relocated to the Dead Sea before Spring 2051, as Aliana did report Operation Couatl took place on an island, but it should be acknowledged that her memories may have been altered after being mothballed, unless the mention of an “island” literally referred to the Avernus Platform floating above the Dead Sea. To be fair, if Avernus was initially located on an island in the Southwest Pacific, the exposure of its location would surely justify airstrikes or bombings against the structure. Having caught wind of US Army Ranger transports moving into the region, well within Warsaw Pact lines, 3rd Platoon was tasked with surveilling their movements to identify the purpose of their deployment.

For the Americans to push inward so far spoke volumes of their objective; nothing of strategic importance was in the immediate region that late into the war, let alone in a Contaminated Zone behind enemy lines, arousing suspicions among the ranks. Nevertheless, their presence signified a wider operation or target, and worse yet was their movement towards the Dead Sea Red Zone “island” - further confirmation of this section taking place in Germany. Inexperienced, outgunned, and insufficiently supplied, 3rd Platoon could only reconnitor the Rangers, setting up two primary Sentry Points, as direct confrontation would surely end disastrously. The first wave of Rangers had allegedly already entered the Dead Sea, and given significant electromagnetic interference from the Yellow-Red Zone border region, Alexander - a role assumed by RPK16 - and 2nd Squadron’s Wiktor’s radios were useless, maintaining watch for the Rangers and their alleged reinforcements. While Anna was ascertaining the received surveillance data, 2nd Squadron Leader Pan reported an unusual Collapse index spike at Sentry Point 2, dropping to ambient levels soon after, possibly from a Paradeus-Galatea weapon, though the controllable Boxes of Iaso hadn’t yet been created, indicating a Collapse Radiation weapon or an Epiphyllum bloom. Alexander, initially searching for additional anti-radiation drugs, found Anna deliberating earlier surveillance data, asking her role in “winning” the war and bringing everyone home - a promise that, of course, was gleeful of picturesque post-war celebrations, not the millions that lay silent below the surviving cheers. Engrossed in the local topographical, a communicator rang nearby; on the other end was Captain Ramzan, maintaining his rigid composure, issuing orders to 3rd Platoon to intercept a company of the Rangers’ ground reinforcements that slipped through the NUSSR’s military blockade.

Authorized from the brass, Ramzan pulled rank on Anna to direct the ground operation against the Ranger reinforcements, likely following the rear of the initial detachment that entered the Dead Sea. Confused by his authority, Anna explained that 3rd Platoon only had two squadrons, currently divided between Sentry Points 1 & 2, all of whom lacked ammunition and equipment to defend from such a force. Ramzan affirmed her concerns, ordering her to relocate 1st and 2nd Squadron to a line of defense, which would soon be supported by Ramzan’s men. Before disconnecting, Anna bluntly asked what the Rangers’ objective was, understanding the innate criticality of their target, to which Ramzan had reported their objective was a war criminal codenamed “Capita”, who possibly held “top secret information pertaining to Relic technology.” but limited Soviet intelligence was unable to confirm identity. Literally translating from Latin as “head” or “principle [thing]”, a dominant noun, Capita was also the target of Daybreak’s Operation Couatl in Spring 2051, with the initial Ranger party tracked by 3rd Platoon likely to be Daybreak or fellow contingent. While speculation, Meitner’s research was invaluable to Oberstein and his colleague’s plans, and in view of her move to Moscow after Beslan, it’s feasible she found herself in the Soviet Relic Department, later illegally extracting Relic data from the Soviets, assuming she found work in Moscow, for her collaboration with Oberstein in early 2051, aspiring to restart the Holy Grail to resurrect Sana and advance her research without restriction. As a former American Relic researcher, principally one who fled the US after her expulsion, both sides of the war had a vested interest in capturing or killing her before the other. From earlier leaked documents from WAVE Tech and Witkin, the Soviets cracked down greatly on illegal Relic research - especially into weapons - from 2050 onwards, sentencing sixteen to death for Relic weapon development, something Tsvigun was disheartedly familiar with. Misuse of the Relics is mirrored across the sorrowful world, and averting the possibility of another catastrophe could only be averted through total compartmentalization and capital punishment.

Operation Couatl & Capita

Group photo of Daybreak Squad, 20XX
(Unknown if CBRN soldiers in background are attached to Daybreak)

Months after their mission at the Berlin Metropolitan School, Daybreak Squadron were given a new assignment: Operation Couatl - a decapitation operation against a former Relic Agency scientist under the surname “Laplace”, codenamed “Capita”, suspected to be male by Sergeant Aliana. With limited intelligence, however, Aliana couldn’t verify the target’s identity, nor would the USASWC 75th Ranger Regiment likely brief Daybreak on every detail for the sake of operational security, in the event their data was captured by the Warsaw Pact or Laplace’s faction. Eponymous of Aztec legends of deific serpents, literally translating from Nahuatl as “serpent”, Couatl was a multi-phase excursion into the Contaminated Zone, well within the Warsaw Pact’s line of control, west of Berlin; however, the vast expanse of the northern German Yellow Zone likely provided ample cover for limited clandestine deployments. Even if the Soviets and East Germans had pressed the line of control to the edge of France, there’s a noticeable cost of sustaining forces with supplies, aid, and equipment needed in the Contaminated Zones, as 3rd Platoon, for example, required rolling stocks of anti-radiation drugs near the Yellow-Red Zone borders. Without consistent surveillance and ground overwatch - including fractured satellite networks after years of interference and ASATs, likely triggering a limited Kessler Syndrome event - a limited force could hypothetically evade detection, and given that Daybreak had already infiltrated Berlin by December 2050, American forces may have clandestinely embedded themselves in the region, perhaps disguising themselves in refugee caravans - a tactic employed by Antarctic forces in 2092.

Considering the Rangers’ actions, Daybreak was flown via transport helicopter to the Dead Sea as the initial force, receiving additional ground reinforcements - and less inconspicuously, unidentified fighter jets - after arriving at the suspected target location. Anna’s 3rd Platoon was tasked with surveilling the movements of the ground reinforcements after Daybreak infiltrated the Red Zone, with Ramzan’s comments revealing the Soviet brass caught wind of the American operation and its target. How said information leaked remains unknown, but considering the Soviets shared interest in the Relic scientist, it’s possible certain figures in Moscow suspected the American target to be the same rogue scientist, but this doesn’t explain how either side identified and profiled “him”, who allegedly possessing illegal Relic research or technologies. Obviously, “Capita” - “Laplace” was not male, instead the pseudonym of Professor Martha Meitner in her letters to Gray Blackwell; however, neither side would’ve known about these conversations, misleading the Americans to believe “his” surname was Laplace, but if limited intelligence was provided to Daybreak, then perhaps some knew her real identity. Likewise, Meitner spent a few months in Moscow after Beslan, and after Anna enrolled in the Command College, Meitner’s portrait was mounted on a wall of influential figures in the NUSSR, only rationalized if she contributed to Soviet Relic research or aided Warsaw Pact R&D, akin to her Project NGAD contributions in the USA.

In the redacted MB-13-A document - possibly from within the Promethean intelligence, given Witkin was the source - the author prefaces that a specific [REDACTED] department in the NUSSR pushed for the development of secondary Relic weapon technologies after 2050, but were promptly denied by the Central People’s Committee in Moscow; this rejection, though, was ignored by group members, who carried on research, now illegally. Once their transgressions were disclosed, sixteen “high ranking officers within [REDACTED]” were executed, with an additional unnamed individual - possibly the head of R&D - sentenced, though it's unclear if they were among the executed. This microcosm remains shrouded in mystery, only mentioned in passing from Witkin’s document in SC, and although the document certainly alludes to Carter and William’s illegal research in the Baltics, this unknown group of officers, operating outside Soviet law, paid the price of their work. Considering Meitner’s insubordination, driving her research forward by pushing the ethical boundaries and ignoring conventional methods, might it be the case she assisted this group of officers, escaping to Germany with illegal Relic data in 2051 after the crackdown? It’s tenuous at best, with the only tangible links being that of illegal Relic research and Moscow, where Meitner moved to by 2051; not to mention, in the only letter signed in Moscow, Meitner expressed her epiphany on the potential reactivation of the Holy Grail, shedding her past, supposedly cowardly, self for a new name - Hela, signatory “Laplace”. If entangled in the enigmatic group’s endeavors, perhaps Meitner escaped under her new identity, and theoretically, the Soviet Relics Department may have issued kill or capture orders on any surviving contributors or accomplices. After Blackwell recommended Oberstein, soon to assume an affluent official position, Meitner came again to meet her old friend in Germany, where she was approached by Oberstein, introducing himself and offering the collaboration for Sana’s Holy Grail experiment. Considering Paradeus was seemingly operating independently of the FRG and GDR, it’s possible Western intelligence caught wind of materials on their research, with some theoretically coming from someone surnamed “Laplace”. There’s too little information to confirm anything, but information must’ve made it to the Americans somehow, apparently necessitating a decapitation operation, though certain USASWC or intelligence officials may have deliberately concealed information on their target’s identity; tangentially, 90wish was officially a Bundeswehr special R&D group - Oberstein as its head, so unless he forsake the FRG, the Americans interestingly were conducting an assassination on a Relic Agency scientist associated with the director of a NATO ally’s R&D group. However, it’s possible intelligence suspected “Laplace” was the pseudonym of Oberstein or another official, but not directly knowing his identity.

Remarkably little is actually known about Operation Couatl’s progress, with Aliana only recollecting certain segments to the Commander in Eclipses & Saros, informing them of the squadron’s discovery: Avernus - an avaricious skyscraping monument of relentless scientific progress, floating amidst a sea of death. From Aliana’s testimony, only one tower was apparently constructed by Spring 2051, though it may have been work in progress construction, and considering the prominence of the Eastern Tower - the Hall of Prayer, its secret laboratories, and the restricted Relic Experiment Zones and Hela operating theaters - it would reasonably be erected first. Once on-site, resistance was more resilient than expected, and from what’s currently understood, Daybreak disembarked somewhere outside of Avernus or in the hot zone, encountering a considerable enemy force, presumably that of several platoons or a company of Paradeus mercenaries or Soviet ground troops. After entering the Dead Sea, Daybreak’s helicopter was downed by a missile, either crash-landing before Daybreak could properly exit or while the squadron was attempting to breakthrough, removing their only immediate allied exfiltration until reinforcements could arrive. Ambient electromagnetic interference rendered SATNAV useless, ammunition was limited, and with reinforcements stalled by Soviet forces on the Yellow-Red Zone border, likely forcing the fighters to divert and defend, no one was coming to save them; they were totally cut off, facing at least six “elite squads”, either Paradeus or a Soviet intercepting platoon or company. Notably, the situation was at its worst when Daybreak found themselves pinned down in a tunnel with masonry walls, and although exceptionally tenuous, it’s possible they were chasing Capita in the Avernus Platform, who may have been rushing for the regional subway out of the Dead Sea, as the pre-WWIII industrial architecture denoted the former UNRA base beneath Avernus. Supported by Private First Class Amaris’ sniperfire, the other eight Daybreak members steadily advanced, but their stagnant rate of movement would’ve ensured Capita’s escape had Aliana not received the order from command.


Aliana’s crimson-red vision after the Dog Tag procedure was executed.

Had Aliana’s performance just slightly improved, she believed it was the edge needed to turn the tide, only to receive a superior command once it became obvious Daybreak’s ground and air support wouldn’t arrive in time, ordering her to execute Dog Tag procedure. Given the design of the Dog Tag & Door System was based on the principles of Meitner and Blackwell’s Holy Grail and later Evangel Axis designs, Aliana protested, knowing the consequences that would befall her teammates, but her pleas went unheard when Couatl’s Commander force-executed the program, instantaneously flipping a switch in her neural cloud as she lost all supremacy to the Dog Tag. Almost as if swapping to an alter-ego, Aliana’s operating parameters and behavior flipped, her optics now stricken in crimson, determined solely at the completion of the mission through sacrifice - but not of her own. Amid the fight, Aliana turned her rifle on Eula first, swiftly putting down her “sister”, followed by Olivia - reluctantly accepting Daybreak’s “destiny”, promising Aliana she’d one day regret this - until all of Team A had fallen; watching from afar, Amaris tried contacting Eula to restrain Aliana from making rash decisions, instead met with the grayed-out profile in the team’s Daybreak System, then changing to “Deleted” after Aliana put Eula down and absorbed her “Dog Tag” (abilities) to bolster her own performance. When Aliana returned with an order to snipe a certain person, Amaris saw firsthand her leader execute Samantha and the others; overwhelmed, Amaris shouted at Aliana to explain what happened to Eula, who was alongside Aliana at the time of the Dog Tag’s execution, to which Aliana bluntly assured her soldier that they needed to force their breakthrough. It’s believed at this time Amaris realized her team leader “turned traitor”, choosing to desert; meanwhile, Aliana’s last order to “purge the traitors”, possibly that of the program to absorb the abilities of those artificially deemed “traitor” to her Dog Tag half of the System, went unfilled against Amaris, limboed for thirteen years.

According to Aliana, she made contact with “him” during the operation, but her team wasn’t “sure if we encountered the man himself”, and in the most inexplicable moment of Operation Couatl, Aliana shattered enemy defenses towards Capita, bullets cracking around her. Here, the narration tells of a blood-red sky as “white light bloomed in the air”; although the sky can be rationalized as Aliana’s blurred crimson optics after the Dog Tag program activated, the white light may be extraordinary, assuming this brilliance is related to Meitner’s research. Outside of accentuating the “holy” artificial light beaming on the statue of Nike, Athena, or Nemesis in the Eastern Tower’s Prayer Hall, there’s only two known significant sources of “white light” throughout the story: the blueish-white radiance of the ephemeral Epiphyllum bloom, and the white void of Nirvana. The first lacks any definitive relation to Couatl, but “William” in 90wish, who was far too young at the time to be our William, held keen interest in the potential of these divine flowers, despite others abandoning the Collapse-Epiphyllum-purification study after the explosive bloom cycle was deemed unsuitable for their objectives. When the Epiphyllum oxypetalum outside Tallinn bloomed, a radiant blueish-white showered the sea of flowers as they bloomed. On the other hand is the possibility of a Relic activation, wherein Meitner or another Paradeus researcher initiated an experiment before or as Daybreak were detected, luminously bathing the air in white. A similar “white singularity”, so to speak, was observed emitting from the Starfish’s “core” behind Elisa as she attempted to activate it, perhaps a energized focal point or literal point of “resonance” with the Relic Network, Nirvana. The Relic’s activation opened the figurative gate between worlds, enabling those perceptive of its cryptic data streams to feel “the summons of the Source”. With only a single line in E&S, it’s a flimsy theory, but considering Meitner’s Relic research field often related to Nirvana, a similar “gate” to the Relic Network may have opened in Avernus, though there’s no evidence of this. A tertiary option was Meitner’s “flashbang” devices, temporarily disrupting Aliana’s optics as she closed the distance.

Regardless of this cryptic light, Aliana reported she entered the suspected room alone, then the operation failed; although the individual in the room is unseen, Aliana’s confirmation that she encountered the suspected Capita, though she couldn’t verify their identity, suggests she made contact with someone in that room, only to fail or be disabled before delivering the fatal blow. Ludonarrative dissonance in mind, majority of gameplay maps do not properly reflect the story; however, one battle map ends in Aliana opening a locked room, and upon moving her into the doorway, a female refugee NPC enemy is revealed and the mission immediately ends. In Aliana’s account, the climatic moment came when entering that room, and ignoring possible ludonarrative dissonance, the target within was a female NPC with telltale signs of early-state ELID. The individual’s identity was left as mystery, possibly Meitner, Lunasia, or Nemhran, but something catastrophic in that room labeled Couatl a failure. If Aliana truly came face to face with Meitner, then she hypothetically could deactivate or stall her former Doll creation, dropping Aliana in her tracks, akin to RPK16 hacking AN94 before she could kill Nyto Gray in MS; moreover, Meitner’s unnamed flashbang devices may have been enough to stall Aliana momentarily while making a break for it. A second, considerably more tenuous theory is that of Lunasia, who was forcibly taken from the Oberstein Manor in 2051, later undergoing at least 300< procedures for Paradeus’ probable experiments on immunes, consciousness, and Nirvana, eventually expiring from the torment or having lost habitance of her organic body. As Lunasia’s memories are mysteriously absent from the Lake of Cognition, yet are acknowledged by the Voices of Nirvana and the coalesced M4A1-Lunasia entity, the purpose of Lunasia’s experiments were seemingly directed into Nirvana, possibly isolating her consciousness into the data blocks, though this lacks basis, given the OGAS consciousnesses and their hosts shared a memories of the Oberstein Manor gardens’ serenity, signifying Paradeus using select memory sequences to format segments of Lunasia’s consciousness in neural cloud test subjects. If Lunasia was taken before Operation Couatl, then she probably arrived at Meitner’s operating theater, continuously extracting or resequencing memories for the Relic experiment.

When Aliana barged in, the internal circumstances are but theories, but in a very hypothetical scenario, she encountered Capita and Lunasia or Lunasia alone in the laboratory room, where Lunasia was purposefully shot or hit by an errant round or ricochet while undergoing Hela or another experiment, possibly as a link to Nirvana was established. Beyond circumstantial dates and Aliana’s incomplete testimony, little evidence exists to vindicate these ideas, but whatever truly happened in that room triggered the operation to fail and Aliana to be mothballed. As her creator, some backdoor into Daybreak could hypothetically exist, enabling escape even when Aliana closed the distance; moreover, Aliana must’ve been captured by Soviet forces eventually, given she remained in StateSec storage for thirteen years, likely pulled out and examined on multiple instances to learn more about NGAD, Paradeus, and the Dead Sea. StateSec’s “gifting” Aliana to the Commander aboard MBV Elmo alludes to the idea of certain intelligence officials knowing her history and target, believing Paradeus’ supposed facility in the Dead Sea was a continuation of the floating skyscraper discovered in Operation Couatl.

Tides of War on the Dead Sea
Although unconfirmed at this time, it’s believed Daybreak’s mission was occurring simultaneously to 3rd Platoon’s reconnaissance of the Couatl’s Ranger reinforcements outside the Dead Sea. After receiving orders to stop the flanking American contingent, 3rd Platoon swiftly ambushed the three transports, but before celebrations were in order, the characteristic thunk and whizz of mortars carried in the air as the American survivors made their retreat. Anna yanked Alexander, a role assumed by RPK16, to the ground just before impact, with both thrown by the shockwave, debris and Collapse crystal fragments crumbling over 3rd Platoon’s bodies. Before blacking out, Anna’s erratic vision and hearing sensed a familiar figure, and several minutes later, she was shaken awake by Alexander, offering a glucose ration for energy. Surrounded by her injured men, Anna caught sight of a medic Doll aiding the wounded - part of Ramzan’s squadron of Dolls sent as a rescue force just after the mortar strikes. 2nd Squad caught the worst of it, taking several casualties, including its leader, Pan. Standing before the fallen, Anna solemnly told Alexander the reason she continued pressing on, first asking his reasons for enlisting, then stated she wanted to end the war, no matter how idealistic of a dream or delusion. But as Meitner ingrained in her student, what would be the point in struggling at all if everything was futile? The war goes on, with or without them, but to trip or fall only deprives one’s self of agency; so regardless of the delusionally idyllic, we must strive for our raison d'être. Many who came before Anna held the same dream, but were it not for them, the believers of the next wouldn’t have a pathway to follow, continuing to preserve the embers through darkness.

Collecting themselves, 1st Squad’s leader, Wiktor, reported the aforementioned disrupted radio signal was received again, but due to their channel encryption, they’d need Dolls to decrypt the signal in short order; fortunately, Ramzan’s squadron comprised a few Dolls, but he refused to speak to anyone but Anna, hesitant to speak since their spout in the Command College. Entering a temporary command post established, the siblings' sternness spoke louder than exposition, exemplifying the awkwardness between them. If we are to believe they’re not twists of the Lake, the Griffin Dolls SVT38 and KS23 once served beneath Ramzan during WWIII, connoting them among the oldest Dolls in GFL, alongside Aliana, Amaris, Lee Enfield, Type 88 Hanyang, and the Fox Sisterhood. Thanking 3rd Platoon for their interception, Ramzan was justifiably worried about offering his Dolls to Anna, fearing they would reveal themselves after already sustaining casualties. Understanding Capita was likely in the Red Zone and their opportunity was closing, Ramzan’s hesitancy lost to Anna’s obstinacy, saying she’d crawl on all fours through barbed wire if circumstances left her no choice - a belief embedded into her during Beslan and eerily reflected by the price paid by her and Angelia in Slow Shock. It was only a matter of time until Capita could escape or be captured by the Rangers, so Ramzan ordered KS23 to begin decrypting the “Ranger” signal.

Once decrypted, it didn’t take long for the Soviets to realize they hadn’t intercepted the Rangers’ communications, but an unknown faction, suspected to be working beneath Capita. Over the comms, they picked up a few distinct - one in command and a three team leaders from transport “Teams 6, 7, and 8”. The individual in command ordered everyone to pick up the pace, adding “the Professor” wouldn’t wait for them to finish collecting “specimens” from their fallen enemy. By 11:22AM, all were tasked with the “loading of the specimens back at the plant”, with evacuations scheduled by 11:30AM, rapidly closing the window for Capita’s faction or the Soviets. One of the team leaders questioned why the Americans, perhaps suspecting “Capita” was the former USRA scientist Martha Meitner, had encroached this far, to which the other leader sarcastically laughed, saying that if the Rangers hadn’t come from them, they wouldn’t have made “a fortune” of “specimens”; however, this faction wouldn’t have had to “relocate” if the Americans hadn’t attracted the Soviets’ attention, pulling in the military to investigate the deep incursion into Germany or the Southwest Pacific. Notably, the first team leader expressed annoyance at having to “move” again, implying this faction has been forced to relocate to avoid exposure before, meaning its equally possible for these memories to have taken place in Germany, outside the Dead Sea, or in the Southwest Pacific, isolated on an archipelago thousands of kilometers away from the Avernus headquarters. Although these memories are suspected of taking place in Germany, it’s possible Avernus was miraculously relocated elsewhere, but to displace a skyscraper island that far without notice seems too convenient, unless this specific Ranger operation was independent of Operation Couatl, which certainly doesn’t seem the case. Nevertheless, despite the United States soon to divorce into the Second American Civil War at the war’s end, the Americans’ incessancy for Capita speaks of great importance placed on either securing her or her Relic data - especially Soviet Relic data, assuming Meitner had extracted it from Moscow - or ensuring such sensitive information couldn’t fall into the hands of either side. The most interesting part of the radio interceptions, however, was that these communications were in English. As an international lingua franca, the implications of Capita’s faction, presumably Paradeus, speaking English connotes several theories, but for brevity, these ideas are reserved for the “Possible Paradeus Origins” section in the following chapter.

Realizing the “Professor” was Capita, Ramzan and Anna knew the Capita the Rangers in the Red Zone would fail, enabling the VIP to escape long before the main Soviet force could move in; furthermore, if 3rd Platoon could verify Capita was located in the “Dead Sea”, the Soviets likely would’ve maintained surveillance and operations into the zone after spring 2051, attracting too much heat towards Avernus, unless Paradeus covertly restored its position well afterwards. Considering Bramedb mentioned privately to Gray that Operation Aeneas was Avernus’ first time being exposed, likely knowing nothing of Operation Couatl in 2051, it’s possible she was truthful, wherein Avernus hypothetically could’ve been relocated to other “stations” globally, such as the Southwest Pacific Red Zone island, though this belief rests solely on the idea that Operation Couatl and Anna’s spring 2051 memories depict different operations in 2051, thus implying the Rangers were tracking Capita for months or years. As Avernus rests upon an artificial island, mirroring the CG video discovered by Fe56 in the Avernus Platform, the “island” mentioned by Aliana may be a misnomer, unless there’s multiple skyscrapers worldwide, itself carrying many implications. Simply, with limited information currently, we cannot aptly describe Paradeus’ reach in 2051, but Oberstein - through association with Galatea and, possibly, a faction of former UNRA - possessed the necessary capital to support Meitner’s research for his group’s “plan”. Unable to break their connections, they were traced by the enemy officer, arrogantly asking if they had fun eavesdropping, with Ramzan issuing an immediate reboot order to forcibly sever KS23 and the other Dolls communications. While rebooting, SVT38 reported an “unidentified flying object” within the Red Zone bearing towards them, piercing through the green haze like a ghost, only discernible as an aircraft with two “bright blue orbs of flames” and a blazing afterburner. Closing the distance, the aircraft swept low for a pass, dropping an explosive munition on their position, then climbed away just as quickly as it arrived.

Curiously, the “UFO” attack craft is only mentioned in passing, despite obvious ownership by Meitner’s faction; emphasis on its irregular bright blue lights may indicate this as the first ingame instance of a Relic-derived aircraft, akin to the American U-2, SR-71, F-117, F-22, and “F/A-00” (sixth generation) Air Force and Navy programs. The discovery of the D-1 “Door” Relic Site underneath Lake Vostok during the First Cold War was a watershed moment in Relic development history, marking Americans’ first Relic site discovered. Through various military-industrial R&D collaborations between the Defense/Advanced Research Projects Agency (D/ARPA, probably the USRA), Lockheed Martin’s Skunk Works Division, and the US Air Force and Navy, the remnants from D-1 and other Relic sites were extracted and reverse-engineered, resulting in the development of various breakthrough airframes, avionics, and thrusters, perpetually upholding the American edge on air power over the former Soviet Union. Around the period of the SR-71A’s development, an additional draft was submitted for a cutting-edge high-altitude, high-speed strategic bomber, potentially offering a first-strike capability beyond the range of Soviet anti-air. Known as the Aurora - a name stemming from real-world alleged reports of a supposed black project reconnaissance craft, possibly hypersonic, though many of these accounts are rife with controversy - it remained in the conceptual phase until the 1970s, taking its maiden flight in July 1973. In a direct statement of superiority to the Kremlin, a squadron of Auroras took off from a Yukon airbase, traveling as needles into the Iron Curtain; at exactly 9:00AM Moscow time, the bombers crossed into Moscow airspace as a show of force, stunning the Soviet government and citizens. After ARPANET was formalized for military use, DARPA drafted a concept for an autonomous control system, based on ARPANET’s framework, for the Auroras, continuously working until the Relic Arms Limitation Treaty in 1981 was ratified; however, it’s unclear if DARPA had ever finished the design before the treaty and the end of the Cold War in 1983. While theory, the unknown attack craft that bombed the temporary command post could’ve been another example of a Relic-technology reproduction craft, equipped with air-to-ground weapons; furthermore, it’s hypothetically possible Meitner and Oberstein’s faction was made up of USRA and UNRA members, who could’ve possessed these craft, their schematics, or an understanding of the technologies in their construction. Notably, in the opening cutscene of Groza in Girls Frontline 2: Exilium, there’s a short glimpse of a bizarre, almost-fighter-esque aircraft soaring above Odessa, leaving two distinct afterburner trails from its thrusters. Although nothing links the Auroras and the GFL2 aircraft to the “UFO” exiting the Red Zone, it was clearly flown by Meitner and Oberstein’s faction, suggesting Paradeus or its predecessor had at least one Relic-based attack aircraft by spring 2051.

Minutes later, Alexander and Ramzan, whose CBRN suit was tattered in the attack, pulled Anna from the rubble of the command post while under fire from the unknown enemy faction. As soon as the Dolls and men were standing, Ramzan and Anna organized a breakout while Wiktor and Alexander tried contacting the wider Soviet force and command to no avail; however, signal for a moment, made meaningless when enemy fire destroyed Wiktor’s hand and the radio. Unfortunately, Ramzan’s support came too late when Yuri and Kozlov, two men under Wiktor’s 1st Squadron, were mortally wounded after trying to drag the dying Wiktor into cover, leaving Anna and Alexander as 3rd Platoon’s sole survivors. Still under fire, Anna requested Ramzan rendezvous with her at an abandoned building near the Red Zone, reconvening soon after while a Doll stayed behind to cover their retreat to the east. Hoping to contact the nearby Soviet sentry post for evacuation, the trio temporarily broke free from the enemy, making way towards an dilapidated factory used by their transport teams, but just before entering the building, a single gunshot rang out. Peeking through the cracks, about a dozen well-armed soldiers and their leader were standing around the body of one of the transport drivers, while the other two were held at gunpoint. No discerning features about this “Paradeus” enemy force are provided, apart from Ramzan’s guess that they were mercenary forces, probably funded by Meitner's associates.

According to his men, three stragglers managed to escape, but for the transport drivers of 3rd Platoon, the trio were powerless to stop a fully-armed squadron, forced to watch Capita’s crimes firsthand. With time running thin, a soldier pulled a few syringes of light-green fluid from a medkit while the others held down the living drivers, injecting both and the deceased third in the back of the neck. What gives the game away on the purpose of Capita’s experiment and the injections is their leader’s comment, hopeful that they’d “find it” to please the Professor; when injected, all three violently spasmed as their faces turned pale, howling like cornered beasts through gnashing teeth. Amid their mutations, the soldiers kept their muzzles raised throughout, awaiting to fire if the subjects proved failures, which all three were. With limited time, their leader ordered them to load the three bodies in the vehicle and prepare to return to base for evacuations. Considering the light-green agent employed to screen the bodies as “specimens” certainly alludes to immunity screening through Collapse Fluid exposure, which when injected into the neck, immediately triggers violent reactions among non-immunes and those of low resistance, as internal exposure to the matter would invariably cause the subject to expire or mutate from rapid-onset ELID. This places Paradeus’ immunity research well back to 2051, aligning with Riefenstahl’s assumptions about the Dead Sea, suggesting someone or a “group of people” devoted to radiation research could’ve managed to hone Nyto genetics to survive prolonged periods in high-density environments, though complete immunity has yet to be achieved. If Lunasia herself was a partial- or full-immune, it’s possible she was taken as a victim of these experiments, while Paradeus’ soldiers in spring 2051 were tasked with gathering enemy forces to screen them for their aptitude as “specimens” for immune research; however, even the bodies of failed specimens were still gathered and dumped at the Red Zone border facility, possibly used as a source of parts or raw genetic material for Paradeus’ future cloning prospects.
