In the communications intercepted by the Dolls, one of the presumed soldiers sarcastically thanked the Rangers for drawing in so many American and Soviet sacrificial lambs, providing a wealth of specimens and raw material for future endeavors, showing the group’s vested interest in immune screening.

On the other side of the factory wall, the trio were naturally furious, but all three understood there was nothing that could be done for them, except to survive with the memories of their service. As the squadron sped off, the trio agreed to rush for one of the mothballed transports, but realizing the soldier-in-charge had ordered the site to be cleaned up, Ramzan yelled for everyone to dive for cover as enemy artillery whizzed and detonated squarely on the factory, collapsing one of the walls totally; Anna was sent rolling by the pressure, Ramzan protected his head with his prosthetic left arm, and Alexander tragically was left in the open, debris crushing his lower body. Wheezing as blood pooled from his mouth, indicating his lungs were critically wounded, delirium quickly set in, calling out to his family back in his hometown as he gradually faded. Blood, soil, dust, soot, and their tears stained everything from Alexander’s suit to the Earth, with the warmth of Anna’s solemn embrace replacing his own. In his last words, he asked if his platoon leaders would lead him home, which Anna assured she would; as his eyes faded, “Alexander” told her that he’d hold her to it - possibly something Alexander actually said in 2051 or RPK16’s reflection through Alexander, indirectly insinuating her willingness to carry her leader to their destination - followed thereafter by Ramzan’s salute. Without motorized transport, all men but them lost, and a single functional radio, the situation couldn’t possibly have been more dire; moreover, the intertwining of Anna’s promise to “end the war” and honoring 3rd Platoon ignited obstinacy, impelling her towards brazenly chasing Capita, while Ramzan rhetorically asked the logic of her actions, asking what difference throwing her life away for Capita’s demise would make in the grand scheme of the war. Knowing the Rangers’ failed, this was her sole opportunity to exact revenge upon Capita, soon to evacuate; truthfully, Ramzan feared Anna pointlessly sacrificing herself, losing another closest to him, yet recognizing her incorrigible position, he followed her stubbornness to the edge of the Red Zone plant.

Into the Hornet’s Nest

The Avernus Platform in October 2064.

Surveilling the primary plant on the Yellow-Red Zone border, the base was effectively a small fortress, ringed with “trenches, high walls, electric fences, towers, and armed guards”, guaranteeing any soul brave or foolish enough to transit this far into the Contaminated Zone would certainly be spotted. At the front gate, multiple convoys of eight vans were quickly loaded with materials - presumably laboratory and medical equipment, weapons and ammunition, various drugs, “sample” boxes, and specimens - then sent on their way, replaced by another group immediately after, moving as an assembly line before the main Soviet force could arrive. Without a doubt, the amount of foot and vehicle traffic confirmed this was Capita’s primary laboratory in the region, and if we are to believe Anna’s memories occurred simultaneously to Operation Couatl, then it’s possible Paradeus evacuated via the underground railyard after Daybreak’s failure, taking the subway lines described by Judge of Fe56 as heading out of the Dead Sea Black Zone. Perhaps one of these lines connected to the primary plant on the Yellow-Red Zone border, wherein evacuation protocols involved transporting men and sensitive materials underground from the Avernus Platform to facilities on the tides of the Dead Sea, which are then loaded and shipped elsewhere by cargo vehicles; inversely, this may also be how Avernus receives materials in the 2060s. While Anna continued surveilling, Ramzan’s radio temporarily received reception, just enough to report the situation to command - in response, the brass ordered them to “monitor the plant and gather more intel on Capita”; notably, Anna and Ramzan’s mission could’ve been the Soviet and Prometheans’ first exposure to the illegal research conducted by the Relic scientist “Capita”, initiating a decade-long investigation into the unknown faction and its technology. Reifenstahl, after all, had suspicions Paradeus’ headquarters were located in the heart of the Black Zone, though if they truly suspected the Dead Sea, it’s likely they would’ve approved a clandestine reconnaissance long before Operation Aeneas in 2064. With a direct approach impossible, what Ramzan suggested was a “textbook infiltration” for rats, slipping into the facility from the exposed sewers.

Infiltrating the facility through the outlet pipe and sewers, Anna and Ramzan drudged through the dimly-lit tunnel, filled with the vile sight and smell of wastewater, blood, and the rotting flesh, unnerving to even the stern Ramzan. Passing under the perimeter barbed wire fencing, the duo continued crawling, barely maintaining composure of their movements and stomachs, eventually reaching the rear of the facility. Stopping short of their entry point, Ramzan commented that “things” were laden across the plant and its recess, presumably referring to the decomposing, gory bodies, adding that he felt he was “being drawn to them”, later ascertained by Anna to be a symptom of Ramzan’s ELID mutations after his protective suit was torn in prior attacks. Hiding behind a grate to the plant’s corridors, two soldiers were busy disposing the waste and failed specimens into the waste tunnels, casually chatting that they should follow suit after the Professor evacuated, as without her “tranquilizer, these monsters” would turn feral. His fellow soldier questioned the unusual characteristics of these “monsters”, confused how they appeared as ELID Infected, but also not, implying Meitner’s regular soldiers were not read-in on the experiment, instead paid to complete orders and avoid superfluous questions; moreover, the half-ELID appearance of these “monsters” indicates the subjects injected with the green serum were transported to this facility as possible specimens, though some could’ve undergone Hela, with ELID symptoms confused with acute Hela rejection. Disappointed in the lack of suitable specimens, the men dumped the rest of the failures behind sealed doors, then left. With the coast clear, the duo entered through the drainage grate into the corridor, then proceeded to approach the aforementioned door; peering inward, Anna was aghast to see Wiktor’s bloodied and silicified body atop a pile of others, dressed “in different military uniforms and even civilian clothes”, implying Meitner’s subjects came from all backgrounds - civilian or military, regardless of side of the war, having captured both Soviet and American troops during this operation. Without tranquilizers, any mobile subject would invariably attack any intruder through the sewers, as Ramzan had ascertained.

Planning their next move in the hallway, Ramzan preparing for a sensitive site exploitation and Anna readying to pursue Capita, one of the enemy soldiers abruptly returned, startled then terrified that these intruders were actually escaped monsters. Anna dove through the crack of the emergency door, kicking the soldier to the ground while Ramzan charged through, and in a few swift motions, Anna and Ramzan pinned the man to the floor, delivering several blows between them, including one from Ramzan’s prosthetic; notably, while pinned, Anna yelled in English, asking how to turn off the tranquilizer valves, possiblying signifying these monsters - perhaps early predecessors to Nytos - were specimens of either unsatisfactory or successful result, depending on Meitner’s intentions with these beasts, given the drugs injected into the Specimen Compartment rooms were of the same categories as Anna’s postoperative. However, these drugs may not necessarily be the same, as the characteristics of these monsters are not entirely synonymous with modern Nytos, as the crude, almost Frankensteinian abominations of spliced flesh and metal in Commander Angelia’s section were more akin to contemporary Nytos, with these 2051 monsters as either attempts to control ELIDs or rejected Hela subjects or both; in this case, filtered successful specimens are presumably taken to the facility for processing and operation, undergoing either Hela or another experiment on “controlling” ELID, perhaps honing the genes of partial- or full-immunity.

Beating the English-speaking pinned-soldier, another straggler slipped away towards the facility intercom, intending to ring the alarm, only to be put down by Ramzan’s handgun, while the other was incapacitated. Looking to initiate a wider distraction, Anna walked over to the floor’s primary control installation; with the tranquilizer valve closed and the reviving agent opened, analogous to Anna’s awakening during Operation Aeneas, the specimens awakened from their docility with cracking limbs and sporadic movements, revealing the feral, sensitive characteristics of ELID Infected. By unleashing the horde, they were pressed for time before Capita could escape, knowing the enemy’s core objective would be to protect the Professor in the meantime, but the subsequent chaos no doubt provided them a necessary diversion and cover, though the duo promised to save a bullet for the other if the situation demanded it. Now side-by-side and handguns charged, it was “time to chop off the head”, referencing Daybreak’s decapitation operation against Capita, and so they dashed for the stairwell with the specimens in tow, rapidly ascending to the 3rd floor while letting the behind them guards face the pursuing horde. Adversely, the 3rd-floor corridor beyond the stairwell was open, lacking any cover to maneuver inside, with the horde behind them - said to be on “two legs, some on all fours” - leaving them no choice but to charge into the kill zone. Anna rolled into the corridor under Ramzan’s suppressive fire, putting down the two soldiers flanking the stairwell, but such aggressive action did not come without cost; in the short exchange, Ramzan took a round to the chest, limply leaning against the wall under Anna’s support. Simultaneously, four soldiers barged through a door at the end of the corridor, immediately targeting the intruders, now pinned down and sustaining injuries.

Amid the firefight, one of the concerned soldiers asked how much longer it would take for the “aircraft” to arrive, possibly referencing a Relic-technology craft similar to these “UFO”, to which the soldiers below reported being preoccupied with the horde, unable to ascend the stairwells. Above, the men ordered those trapped below to use anything available to break through to  protect the Professor, even if it meant using grenades and RPGs indoors, all while Anna maintained pressure on Ramzan’s wound. Now with just a corridor between them and Capita, along with gory sounds of rambling flesh and gunfire echoing below, they too needed to press a textbook breakthrough. Rising to cover, Anna loaded her handgun, but just before launching herself towards the end, she felt a firm grasp on her ankle as the monsters - apparently “excited” by the scent of living humans, likely emblematic of the sensitivity of ELID Infected towards anything living - were just meters away. Gripping her leg, his eyes burst open in bright red, as if completely bloodshot, while the bullet lodged in his chest was visibly ejected from his wound as his internals silicified; these symptoms retroactively revealed to Anna his high-level absorption of Collapse Radiation since the first explosion tattered his protective suit, even recalling is off-hand comment on how he felt a “draw” to the things in the sewers, as if his worsening mutations were impelling his being to “join” the horde. Readying her gun to put him down, she hesitated for a moment as the monsters were soon to swarm around Ramzan towards her, but miraculously, Ramzan’s fury erupted, jerking around to knock down the mass of flesh barreling down the corridor. Amid the grisly thrashing, blood smeared across the walls and ground, flesh was torn from bone, hanging loosely from Ramzan’s chest and jaw, and tattered fabrics were shredded from clothing as the collective roar reverberated like a scene straight from a zombie movie. Guarding Anna with the last vestiges of instincts to protect his younger sister, just as he’d promised Armin, Ramzan howled again, but this time, as instructed by an ELID “pack leader” or “alpha”, they ignored Anna and surged the corridor towards the wave of enemy soldiers, opening a temporary window towards the door. Right before entering, another soldier turned the corner and fired an HE grenade or rocket towards the crowd, detonating short of Anna and blowing the door off its hinges; however, instead of being thrown or taking shrapnel, Ramzan’s broad figure shielded her, receiving the brunt of the explosion to his back, goring it before collapsing in his last breaths.

“Happiness for Everybody, Free”

Professor Martha “Laplace’s Demon Meitner, aka Hela, stands before Anna in the Red Zone-border facility.

There, beyond the door, came the voice of that responsible for this slaughterhouse: Capita, now given a moment of respite after the horde was temporarily suppressed. Standing solemnly before a ground-to-ceiling window, sunlight silhouetting her, the devilish, serpent-like gaze gleamed back at her former student. This was Professor Martha Meitner, just as surprised to reunite under such circumstances. Bewildered and pistol raised, Anna asked if she was responsible for the research and operation, which Meitner simply confirmed, but when asked why, her reasonings were rather cryptic, still reflective of the lessons of tenacity and trust in one’s self that she ingrained in her student from 2047 onwards; moreover, their “lessons”, per se, reflect the “kindred spirit” mentioned by Meitner in her 2047 letter to Blackwell, noting her new student’s shared mentality, despite being from an entirely different background. According to her, no explanation would change or rationalize their positions, also symbolic of their shared obstinacy to pursue drastically different goals, regardless of what others say or explain otherwise; “perhaps this was meant to be from the very beginning…”, as none could alter their incorrigible decision once determined. To quote Meitner during Anna’s Hela procedure:

“No matter how many times you lose your memory, no matter how the people around you present themselves, you never change your mind. I expect nothing less from my student.”
    • Professor Martha “Hela” Meitner, aka Laplace, Chapter 1 of Slow Shock 

Although entirely theoretical, Meitner spoke how they were “destined to stand on opposing sides in the world of humans” - with Anna retaining her humanity in face of tragedy, while Meitner immolated what remained of her former identity, embracing herself as the Laplace’s Demon over Hela - likely implying their shared, yet diametrically-opposite persistence would inevitably clash; however, the direction of Paradeus’ research, aimed at the activation and entry into the Relics and Nirvana, perhaps Meitner knows they will always stand opposed - not just from the lessons, but of prescience, hypothetically perceived through Nirvana. Given the limited information from their 2051 encounter, this is little more than theory, and it’s a considerable reach because of their previous relationship, more akin to Meitner recognizing similar methods, yet differing ideals in her student.

Aghast by her former teacher’s actions, Anna uttered that Meitner sold herself to the devil, but she rejected this notion, promising she had never sold herself to anyone, yet something pushed her to such detestable ends, presumed by Anna to be the Beslan attack on September 1st, 2050, when Sana and Armin were killed. Meitner continued, assuring her indifference towards Anna, the Beslan Guards Regiment’s absence, or the tragedy itself, as the fact of the matter is that she “should never have gone to Beslan”, for her mere presence with Sana led her to where she stands today. Expelled for her deliberate violations of Relic research at the USRA - having only sold herself only to her controversial research interests, depriving her once-admired status as lead researcher of the Holy Grail Project on Nirvana and Nyto technology - she eventually found herself alone with Sana in Beslan, yet another complacent link in a chain of events from Maryland to Berlin. Perhaps there was never a change of Meitner’s heart; when an opportunity revealed itself, she always pursued it, eventually growing devoid of humanitarian restraint. Although difficult to come into the role as a mother, her actions skirted the neglect of her daughter, even if she did truly love her. In the USRA, Meitner betrayed her principles to push the boundaries of Relicology; during Sana’s attempted resurrection, she rejected Blackwell’s sorrowful letter telling her of the project’s hopelessness; and during the Hela Project, she continued driving Paradeus’ research, where the sacrifice of human life was made to satiate the Evangel Axis, which may have always been her and, possibly, Oberstein’s intentions with the Hela technologies. Time and time again, Meitner had shed her sympathies, her morals, her ethics, all towards progressing her research - research that, some day, may come at the cost of the world. She and Anna are two sides of the same coin; although they bear the same persistent mentality towards life, their positions will never change - adamant, yet worlds apart in their beliefs. As Blackwell put it, “You were already a servant of the devil!” 

Perhaps in truth, that demon that “possessed” her heart had always festered within, only manifesting when the opportunity arose. In this lust for technological Relic progress through the study of human consciousness and identity, any sense of her prior humanity was shed, degrading definitions of good and evil. By transgressing principle, she betrayed her closest friend and daughter, but through betrayal, the truth at the abyss of her heart rose to the surface, revealing an apparition of her demonic, sinful self. Although she may not have always been conscious of it, perhaps Sana’s death is what drove her off that edge, allowing her to finally reconcile with the unconsciously repressed as she immolated her former, “cowardly” self. In that unassuming novel in 2047, the author stated their inability to understand the human spirit’s virtues in the face of a ruined world. Since Beilan Island, the world’s course has been set for calamity, so how could freedom, respect, and love be defended when all sense of humanity, good or evil, is lost amidst this dying world? That nihilism is the unfeeling of Meitner’s heart - a scientific demon lacking regret, willing to sacrifice anything, including her past self, to achieve the illusive potential of the Relics and Nirvana. And like the couatl in the Garden of Eden, Meitner’s viper-esque, green gaze reflects only sin. Despite differing motivations, William and Meitner share common ground in discovering this potential; the objectives differ, but the methods stay the same. If the Relics are but a monkey’s paw, cursing the world to destruction when that ultimate day of communion arrives, then all this bloodsoaked effort would prove naught.

Standing before that which was once her teacher, gun raised, they sat in silence for a moment, broken by Meitner quoting a revised version of the end of Roadside Picnic, by the Strugatskys brothers. Set in an unnamed country many years after the “Visitation”, the alleged first contact of a rational extraterrestrial species with Earth, the novel highlights the adult life and introspections of Redrick Schuhart, a former International Institute for Extraterrestrial Cultures laboratory assistant-turned-“stalker” surrounding the “Zone”. Almost thirty years before, Earth was spontaneously “struck” six times, seemingly at random, from the “Pilman Radiant”; eponymous with its proponent, Dr. Valentine Pilman, who postulated the source of these so-called “Visitation” impact “Zones” originated somewhere along the Earth-Deneb Line - Deneb being the apex star of the Cygnus constellation - colloquially referred to as this radiant. One of these “Visitation Zones” landed squarely in the fictional small mining town of Harmont, presumably in Canada; overnight, unusual phenomena - gravitational concentrate anomalies that can eviscerate the body; fields of sudden scorched air, as if encapsulated by an invisible thermobaric; spontaneous, low-arcing lightning amid blue skies; land laden with the horrid stench of viscous slime; inexplicable mutations of the former residents and children of the Zone explorers; and so forth - coincided the emergence of even stranger objects - infinite batteries, immovably linked disks, physical growths of unidentified substance, and harmless nicknacks and jewelry - across the Zone that drew attention from the global scientific community and those seeking a quick paycheck alike. Often conflated in legend, these objects were otherwise strewn about randomly, discovered by prospectors and would-be wish-seekers; colloquially referred to as “stalkers”, these daring few dove into the Zone for these artifacts, always ending up the same: rich, imprisoned, or dead - their one commonality, however, is their desire of the riches - be they scientific, religious, or purely monetary - from legal and illegal expeditions into the Zone. Becoming the core focus of the global scientific community, including the Extraterrestrial Cultures institute, in the past decades, the Visitation itself was one of the hottest debated topics, insisting on who, what, when, where, and most significantly, why. Why did this alien civilization contact us? Did they seek to be our salvation, our destruction, our masters, or simply, a short stop amidst the relatively infinite cosmos? These questions are the core of Roadside Picnic, with humanity’s reactions to the Zones’ phenomena and technologies taking focus, namely the path of an individual’s self-satisfaction or self-discovery, even if it ends in death.

The concepts and themes presented in the novel echo throughout Girls Frontline’s wider worldview, particularly regarding the discovery and exploitation of the Relics, as well as the deadly consequences for our misunderstanding or deliberate misuse. The discovery of the Relics and the emergence of the Visitation Zones both prove that humanity was not alone in the universe, though the former has exclusively come from Earth thus far, seemingly predating humanity; nevertheless, the miraculous potential of these phenomena and technologies exceed that current human perception, though over time, our civilization continuously studies and develops hypotheses on their origin and purpose, furthering our collective understanding and communion with the unknown. In Chapter 3 of Roadside Picnic, the “supervisor of the electronic equipment supplies for the Harmont branch of the International Institute of Extraterrestrial Cultures”, Richard Noonan spoke privately with Dr. Pilman, exchanging theories on the origin and purpose of the Visitation as a whole, spanning from the prelude to an alien invasion to something as benign as the eponymous title, “roadside picnic”; however, all these theories mirrored what the individual sought from the Zone in some way. Pilman was prolific in his field; as a former Harmonite and man of science, he likened the concept of humanity’s perception to that of a monkey and set of two buttons - one red, one white, releasing a banana or orange, respectively. The monkey may understand that hitting the button delivers its fruit, but it currently lacks the comprehension required to understand the source and “relation” these buttons, symbolizing products of the Zone, have on the outcome, symbolizing the effect and purpose of the unusual artifacts and technologies.

All this technology was left behind for a civilization that fundamentally cannot ascertain its purpose in its current stage, yet in this indeterminacy, the agents of the Visitation may very well be elevating humanity indirectly, bestowing the Visitation as the gateway to civilizational progress. Likewise, both the Relics and Zone objects are akin to the buttons, pressed by a primitive civilization that hasn’t yet understood function and purpose but recognizes results - “Empties” become nicknacks and subjects of material science and Morons become doomsday weapons. As for extraterrestrials’ reason for Visitation, that question may not be answered for many years to come, if ever, but when asked by Noonan for his belief, Pilman characterized it as a “picnic”. In this scenario, a hypothetical group of people are riding down the countryside, surrounded by nature; on the way to their destination, the party takes a short detour and pulls over near a “meadow”, emblematic of a pristine planet, to enjoy the rest of the night around a campsite. All the unnatural objects and technologies that are intrinsically human, ranging from candy wrappers to radios, are brought out during their short visitation to the meadow, where human comradery occupies a small area of wildlife until the morning. From the perspective of fauna, a force as alien to them as an extraterrestrial civilization is to us temporarily visited their otherwise quiet land, all once living in harmony until the emergence of this external, unknownable presence; meanwhile to us, all we’ve done is leave a meager imprint on the land, evidenced materially by unknown substances or pollutants left behind, such as gasoline and batteries, and physically, such as forgotten tools, torn fabrics and loose metal, and containers strewn about - none of which could be rationalized by a lesser species, only experimented with for the results, oblivious to function. That is the Roadside Picnic hypothesis - that the Visitation may have been nothing more than a temporary stop “on some road in the cosmos” (Strugatsky, Roadside Picnic [Cryptomaoist Edition], pg. 88). Even if the Relic Civilization wasn’t some cosmic passerby, its technologies nevertheless faced similar dilemmas to humanity in wake of the Visitation, inspiring scientific research to ascertain the results of technology we haven’t yet understood the function of.

Although united in the Zones’ mysteries, the stalkers, working for their own self-interest or paid by greater entity, are just as factionalized as the scientific community, presenting a span of characters with thoughts of spoils taken from perilous treks to those who willingly dive head-first into the expanse to return the Devil’s things. The subject of much of the novel, Redrick Schuhart was a veteran of the Zone living just outside the Zone in Harmont, taking routine dives for IIEC research purposes and later personal-gain, accepting the stalker lifestyle as the only way to support his later family. At age 23, a trio of stalkers, Laboratory Assistant Schuhart at its stead, set out for the garage, an untouched goldmine of “swag” - stalker slang for objects extracted from the Zone, often sold for profit. His two “greenhorns” - slang for Zone newbies - Kirill and Buzzard Burbridge narrowly escaped with their lives, but all three returned in relatively safety, cautious of the visible and nearly-imperceptible dangers. Returning from their expedition, Schuhart eventually made his way to the Borscht bar - common grounds for stalkers, military, and scientists in the Harmont region - to blow off steam. While immersed in the atmosphere, Richard Noonan of the IIEC and Gutalin, a fellow “stalker”, so to speak, barged in together, inviting Schuhart to join them for a round of drinks. Gutalin was unique in that regard: he did not seek the wealth of knowledge or gold, but the return of the Zone’s artifacts to their home, believing the Visitation to be a sign of demonic intent on upon the Earth, with their swag representing nothing but the temptation of Satan; the inverse of other stalkers, Gutalin’s organization, the Fighting Angels, voluntarily purchased swag to return it to the devil’s domain, ensuring none would unintentionally become its evil servants. Juxtaposed to Meitner’s unquenchable technological progress, untold thousands have been offered up as sacrificial lambs to an idyllic fantasy built upon foundations of blood, proposing that human life as it from the Creator could be emulated. It’s likely the case that Meitner’s mentality towards life was a precondition for heinous research, never once hesitant to push another boundary, but it wasn’t until Sana’s death that the veil worn by the devil within her was removed, never selling her soul to anyone but herself. In Blackwell’s final letter to Meitner in 2051, Blackwell lamented that her once-praised senior stooped to such abhorrent ends to revive Sana, itself an excuse to restart the Holy Grail Project, thus rejecting the cycle of life by wielding the keys to the lake of fire. When Blackwell priorly explained the enormous energy consumption of the Evangel Axis, she expressed that acceptance was paramount, as the Nyto result was demonstrably not Sana, and she would never go to the extent of sacrificing the living’s bioenergy to satiate the Evangel to maintain and perfect the Lake-Evangel System. Yet, Meitner accepted the unacceptable, researching that which humanity may have never been bestowed, defiant to Gutalin’s warnings.

Ready to raise glasses with Schuhart and Noonan, Gutalin gleefully sung the praise of God in defiance of those who embraced that which was taken from Satan’s nest, joking with Schuhart about his “servitude” to the devil and its toys. Although initially presented as factually zealous, which he certainly was, Gutalin grew close to Schuhart despite their diametrically opposite, yet mutual in cycle, beliefs; Schuhart and the stalkers extracted artifacts, and Gutalin returned them. However, amid his cheer in the Borscht, Gutalin spoke of their “blindness”, telling them to awake from their daydreams before temptation of the satanic “gifts” cursed them, immediately stalling to order a round of drinks. Obviously, he harbors little hatred against those who succumb to temptation, instead preaching the consequences of such transgressions, for what honor and reward exists in only loving those who hold you in the highest respects? Both Gutalin and Noonan were close friends with him and his family for nearly a decade, with his daughter even referring to him as “Uncle Gutalin” later in life. Unfortunately - or rather, inevitably - for Schuhart, temptation caught up with him as it did others, with lives lost to various phenomena in the Zone, left penniless in the streets, families divided, or thrown behind bars when deemed inimical by others.

Submerged in the Lake of Cognition, Angelia and Blackwell’s 2051 snapshot discussed the structure of the Lake-Evangel System, explaining how the quasi nature of the system’s supposed immortality - that all things born from the Lake are bastardized shadows of a former self, crudely sequenced and imitated as the reflection of one’s image in a cracked mirror; the resemblance is there, but imparity separates human artifice from the true Creator. In the morally-sound foundation of Blackwell, the perfection of Nyto technology is antithetical to her core - albeit, even she recognizes the Holy Grail’s innate allure. Capturing a soul in the Lake like lighting in a bottle was a miracle of science, surely, but what defines the red line of the scientific community regarding this miracle, and at what cost? Meitner, tenacious as ever, ascribed to the mentality of continuously pushing these boundaries, never selling loyalty to anyone but herself and her work; Blackwell, on the other hand, ascribed to a strict moral code, conducting herself and teaching ways befit of her life-long oath, adherent to never surpass her dignity and ethics. This epiphany is the crux between the Hopkins researchers, so when a grand opportunity presented itself, both were naturally prideful of their work, yet opposite in willingness to pursue the morally gray. In the Lake, Blackwell commented about a “vague sense of triumph” within her when learning Nyto technology had progressed to a point of stability, that her theory for the Evangel Axis was vindicated; however, her antipathy to her abhorrent creation, unable to close Pandora’s Box, was self-evident: the Lake-Evangel System is built upon a foundation of bodies and souls, utterly antithetical to her ascribed morals. It is, ultimately, “a deadly temptation for all scientists”, so easily wooed by intrigue and potential of this sanguine miracle. Just as Gutalin believed the devil’s things should rest with the devil, the allure inevitably drew the temptation of stalkers and researchers alike. Whether it be self-gain or research, the cost for many was their humanity, accepting depravities and crimes as mere stepping stones to ascertain meaning or fill their pockets. After witnessing so many lose their individuality and humanity - in a literal sense, with the dissolution of consciousness in the Lake through the Evangel, and in the figurative sense, with Meitner abandoning her sense of morality and “saving humanity” to ascertain the Relics and beyond - Blackwell of the Lake was haunted by guilt, realizing she was used, yet voluntarily accepted to create this abomination, forced to accept she could not return the genie from the bottle she opened. Like Gutalin, the price of Nyto technology and related research was a temptation that mustn't come to fruition, for she understood best the demonic cost of pursuing it, as her once-closest friend was stolen by Satan’s allure.

At age 28, now working as an independent stalker, Schuhart said goodbye to his wife, Guta, and his daughter, Maria - or “Monkey”, born of the blood of a stalker who long exposure to the Zone had drastic effects on his kin, resulting in a human girl of fur; the very reason stalkers usually don’t have children - before setting out an another expedition, this time with fellow older stalker, Buzzard Burbridge. On this mission, Burbridge sustained major injuries to his legs, unable to steadily return without assistance; pleading to Schuhart, desperation was setting in before security could discover them, surely stealing their swag or worse. In return, Burbridge offered up the location and a map to reach the pivotal artifact: the Golden Ball, a legendary tale of a radiant orb, said to grant the wish of any prideful or timid soul. Upon their narrow escape, Burbridge urgently needed a doctor, though time had already gone on too long, requiring the Butcher to amputate both his legs from the knees down. In the time following their extract, Burbridge’s wife, Dina, warned Schuhart to stray from the foolish course that Burbridge allegedly set, the Golden Ball itself becoming a trap for the prideful and avaricious, but this warning meant nothing in the context of myth, for how could such a thing exist?

At age 31, following a three-year prison sentence after being set up by local military and influential figures in wake of his rescue of Burbridge, Schuhart returned to the stalker life once more, incapable of work beyond the Zone’s scope for his proficiency; however, nearly a decade of constant scientific, military, and private development around the Zone was virtually starving it, becoming a sort of tourist destination on its fringes, but the Golden Ball remained as the one the Zone’s last kept secrets, unmoving and well-hidden deep into the Zone, beyond several phenomena. Destesting Burbridge as much as he had, Schuhart accepted the offer nonetheless, but penetrating the Zone that deeply necessitated a partner, traveling together for equal chances of wishes to all worthy of making it that far. Burbridge’s son, Arthur, was perhaps the most insistent in the family after his father’s accident three years earlier, and on a certain visit, Arthur approached Schuhart about his future expedition to the Golden Ball; having heard the legends from his father plenty of times before, the tenacious young man - fresh out of law school, dreaming idyllically of his future career and the prospect of stalking, and bereft to the brutal truths of the Zone - pleaded Schuhart bring him under his wing, as none could teach him like this veteran. Of course, Arthur was operating well outside his father’s permissions, still very much young and eager, but neither of them were too certain the Golden Ball was capable of the fantastical tales told by Burbridge; nevertheless, this Schuhart didn’t accept the young man’s requests out of good will, but as a way to get back at the roughneck and apparently ruthless Burbridge, who likely used the Golden Ball before to attain status and perfection in his family and public life, all while Schuhart was consistently the subject of “meanness and treachery”, dealing with who he described as fools. Anything antithetical to Burbridge or those that led him to destitution became false justification, willing to expend Burbridge’s perfect son as the sacrificial lamb for a promised 500,000 payment and the possibility of changing all in his downtrodden world.

After an arduous hike towards an abandoned quarry, far off the beaten path of the Zone, both nearly meeting grisly ends from scorchers, lighting storms, and so forth, the mine and its golden treasure were finally in sight. As the sole marker Burbridge placed on the map, the Golden Ball was located somewhere near a decrepit excavator’s cabin, too heavy to carry on its own. During their approach, Schuhart’s sporadic mind caught up with him, reflecting the shortfalls and challenges faced over his life’s journey and this expedition, increasingly boiling at evoked self-pity. He imagined the abrasiveness of his father; the sweetness of Guta, replaced by his beloved, yet abnormal Monkey; the cost of being a stalker, emotionally and physically - you could just as easily end up dead as you could with a family lesser than that of Burbridge, ignorant that they and everyone still loved you, despite your stalker lifestyle; the loss of a fellow stalker and great friend, Kirill to a cobweb years earlier in the Zone; and finally, himself. He reconciled with the fact that he was dragging this boy along with him to die, a boy who’d done no wrong but to stand in the way of Schuhart’s detestment of Burbridge, so that he could wish for a better fate for his own family. Wallowing in self-pity, his selfish spite drove him towards the Golden Ball, just as tenacious selfishness delivered Burbridge; despite not being an evil or immoral, per se, Schuhart’s epiphany was brought on by his decisions, mired between his unyielding adherence to being a stalker and the effects it had on himself - escaping by the skin of his teeth on multiple occasions, even being thrown into a prison for a couple years for his stalking; his friends - losing Kirill to the Zone; and especially his family - Monkey’s condition and Sr. Schuhart’s “zombification” into a husk. Interspersed by the imprints others left on his life, all he could harp on was how his selfishness consistently brought him back to the Zone, even when its effects were self-evident. Throughout his life, Schuhart wasn’t inhuman, nor did he live deliberately malicious, much the opposite regarding his beloved friends and family, but as he and Arthur journeyed towards the quarry, the dam of repressed self-pity burst, visibly shaken by his reconciliation that he was, in fact, letting an innocent young man for the sake of his idyllic scene of his family.

Nearing the edge of the quarry, he subconsciously questioned if he could actually save both of them, defiant of Burbridge’s methods to seek the Golden Ball, yet these thoughts were repressed when daydreaming of watching Burbridge pay a price of blood for supposed transgressions, even when his son had done no wrong than exist in the shadow of his father’s sins. This is the dilemma Schuhart found himself mired in: he recognized this course was innately morally wrong, displaying his false belief that his ego was worlds apart from the pompous Burbridge, though there’s certainly differences between them, but when you acknowledge your inhibitions, an opportunity at redemption may still be possible; nevertheless, his egotistical self painted its own vision for a world antithetical to redemption, a world in which the forces who wronged Schuhart and his family paid the price, ironically often brought on by Schuhart’s own tenacity. He would let none lead his life no longer, taking the lead of all decisions in his life, becoming egotistical embroiled in the world order, but this would surely come at the price of his humanity; and that was something he wouldn’t so easily abandon, as humanity’s abstracts, such as love and compassion, remained embedded deep within him. Although he certainly fell victim to mistreatment and disrespect from others, he projected his lesser side on others, feigning fault at the feet of awful men like Burbridge. Walking a tightrope between dignity and egoism, he was brought ever closer to the world-altering legend, leading Arthur on a treacherous roadside stroll built upon a lie to Burbridge and himself.

Mirroring Schuhart’s dilemma greatly, Meitner’s life has long been divided between the premier Professor Martha Meitner and Hela, the manifestation of self-interest once buried deep within her heart. Once the shining star of JHU APL and the USRA, Meitner’s grounded, ethical approach towards Relic research represented foundations paved in the field, but after consistently being railroaded by the USRA, even by the standards she created, she probably was faced with a similar epiphany to Schuhart, questioning her life’s decisions after seemingly innumerable shortcomings in her work, with her apprehension towards the USRA suggesting the artificial guidelines were roadblocks to advancing the Holy Grail Project’s research. After the order came down to expel her from the agency, the two officers sent to inform her of the immediate termination were verbally assaulted, lambasted with exclamations of the USRA’s “bubble of bureaucracy” that allegedly made it impossible to progress without shattered boundaries. Even if Meitner is factually correct in the belief that the Relics wouldn’t respond to conventional means, she was ignorant of Gutalin’s warning of temptation, evidenced by the moral abhorrence of the Lake-Evangel System - a construct to sacrifice bodies and souls to refine Nyto technology, so as to activate the Relics. Although obstinate in her studies, always pursuing an opportunity when it presented itself, regardless of the cost of dignity, Meitner’s violations caught up to egoism, landing her in the sights of the USRA’s upper brass, and after Sana’s death in 2050, what remained of the facade that was Martha Meitner, stuck between adherence to human order and egoism, was erased as Laplace’s Demon took root in her soul, exemplified by relinquishing her former name for Hela, the eponymous goddess and realm of death. Laplace’s Demon and Hela - once human, turned demon after possessing the vessel of Martha Meitner; however, where she strays the furthest from Schuhart’s dilemma is her abandonment of self, accepting Satan’s alluring song gnawing at her consciousness, while Schuhart remained in that limbo until recollecting Arthur’s parting words to him.

Upon their arrival at the quarry, the Golden Ball was well in-sight, just down the slope, past the long shadows of excavators and mining buckets. Tucked into the dirt and scrap, the actually-copper-colored orb was expectedly not exactly as myths told of it, but there was an allure, subconsciously pulling their minds closer to rest next to it; and now near the end of their journey, Arthur could do nothing more than cheer. Clearly too large to move alone and trapped behind nearly impenetrable waves of phenomena, it was no wonder the Ball was believed to be the last major object left in the Zone, as if fallen from the pocket of a massive entity along with the litter of other artifacts. Enamored in joy and beret of caution, Arthur threw himself down the slope towards the Golden Ball, his mind adrift in wishful daydreams to carve his own future, beyond the projected path Burbridge laid out for him. The Golden Ball answered the innermost desires of one’s self, and so too would it answer Arthur’s - if Schuhart had warned him of the quarry’s meatgrinders. Arthur was not just a traveling companion, but his “talking key” to the Golden Ball, blocked from entry by the meatgrinder gravitational anomalies hidden in the long shadows. As Burbridge had told Schuhart, someone must fall victim to the meatgrinder to reveal the path forward; only then would the Golden Ball listen to the heart of its beholder. As Arthur sprinted downward, Schuhart overheard the young man’s exhilaration for making it this far, shouting out his wish for the world and his epitaph: “Happiness for everyone! …Free! … Nobody will leave unsatisfied!” (Strugatsky, Roadside Picnic [Cryptomaoist Edition], pg. 124), wishing for ubiquitous idealism of happiness, freedom, and self-satisfaction for all, antipodal to his father’s own selfish wishes. Schuhart couldn’t bring himself to watch, but Arthur’s last words resonated within his soul, realizing that wishing against someone was no better than cursing, and if he was to wish for something bad, what difference would there be between him and Burbridge, reconciling that Arthur was entirely his fault; however, despite committing a sin that would cloud his conscious forever, amends could be made in respect to him and the imprint he left on Schuhart. As Arthur charged, Schuhart sat in silence, drink in hand, awaiting the inevitable to take Arthur. All the picturesque scenes dancing in Arthur’s mind of wishful, ideal thinking were silenced as a force threw him into the air, contorted his body, and cast it above and beyond the quarry.

While he may never be forgiven for Arthur, such an overtly egotistical act brought his self-pity to the forefront of his consciousness - not wallowing in sorrow for forgiveness from the Golden Ball, but using the opportunity to find a quantum of salvation for the betterment of humanity, rather than himself. Similarly to Meitner, this moment of human clarity came at the point of tragedy, diverging in positions while mourning. To quote the videogame, Deus Ex: Human Revolution, when “morality can become our saving grace”, the recognition of wrongdoing itself is proof of a chance at redemption, for as long as you realize and regret the consequences of your negative actions, a glimmer of your dignity remains; although redemption may never come, a chance of reconciliation is a privilege only befit of those still morally-sound, representing the inhibition of your soul, karma, or consciousness against the morally-reprehensible. Schuhart never shut that voice out, enabling the Golden Ball to grant his wish of an idyllic world for all, yet Meitner had shut it out, leaving nothing but a physical human vessel, solemnly empty of the humanity that once occupied it. Or could it be said that Meitner’s answer to humanity’s raison d'être lies beyond Nirvana, and the abandonment of her humanity for Paradeus has advanced her closer to the Golden Ball that could paint a world of Paradeusian unity?

With the road clear, Schuhart followed Arthur’s footsteps, cautious not to fall victim to dangers cloaked in shadow, and as he drew closer to the orb, all thought left him, replaced only by Arthur’s cheers playing back innumerably, louder with every step. With Anna’s gun raised, Meitner paraphrased Schuhart’s litany before Golden Ball, indirectly stating the similarity between her and Schuhart, while highlighting the pivotal foil in their lives. Both were animals driven by self-interest, willing to sacrifice an innocent life for a self-centered fantasy, whether it be the Lake or the quarry; both lacked the words to rationalize their ambitions, as they were both held back by vanity, stubbornly opposed to diverting their course; and both were couldn’t think, as those around them, as well as their innate egocentric mentalities, meticulously deprived them of morality to different degrees as the artifacts of another civilization tempted them. Ultimately while not the same, Meitner and Schuhart share a resemblance until Arthur’s death, with the sacrifice of the innocent as the back-breaking straw either eroding all sense of their humanity or compelling morality to reconcile with their life’s missteps; Meitner satiated the Lake of Cognition and Evangel Axis with the memories and bioenergy of students and many more after 2051, and Schuhart sent Arthur to the grave to reveal the pathway through the meatgrinders. Meitner embraced Burbridge and Schuhart’s egocentrism to advance her research through unspeakable methods, while Schuhart embraced the golden opportunity to help the world, unwilling to curse his fellow men, thus preserving the embers of his morality. Neither might be forgiven, but the foil between them depicts Schuhart’s reconciliation as the pivotal departure from Meitner, whose sanguine research smothered her flame of humanity, now just another vessel embracing by the serpent's sinful allure. The irony in Meitner quoting Schuhart’s litany is self-evident, as she is his foil in the end, innately cynical of the futility of defending what little remained of humanity in this collapsed world. Before the Golden Ball, Schuhart’s litany was now a declaration, promising that his soul was still very much human, and for his self-interest, he never was a slave to anyone like Meitner. Only answering to the innermost desires of its beholder, the Golden Ball - all knowing as it were, with Meitner paraphrasing a revised “Laplace’s Demon” alongside “all-knowing”, likely the origin of her pseudonym - supposedly could glimpse the essence of our beings, reading our consciousnesses over the course of our lives to conjure that we most desire, and as a pure, human soul of sound morality from regret, Schuhart’s heart contained the candor to realize Arthur’s wish: “Happiness for everybody, free, and no one will go away unsatisfied!” (Strugatsky, Roadside Picnic [Cryptomaoist Edition], pg. 126), for the Golden Ball was “all-powerful…all-knowing, like Laplace’s Demon”.

Meitner had nothing to add, only comparing herself to Schuhart’s journey until the quarry, where they differed greatly. When Meitner poses the question “If everything in life is futile, then what is the point in struggling?”, she asks rhetorically what one would do on the edge of the quarry, probing how one would conduct themselves for the rest of their lives when so much humanity, including your own morality, has been scrapped away as civilization and individuality unfurls in face of tragedy. Lacking respite from the Zone and maliciousness from the bad actors that repressed them, including their own inhibitions, Schuhart managed to cling to his humility, while Meitner voluntarily let go, embracing only herself as she fell into Niflhel. For what reason would there be to abandon humanity’s abstracts - turning our daggers against the world while willfully ignorant of our missteps - but to perpetuate the cyclical chaos that brought us to the very status quo we seek to break from? In the final scene of Jr. Lt. Anna’s section, Martha nihilistically states the final end for us all since humanity’s first wars to our current struggles is to kill ourselves. A gunshot then rings out as the screen turns black, followed thereafter by Schuhart’s litany before the Golden Ball. However, its unclear who fired the shot; Anna had her pistol raised, but Meitner’s final words evoke suicidal ideas, possibly implying she quickly drew her gun and killed herself before Anna fired. But if Meitner died in that facility, regardless of who fired - evidenced by Commander Angelia’s brief thought in 2062 about “that person not existing in this world anymore” - then how did Meitner survive? There are a few guesses, and given the total lack of evidence or contextual clues, they’re just that, made worse by the fact that we cannot confirm what parts of this ending may be subject to the twisting of memories by the Lake and the Hela procedure. A - despite Anna believing “that person” didn’t exist in anymore, perhaps Meitner threw on her improvised “flashbang” devices to escape, but as said, this idea is inimical to the belief that Meitner was dead; B - however unlikely it would be for Anna not to confirm the kill, Meitner may have survived the shooting or suicide, recovered by Paradeus after Anna regrouped with the wider Soviet force; C - considering Blackwell seemingly managed to duplicate her consciousness as a snapshot to insert into the Lake in 2051, perhaps Meitner was killed, but was resurrected by a construct of the Lake System without the Evangel, with Paradeus replicating and inserting another instance of her consciousness into a specimen, test subject, clone, or more fantastically, a Doll; or D - a tertiary possibility, wherein Sergeant Aliana barged into the room Capita was suspected to be hiding, disrupting Anna and Meitner’s standoff. In this scenario, Aliana’s Dog Tag procedure was executed as the Soviets were nearing Capita, breaching the room as an immense white light bloomed in the air, which could’ve been that of Meitner’s flashbangs or an opened gate into Nirvana, though this idea lacks precedent and still wouldn’t explain Angelia’s false beliefs, barring the exceptionally hypothetical of Meitner passing into Nirvana before Anna or Aliana could fire. For now, there’s far too little to make an educated guess, yet “something” happened between them that made Angelia believe her teacher was no longer on this Earth.

Chapter 4 - Abide the Day of Her Return (2040s-2062)


In January 2049, Persicaria and Lycoris fled Germany as the Americans closed the net in western Germany, while Oberstein had earlier sent his children away to the Oberstein Manor, presumably to keep them out of harm’s way as well. They might have been moved across the border thanks to Griffin Lyons or Captain Berezovich Kryuger’s help, but the timeframe for their involvement is murky; this wasn’t the end of 90wish, though. When she first joined, she believed it was a simple, private research group, but soon discovered it had massive funding from an unknown sponsor, later revealed to Oberstein, using his immense wealth and position to greatly support the organization. The group’s proper name was the Bundeswehr Special Technology Development Group, which likely supported the Federal Republic of Germany’s Bundeswehr early on, later shifting to a more independent, isolated position. Although tangential, it’s possible the Leipzig University of Karl Marx’s Doll project was granted to the team by the Bundeswehr, without actually informing the Labor-90 laboratory researchers of what they were involved in. As she dove deeper into the organization, she realized that sects of 90wish were involved in various illegal research fields, leading to her to leave the organization sometime in the early 2050s, possibly 2054. When asked if 90wish was responsible, she denied, believing that its research had ultimately just fallen in the wrong hands, but previously unbeknownst to her, there was a direct connection between 90wish and Paradeus, being the research group’s own head and son.

90 Long-Cherished Wishes - 2045-2054?
Presumably after 2051, while Persicaria and Lycoris continued their work in 90wish, an enigma of a 90wish colleague, simply known as “Professor William”, rose to prominence, but nothing was known about “him” to many within the group. Although many fields were researched, some even considered illegal, William was ruled as an exception among exceptions - his identity was entirely veiled, made opaque by his electronic voice modulator, along with him never revealing his face before. Disliked among the team for his generally rude and off-putting manners, little positives could be said about his character; however, Persicaria recognized his practically unrivaled genius and was concerned by his research field - he was obsessed with Relic technologies and the Epiphyllum oxypetalum flower, a species possessing a natural ability to absorb ambient Collapse particles, with one major issue: the explosive release of Collapse Radiation during their nocturnal bloom. 90wish had once conducted a study on the potential of plants to decontaminate the zones, but the exceptionally-hazardous bloom meant no such effort could be achieved with this species. Persicaria added that, before she’d left 90wish sometime in the early 2050s, William was constanting cultivating new iterations of the species, despite the flower’s obvious failure.

In another one of 90wish’s experiments, they hypothesized the Relic Civilization used genetic information for access privileges into the systems, and 90wish aimed to test the compatibility of the human body to the Relics’ ionized-state adjustable-volume devices. Traditionally considered impossible due to the immense emission of Collapse Radiation, guaranteeing infection in research subjects, it was postulated that a subject with a body of similar affinity to Collapse Radiation could bear the brunt to activate Relic’ outermost devices, where others would rapidly contract ELID. Of course, this was entirely theoretical and there was no humane way to test it in reality, so 90wish turned to one of its supercomputers to perform a series of trials. After three million failures, likely caused by a flaw in the experiment or the Relics’ inability to “respond to such crude methods”, to quote Persicaria’s conclusion. According to Persicaria, despite the failure, one man refused to accept this outcome - William, believed to have rejected the failure, viewing failure as representation of unfulfilled conditions to achieve a Relic activation. She believed that he would go to unspeakable ends, and he has, to attempt the experiment in reality. 

For a biological subject to achieve a Relic activation, their bodies must be attuned to Collapse Radiation; in layman’s terms, they must be partially or fully immune. Since the Beilan Island Incident, only one truly immune individual has been discovered, Kawasaki Kazusa, though there have been instances of partial-immunity, such as the original girl Machlian and Morridow were based on, Machlian herself, and the Commander. Helena in Girls Frontline 2: Exilium seems to be a fully immune subject as well; however, this is yet to be confirmed. To William in the 2060s, the “Nytos” are created for a single, fate-deciding purpose: an immune for application in Relic research, particularly their activation. Those that failed in this test were automatically deemed trash, only serving as Paradeus’ mindless drones, genetic material, or sources of energy to feed the Evangel Axis. Simply put, any Nyto that does not meet the immune criteria is insufficient and considered expendable. At some point before Shattered Connexion, Angelia warned Persicaria of an unknown faction looking to reactivate the Relics, and given the former’s history with Meitner and her thralls, including her intelligence-gathering assignment on KCCO’s collaborative war effort in Chapter 10, Angelia obviously understood what the powers that be were striving towards. The Relics hold limitless potential, with just as much chance for destruction as bringing about a golden age; it all depends on who’s at the helm to open the gates to Nirvana when that day arrives.

As for 90wish and “Professor William”, there’s a considerable overlap between 90wish and Paradeus’ most prominent figures. Sometime between 2051 to approximately 2054, while Lycoris and Persicaria were in the last days in 90wish, “William” approached them out of the blue with a data block and a request. Contained within was digital sequence information, stated to be gathered during the process of digitizing a human brain, specifically Lunasia von Oberstein’s consciousness. “William” requested they extract the data, then create a neural cloud with reformatted segments of neurological structure. Upon closer inspection of the compiled information, Lycoris and Persicaria were shocked upon discovering memories of Lunasia - Rudolf von Oberstein’s daughter, their former 90wish head and director of the Max Planck Institute for Computer Science. After the outbreak of the German Civil War in late 2044, Lycoris and Persicaria were relocated from the Leipzig University of Karl Marx to the Max Planck Institute, directed by Oberstein. 

Often they would find themselves spending long hours in the labs, only for Oberstein’s curious daughter to venture in to visit while her father was busy. Likely caused by his poor reputation with the “Relics Department” - the former UNRA Beaconists, the Prometheans, or the unknown Relic Department described in the MB-13-A document - mixed with his character being under much fire at the time, Oberstein rarely had time to watch over his children, assuming they truly are his blood children. On occasion, Lunasia and Lycoris exchanged stories about family and 90wish, with Lunasia’s complaints about her father always being busy and Lycoris’ exaggerated tales of the research group. Although she was still just a girl, any violation of informational security jeopardized the 90wish’s expressed closed-loop, a system that held its data close to the vest. Even Witkin, who profiled and recruited Lycoris and Persicaria to an IOP shell, found the infosec superb. With the war continuing to intensify in Germany in 2049, much of the Max Planck team and associated individuals relocated from the city (Saarbrücken?), leading to Lunasia and “William” being transferred to the Oberstein Family Manor in Berlin. Witkin believed this movie was Oberstein’s choice to keep his family lying low, possibly in fear of potential repercussions or an attempt on him or his family. 

90wish was only the colloquial name among members and those few aware outsides, however, it’s real name was the Bundeswehr Special Technology Group, seemingly formed in the early 2040s, tasked with R&D for the FRG Bundeswehr. Unsurprisingly, during wartime, its role could’ve made it a military or internal target. This is where the canon can be somewhat messy, as certain parts of the Confidential Files conflict with each other and the main story, so bear with the following and take it with a grain of salt. According to The Art of Girls Frontline Vol. 1, the canonicity of which should be subject to scrutiny, 90wish planned to release research findings pertaining to Doll technologies online but soon disappeared shortly after. When Lycoris escaped Germany in early 2049, he made his way to Izhevsk, where he submitted the dissertation and, later, argued with the MoD over the upgrades to the Soviet automated division, leading to the December 2049 confidential meeting in Moscow. The “Inverted Forest”, a codename for the first neural cloud development project worked on by him and Persicaria in 90wish, was a LVLII simulated space meant to simulate neural clouds, later serving as the base plate for the development of 2nd generation T-Dolls’ neural clouds. Much of this data was based on 90wish’s surveillance data, along with past knowledge gathered over the past decade. An unapproved public release of a classified military R&D department’s data would certainly draw the ire of some members and leaders, so it’s possible that they had prior failed to reach a consensus over the public release, souring internal relations, as described in Confidential Files 1. Regardless, soon after departing the institute, 90wish fell silent, having gone completely dark; however, Persicaria believed they still operate to this day, which Paradeus might be an evolution or an arm of. All public information on the group has been scrubbed, leaving only rumors of an online organization of research behind. Despite departing in 2049, she and Lycoris mustn’t have exited the group entirely, likely shifting to private online channels to work remotely, given “William’s” request to them after 2051, as they were said to be still in the group.

Before Lunasia left the city, Persicaria noticed Oberstein’s consistent anxiety, worrying that the institute might be shut down as a result, however, she wasn’t definitively sure. Before departing, Persicaria, Lycoris, Oberstein, and Lunasia took a picture together, marking the last time they would ever see each other in person. Upon arriving in the manor sometime in the late 2040s, the children were consistently neglected, likely to protect or isolate them from Oberstein’s work in 90wish or Paradeus. During the conscious link established to William’s consciousness in Chapter 13, a memory was discovered, showing the young boy moping, with Lunasia there to comfort him when their parents wouldn’t. When asked when “Daddy”, indicating a very young William, was going to return, he added that they probably didn’t want them anymore, something that Lunasia assured him wasn’t the case. She explained that they were too busy, and she’d be there to keep him company always, as she loved him dearly. The mention of “they” implies both of their parents were alive back then, with who we assume is Nemhran or her original, non-Nyto self as their mother. The family is already a puzzle in itself, however, Nemhran is an enigma of its own tier. Very little is known about her, as it’s not abundantly clear if Nemhran in 2064 is a clone reproduction or her original self having been “Nytofied”, so to speak. 


The Nytos of Avernus pray before the statue of the Goddess (Nike/Athena/Nemesis).

As Fe56 were investigating Avernus, they discovered someone’s lounge, hidden away on the 40th floor of the East Tower. Inside was a noticeably cozy room, furnished with all things normally found in one’s home, along with a miniature statue of an unknown goddess. Interestingly, this may not be a miniature of East Tower Hall’s statue of Nike, Nemesis, or another goddess proudly spreading her wings and drawing her sword towards the heavens, perhaps Athena - personifying the victory of Paradeus’ aspired divine wisdom. On the surface of the Avernus platform, a cargo truck was found beforehand to contain a box of a conspicuous goddess statue holding a white blossom, bearing an enigmatic smile that evoked déjà vu. The statue found in the room, heavily implied to be Nemhran’s, may be neither of these statues, but it’s added proof of Paradeus’ fanaticism, adding fuel to the fire that is Paradeus’ namesake, “Prepare for God/God, you prepare.” The true discovery of that room lay among scattered notes, detailing a series of experiments from a “long time ago”, and a photograph of two individuals, seemingly tied to Lunasia’s fate after 2051.

Returning to the manor in 2051, Lunasia often spent her time in the manor’s garden - a beautifully well-kempt jungle, filled with lush greens and vibrant flowers. Despite the ongoing war and her parents’ neglect, the house brought solace in an otherwise depressive setting. In Shattered Connexion, as M4A1 was led through the Inverted Forest by an Isomer, an intense nostalgia consumed her neural cloud, as if familiarity of the home brought peace, possibly indicating that “William”, Oberstein, or Meitner had designed it as a testbed for consciousness, given that the Forest was originally created in 90wish. Appearing as an upside-down forest, god rays emanating from the canopies across this virtually infinite cyberspace, the system was perceived by M4A1 as a LVLII space. Indeed, as a mind reproduction of Lunasia, she felt the intrinsic link to her origin self echoing across the Forest, and the Isomer leading her was a total anomaly. 


ST-AR15 stands within the Inverted Forest, attempting to return M4A1 to consciousness.

The Inverted Forest seemed to be repurposed between the Isomers, and with M4A1’s comment on a lack of firewalls, boundaries, or presence of a neural cloud, what she may have tapped into was a shared Virtual Cognition Image, serving as the shared basis for the Isomers based on Lunasia’s brainscan. UMP45 theorized the forest wasn’t M4A1’s internal neural cloud, but an external neural cloud space - possibly a VCI or another shared point of consciousness, like Nirvana or the Lake - that’s being processed internally by its connected “users”. The massive virtual space defied logic, and considering the Forest was created in 90wish to simulate neural clouds, it was as if this cyberspace was formed by the Isomers’ connections. By “compiling and visualizing the data” internally, the Forest appeared in the Dolls’ minds as a shared LVLII space, despite not actually being part of their neural clouds. According to STAR15 and Dandelion, the space was a central realm, a “patchwork of memories”, where all the connections intermingled. Coming across one of the Isomers within, M4A1 was led into a simulated version of the Oberstein Manor.

When asked what the manor was, the Isomer simply replied, “This is our new home. Don’t worry, I’ll always take care of you.” As if a segment of Lunasia’s consciousness spoke to M4A1 through her memory fragments present in the Isomers, the line is clearly allegorical of Lunasia introducing William to their new home. In memories told through the Isomer projections, William loved to visit her in the garden, becoming a daily occurrence to keep her company. Interestingly, around this period, Lunasia coughed and complained of her feebleness, and given Persicaria’s testimony that they heard Lunasia passed away from an illness, there may be some truth to her having an infliction before being dragged out of the manor in 2051. Although merely theory, during Poincare Recurrence in 2064, in the false visions projected into Morridow’s VCI by the “M4-Lunasia entity”, one depicted William furiously shouting over his unsuccessful attempts to find or create a full immune individual. When Morridow saw “him”, she begged that she was, in her mind, the perfection he’d been so longing for. Of course, she was a failure at the moment of her creation, as the ultimate goal of all Father William Paradeus Nytos is to create that immune, and any deviation eternally marked them as failures. She didn’t lose to Machlian in her perfection; she never had it in the first place, the blunt truth lost on so many of Paradeus’ slaves. Turning around, William scoffed at this embarrassment of his design, then suddenly, he was filled with astonishment at another figure behind her. Walking through her, he approached the M4-Lunasia entity, taking the form of Lunasia in the mind projection, possibly set in Nirvana. His personality practically regressed when he saw her, then proclaimed in excitement that his dear sister was “the perfect one”, an individual he’d been longing for all this time. William’s total rejection of Morridow shattered her mind, collapsing her VCI soon after. This scene does carry a strong implication: was Lunasia a full immune?

Admittedly, there’s a chance that the entire scene served no other reason but to fracture Morridow’s false perception of Paradeus and her Father, but the deliberate choice of the entity taking Lunasia’s form possibly indicates that she may have been immune. While true that Lunasia is the perfection that William has sought, given that her resurrection is his lifelong wish, maybe that perfection was actually immunity. Evidence for this is circumstantial at best; however, Lunasia reportedly passed away from an illness, according to Persicaria and Lycoris, leading to “William” sending them the data packet years later. Although we know it was far more than just sickness that killed her, she certainly suffered from some sort of illness in her final months or years. In the memory with William, she mentions her weakened body, bearing no mention beforehand, pointing to its development in more recent times. In the later memories from the resonance formed with William’s consciousness, he describes a group of murderous madmen responsible, so it’s also possible they were tied to the development of her illness. If Lunasia was fully immune, then it’s possible that, according to Kazusa’s autopsy, she was undergoing severe autoimmune disease and organ wastage, weakening her body to any infections, outside of a Contaminated Zone. The autopsy reported that the mutations to the subject’s organs completely adapted her to survival in contaminated environments, no longer able to live in purified areas. Perhaps Lunasia’s body was failing due to the lack of Collapse particles; though, there is one considerable caveat to this theory. 

It’s unknown when the Green Zone in Berlin, possibly known as the “Berlin Testing Zone”, was established; however, an Aktuelle Kamera news story reported nearly 1.7 million cases of ELID at the end of the war, possibly meaning that the Yellow Zone was still undergoing purification. After the Northern Lights Incident, the Collapse particle cloud spread southward across central Europe, forming a belt from the Baltic to the Adriatic. The passing of the FRG’s 2044 yearly budget plan through the Bundestag represented a watershed moment in government policy towards overseas development rather than reconstruction of northern and eastern Germany, igniting fervor among the Social Democrats and eastern German citizens, who lived in the widespread Yellow Zone. With the eruption of violence, subsequent civil war, and the outbreak of WWIII, there likely wasn’t enough support and resources to purify all vital regions in the newly-declared new-GDR. Moreover, the latest generation of purification towers were completed in 2055, four years after Lunasia’s death, but any prior purification technologies have never been explored, though they do exist. If the area around Neu-Tempelhof, Berlin was purified to Green Zone levels, then autoimmune disease may have slowly developed. On the other hand, if Neu-Tempelhof remained in the Yellow Zone, then Lunasia must’ve been suffering from something else, carrying its own implications on her death. If autoimmune disease was not responsible, then would it be possible another illness pushed Oberstein to be taken away? These possibilities are not mutually exclusive, as it’s just as possible that Lunasia’s condition necessitated her extraction, possibly to Avernus, leading to her possibly becoming a Hela subject.

Who is “William”?

William, Nemhran, and a hologram of Lunasia von Oberstein dining together in Avernus.

Returning once more William met Lunasia in the garden, the latter was happy to see him but told him not to worry, adding that he still has “own research” and he should focus on what he wanted to do while they wait out “the storm” for their father to bring them back. Like M4A1, the AR Team, and Elisa, the Isomers also share the blueprint memory fragments of Lunasia, and the manor generated in the Forest is a digital reconstruction of these memories, suggesting that William or the other Paradeus higher-ups used it as a base layer for these Lunasia and OGAS-derived consciousnesses. Although their ages are never outright stated, we know Lunasia was still relatively young when visiting Lycoris and Persicaria in Max Planck, and after arriving in the manor sometime in the late 2040s, her younger brother was still speaking in manners clearly reminiscent of a young child. When William’s true voice is revealed in Fixed Point, Angelia was seriously caught off guard by his adolescent voice, so young in fact that it was as if he was still a teenage boy. Later, as the Wolf Pack were detaining William during Operation Ilya Muromets, his youthful, yet mature manner was patently obvious. Herein lies the crucial issue of Oberstein’s children. Their ages are indeterminate, but William’s adolescence in 2064 riddles the events of the 2050s with questions. For a visual aid, here’s a basic chart comparing his approximate age to his match birth year.

15	2049 (Likely too young)
16	2048 (Possibly too young)

In the memory depicting Lunasia in the garden, not too long after arriving in the manor, the brother’s tone was that of a young boy, even still using childlike terms, such as “Daddy”, to refer to their father. As a young child with a basic understanding of language and grammar, enough so to have a conversation with his sister, he seemingly was of late-preschooler to early elementary age. By 2064, the voice of teenage years rings out, so he likely was born sometime between 2043 to 2048, aligning with the development of his teenage voice into the 2060s. Aside from just concealing his identity, the electronic voice modulator that he’d used for so many years was a ploy to throw off anyone from ever expecting the current mastermind of Paradeus to be “practically a child.” A simple, ingenious solution for sure, but his age is not just surprising; it’s an anomaly that violates the understanding of Paradeus in the 2050s.

While escorting Persicaria to a safehouse in Chapter 13, Witkin probed Persicaria for the truth behind Lunasia and the creation of the AR Team, leading to her admission that a 90wish researcher named “William” approached her and Lycoris after Lunasia’s death. It’s unclear exactly when “Professor William” delivered the data packet and message to them, but Lunasia died shortly before the end of WWIII, and the pair continued working remotely in 90wish for a couple of years afterward. Even at his absolute earliest possible birth year, Lunasia’s brother would’ve only been around ten years old by the early 2050s, far someone who’d be a brilliant professor that outshined most of 90wish. This isn’t to say the brother isn’t a prodigy, as evidenced by his superb expertise in biology and cybernetics, but to become an expert among experts at such a young age is anomalous at best - outright paranormal at worst. 

After Lunasia’s data block was delivered, the pair realized what “William” was planning to do. By reconfiguring her memory fragments into a neural cloud segmented in a neurological structure, they’d be effectively digitally resurrecting Lunasia’s consciousness. Back then, Lycoris’ conservative nature strongly opposed the request, viewing it as an overt violation of ethical principles, and Persicaria, although interested, agreed to not complete the request. Her intrigue would later be her achilles heel in 2057. Initially, Witkin, Lycoris, and Persicaria all suspected that “William” was Rudolf von Oberstein acting under a pseudonym, pushing for the resurrection of his daughter after what they believed was a deadly illness; however, we know now this was far from the truth. Back then, Persicaria discounted Oberstein’s involvement, based on his firm conviction against this research field. She believed that his stance was incorrigible, even in wake of Lunasia’s passing, but this is not entirely true. Even if we assume the younger brother was born in 2045, as an expressed adolescent with a voice to match his current age, that still wouldn’t make him any older than 9 years old by 2054, depending on his birthday. 

How could a child manage to be one of 90wish’s finest, and by further, how would he alone access Lunasia’s body, digitize her brain through unknown means, compile it into the data block, then only for it to be sent to Lycoris and Persicaria so they could develop a brain-structured neural cloud based on it?
