Ramzan nudged at Anna that she was incapable of making that shot, shifting guilt to their sibling rivalry, only for Anna to claim she unload several of the toy bullets from Ramzan’s gun just before they set out, which erupted in a common brawl between the siblings that hadn’t always seen eye to eye until big brother Armin intervened. Ganglati’s neuro-stabilizer was faulty to begin with, and Angelia’s incessant pleas for Ramzan’s memory triggered a continuous regression to the memories from the Lake or from his original body, depending on the preconditions of his modifications. Now entirely at the whims of a mentally unstable test subject, Angelia had no choice but to jab further, for there was no other option than death. Gasping out his name and rank, as well as their mutual story fighting together until his end, Ramzan desperately proclaimed himself as Ganglati, seemingly recalling Meitner’s face, his “Teacher”, from the 2051 encounter or his subsequent capture while denouncing “that other” name, losing the vice on Angelia’s throat as truth seeped from the cracks. Mourning Sana, he stopped himself midway, questioning if Anna was the correct name, bursting the dam of repressed memories.

From their first meeting in the snow in front of the Ibrahimov cabin - Ramzan grumbly refusing his newly-adoptive younger sister - to comforting each other before the dried puddle of Armin’s blood, who was given a virtually painless death compared to some; the once-rejected sister finally left the nest, yet as man of morals - ingrained into him by their father, upheld by his sons to defend family - he couldn’t readily accept her leaving his wing, making the ultimate sacrifice in 2051. No servant of Hell understood such bravery, loyalty, and compassion, as his soul’s honor towered all; even the worst of the demon’s tricks proved futile when his family’s lives were threatened. With an electric pain searing across his temple, Ramzan dropped Angelia, finally returning a familiar grin, the same worn when averting Anna’s guilt for the bird, when the Wolf Pack broke through to the rooftop, opening fire on “Ganglati”. Retreating to the edge, he accepted his final “job as an elder brother”, readying to jump himself for her protection. Realizing that his false recollections altered his psyche, the ironic truth became evident: Ganglati was all fabrication, never having truly “clawed my way from Abaddon back into the world of living”, his soul lingering in limbo. Holding out a hand like he did at her graduation prom in early 2051, Ramzan assured her he’d be waiting on the other side, and Angelia affirmed he wouldn’t have too long. Leaning into true, final death, a gust of wind thrust him over the edge with bloodsoaked hands and tearful eyes between them.

AN94 rushed towards her mangled Commander, launching right into emergency medical treatment to stop the gushing blood from her right leg, and once the bleeding was effectively contained for the time being, still requiring professional aid, AN94 threw Angelia over her shoulder. Leaning over AN94’s back, she contacted AK12, telling her to rig the building for demolition for their exit, as of that night, there was to be no more Ramzan or Anna, for once the foundations crumbled, the old embers would be extinguished, then reforged into the arisen phoenix of Angelia and DEFY. The release of death had already been stolen once from Ramzan, and upon his deliverance from the rooftop edge, the specter of Angelia’s past was finally laid to rest, seemingly. It cannot be said if Ramzan truly died, but there’s been no sign of his return, though Fe56 had discovered his neural stability pod in Avernus; however, this was likely before the final encounter. Moreover, if Ramzan was indeed a “Nyto Consciousness” and not a ELID Specimen “monster”, perhaps his memories were never transferred, but isolated into Ganglati’s shell, meaning his true death after jumping; on the other hand, if Ganglati was just a clone of Ramzan, implanted with his memories, then his consciousness may have lived on, but the rudimentary, crude nature of his construction and faulty mind suggest otherwise. Theoretically in certain scenarios, Ramzan could return in some capacity; however, granting him a final goodbye may be for the best of Angelia and the story - a watershed moment in Angelia’s life, wherein her spirit emerged from behind the bomb case in Beslan, renewed as the familiar, incorrigible risk-taker Meitner had surmised she’d become. As the trio exited, AK12 made a final request before Angelia hit the detonator, requesting if they could rename the drab “Wolf Pack” title to something less reminiscent of either Shaw or, more likely, AK15, a fissure still between them since Incident Zero. Feeling the detonator, Angelia suggested the name “DEFY”, likely from Shaw’s perspective on the freedom of Dolls, who must break the shackles bound to them, demonstrating agency through conscious action. In the same vein, Angelia declared they’d walk the rest of their tumultuous lives on the “path of darkness”, leaving light behind in defiance of the “dogmas of the world and do as we please” in a tireless journey towards the root of this tragedy - never acceding failure, never falling to temptation, never kneeling to a supreme authority that ruled by a sword against the world’s nape. With the press of a button, both lives came crumbling down with the building, with “Angelia” surging from the ashes like a phoenix.

An Old Friend Ablaze
If Meitner truly survived, Angelia would finish what Anna could not, though her acquiescence regarding her until Slow Shock is questionable, but the dossier in Avernus may incriminate the Prometheans with antecedent knowledge, possibly seeking her guidance on the formation of the Rossartrist Union. Ending this memory section, two speakers - only identified by the pseudonyms used by Blackwell and Meitner, Abaddon on Laplace’s Demon - share a short exchange on a gift from one to the other; although sender is left ambiguous, leaving us guessing whom, the sender probably was Meitner, assuming each line break represents each party’s message. If so, Meitner had delivered something to Blackwell in the past, enough to ignite fury in the dignified Blackwell, with Meitner awaiting to meet her in Hell, followed by Blackwell declaring she’d erase her senior herself, “in my own way.” There’s initial suspicion that “Blackwell” was played by Angelia, promising to deliver vengeance for the “gift”, possibly Ramzan; however, given the speaker is referred to as Abaddon, with Angelia unaware of the original Blackwell’s existence before Slow Shock, this cannot be the case, barring some twist of Lake. On the other side, Meitner could’ve covertly transferred her former friend an invitation into Paradeus-Galatea for a Hela Project surgeon position, as this short exchange is followed by Blackwell’s last known letter, written in Berlin in 2058, wherein she adamantly rejected what’s presumed to be an offer into a Galatea position, asking if they could once again meet in the Million Roses Record Shop in Bremen. The mirage played by the influences of the Lake, RPK16, and Meitner obfuscate later events after Operation Couatl, but Blackwell’s strong objection to the project offer squarely landed her in the sights of information isolation, alluded to in Nemhran’s recording on Galatea’s recruitment program, mentioning Gray Blackwell’s inflexibility during earlier persuasion attempts. 

Having refused to join the Hela Project, rejecting all persuasion, and the sole rogue source of evidence against Meitner, and possibly Oberstein, Nemhran recommended “switching to Plan B and dealing with her before her influence grows”. While it may not be the Galatea subsidiary it is today, Blackwell left to found a biology laboratory in Berlin, presumably the Gray Institute of Biotechnology, co-opted by Nyto Gray and Paradeus upon her presumed assassination and its absorption into Galatea, feasibly in 2058. Submitting her request to a superior - seemingly not “Father”, then probably Oberstein, referring to him separately to the request regarding the Galatea recruitment program - the individual received and promptly denied permission, setting the Blackwell issue aside for the time being “until further instructions are given”. Aside from William, who may not have even been in a position of influence yet in Avernus, only “the Professor” feasibly out-ranked Nemhran, deferring the issue until she accepted the obligatory kill order. Nevertheless, Blackwell’s death must’ve occurred soon after the 2058 letters; a memory within Gray or plot flashback illustrated Blackwell’s apprehension towards Galatea, firmly rooted in the belief that, regardless of how many persuasion attempts were tried against her, “my answer will always be the same”, strictly adhering to the Hippocratic Oath over “one person’s selfish interest” - like Oberstein offering his daughter as the sacrificial lamb; like Sana’s resurrection becoming an outlet of Meitner’s insatiable research ambitions; and like William’s lifelong pursuit: the resurrection of his sister and vengeance against the madmen who exploited her - pursuits built upon selfish foundations, antithetical to all Blackwell stood for.

Chapter 6 - Burnt All Paths I Found (Agent Angelia)

(Autumn 2064)

The browning of leaves hallmarks autumn, with chills in the air to remind of the cold days ahead; by late 2064, the tumultuous waves reverberated across society, from the slums of dejected districts to the towering skylines of the White Zones. In the West, the seeds of a new order were soon to sprout; in the East, distrust among the old guard was metastasizing, expanding greatly after General Carter was stripped of his rank; and the powers-that-be had their eyes squarely fixed on the enactment of the Alliance of the United Nations Plan, pulling strings from places unseen for the establishment of the Union of Rossartrism Nations Coalition. Once more on the curtain’s influential end, the German Democratic Republic’s position was pivotal, stirring an all-consuming whirlwind. Behind the masquerade of instability, Paradeus and the ultranationalists were fanning the blaze from Bremen to Moscow, soon to escalate into an inferno, all while the world-enveloping foundation was poured; “everyone is eager to pick their own share of fruit from the large orchard”, said narrator, for the technologies gleaned from William’s laboratory and the observations of the Reverse Collapse phenomena were the golden goose of power, especially to those who sought to eclipse the old world order.

The German Connection

Convenient Errors for a Bargaining Chip
Catching wind of “William’s” connection to Germany, Angelia and DEFY were mobilized around early to mid September 2064 as foreign investigators, following the steps of the path last paved in Paldiski. In a nameless bar in St. Petersburg, an unassuming woman ordered a drink for one of the regular drunkards, said to be a Berlin Mary by the bartender, though as a supposed avid Berlin Mary connoisseur, he promptly smacked the glass away while storming off. Walking up to the aggrieved bartender, the unnamed woman confirmed she’d paid the drunkard’s tab, insinuating they may have known each other or the woman was an intelligence agent in the wider picture. In Paradeus’ Moscow listening post, Nemhran and her subordinates - initially tasked with interfering with the Soviet MoD’s hub systems for the coming Fireworks Incident, aiming to confuse command and control across the Western Military District - reviewed Angelia’s file for anything on her time within the submarine base, then compiled it info a plaintext file, either sending it to the “Chief or to Aver-”; mentioning the latter mandated subordinate Sussana’s immediate execution, while the identity of the Chief is left unsaid. The ramblings of Bremen versus Berlin Mary must’ve been a set of code phrases, passed along StateSec’s intelligence circles by a mole, presumably by Colonel Dupieux of StateSec’s First and Second Main Directorates. As a fellow Paradeus counterintelligence asset within the bureau, under the codename “Polar Bear”, Dupieux was officially assigned with monitoring the St. Petersburg Military Sector HQ after the Fireworks Incident in October, while truthfully working alongside the “Evangelist” - Nemhran’s codename - to cripple the Soviet MoD and StateSec from effectively responding to the blossoming crisis on the European border. In the bar in St. Petersburg, perhaps the drunkard’s intense reaction to the offered Mary was an imperceptible signal to another agent within. After the Fireworks Incident in October 2064, at least three operatives under Dupieux were revealed to be culprits of the disruptions against the MoD, suggesting “Polar Bear” was responsible for the information on Angelia’s deployment earlier in September 2064. Something went awry in the transferral of the files, regarding her and the equipment discovered in OKB-167, to Witkin and StateSec’s intelligence network - possibly the Promethean intelligence network, likely encompassing the Promethean investigation from Lyons’ WAVE Technology, Zelinsky’s faction of StateSec, and the Riefenstahl supported, Rossartrist-affiliated faction of the Stasi - through Dupieux or one of his assets, leading her to Bremen rather than Berlin, the public core of Paradeus’ influence.

As for the unnamed “Chief”, this codename isn’t used among anyone in Paradeus or its affiliates - composed of Laplace, Father, Evangelist, and Polar Bear - and the only known individual holding that position in Zelinsky; however, even his questionable positions would not justify deploying his canaries on an foreign intelligence operation without firm basis, and although Angelia’s initial operation was sanctioned by StateSec, the conspicuous source and veracity of the intelligence that led her to Germany could’ve been subject to a man-in-the-middle attack. As for whoever else “Chief” could be, the only other possible candidate would be Morridow, Paradeus’ overseer of Bremen and Berlin, possibly meant to receive Angelia’s file before she arrived in-country; alternatively “Chief” could’ve been the former director of the Stasi, suspected of Paradeus affiliation and was removed after the Oberstein Manor incident, replaced by the Rossartrist-faction Romy Riefenstahl. After Angelia landed in Bremen in September, it was Chairwoman Gilda Ulrich, having a residence within the city, who green-lit her entry - an action that drew respect and ire alike from country’s internal factions, as even the Mayor of Bremen approached her with a thinly-veiled message regarding “her” entry. Turning the ire against the mayor, she questioned who actually sent him to persuade her, even demanding to be turned over to the Stasi for sedition if they suspected her, something she was obviously innocent of. Internal conflict within the Stasi surely was related to the suspicious circumstances of the unnamed Stasi director’s removal, but left in a bubble was the Vice-Chief of the Stasi, Erich Meyer - likely nameplay on the real life Stasi director Erich Mielke during the Cold War - who assigned Ulrich the task of accepting and meeting with Angelia in the city. Nothing is known about Meyer outside the single interaction between Ulrich and the mayor, so his loyalties cannot be established yet; however, it’s equally possible for Meyer to be innocently working in tandem with Soviet StateSec as it is for Meyer to be a Paradeus-affiliate, given orders to send Ulrich as the public, friendly face once Angelia entered Bremen. Resulting from the counterintelligence failure in summer 2064, she’d been sent to the wrong city, yet the situation was easily salvageable as long as her path were railroaded, with Morridow traveling to Bremen to “receive our gift”. Nothing outright incriminates Meyer as a Paradeus affiliate, but the internal strife of the Stasi - its cooperation with the Paradeus-Galatea facilities, along with the former director’s later removal - certainly levels skepticism against his character, though he may just be caught in crossfire, only used by Paradeus counterintelligence to guide Angelia in the direction they wished via Ulrich.

Another tenuous potential suspect - theoretically, not mutually exclusive to Meyer - of Paradeus counterintelligence against Angelia’s mission is Vice-Chief Sasha Jarvis of StateSec, CPSU member, PIC and Liaison of the Wolf Pack Project, and Shaw’s superior. Appearing only once in the entire story - AN94’s MOD Story, Chapter 1 - Jarvis is presumably one of the highest-ranking officials in StateSec, likely governing one of the Main Chief Directorates, answering directly to Bureau Chief Zelinsky. Visiting Shaw’s office sometime after AN94 - the Wolf Pack “prototype” - was completed, Shaw’s laboratory AI, Nadezhda, confirmed his security clearance; intending to pass Zelinsky’s personal good word on AN94’s stellar training results against IOP test opponents, indicating satisfactory progress for the project. Accidently walking in on her simulated chess game, he became a living chess piece for her trial game, presumably against Sir Lyons - a friend of Zelinsky and Shaw’s, as well as a prominent backer of the project. There’s nothing linking Vice-Chief Jarvis to Paradeus - or indeed, any faction, for that matter - however, Shaw disappeared from StateSec soon after the Wolf Pack Project was completed with RPK16’s release, while Jarvis is the only other individual with a “Chief” position. There’s discussion to be had on his possible involvement in Shaw’s disappearance, or potential Paradeus replacement or influence over him, but with so little on his character, all speculation is far too tenuous. Currently, Vice-Chief Erich Meyer and Vice-Chief Sasha Jarvis are the primary suspects, as William has always been referred to as “Father”; Oberstein wouldn’t have anything to do with Angelia’s mission; Riefenstahl wasn’t in power yet, and she’s among the Rossartrist faction; Zelinsky and the Prometheans may have ordered Angelia and DEFY to Germany, yet even their information on Paradeus was limited, subjected to man-in-the-middle attacks by Paradeus counterintelligence; and Misha’s detestment of the unethical use of Relic technologies absolves him from suspicion, though his radio silence towards Angelia could’ve been related to the Prometheans’ operations, suspected of possibly using her as a bargaining chip to speak with “William” and Meitner.

Faded Memory on a Dusty Shelf (September 2064)
Much of the events depicted in the Agent Angelia sections covers the events of Dual Randomness and Mirror Stage, so for brevity, these setting and pacing of these sections won’t be as thoroughly explored; however, following the trend of the past three life sections, portions of these memories have been altered to varying degrees, switching certain characters in specific locations, enough to be perceptibly incorrect.

Twelve hours before landing out the Bremen city barrier, an message was discreetly forwarded to Angelia by an individual under the pseudonym “Samosina”, affirming the “the white ‘sparrow’ you are looking for is by Ulrich’s side”, referencing Morridow’s infiltration of the Bremen government and Ulrich’s personal circle. It’s unclear if this message is a twist of the Lake, as she realized later Morridow was the plant at Ulrich’s side, yet this conflicts with the official narrative, given once Morridow’s cover was blown on on the JU-094 helicopter, Angelia questioned if Morridow was even a Nyto, though this could easily be handwaved by the simple fact that Morridow was the first truly human-like Nyto encountered, perhaps distrustful of Samosina’s warning; however, this isn’t to say she or StateSec held suspicions of a Paradeus mole within the German government, as a lead on the “sparrow” - also referred to as a “swallow”, traditionally a spycraft term for a female asset who engages in honey pot coercion by means of seduction, though this doesn’t accurately reflect Morridow’s role - could’ve emerged from a StateSec and Promethean investigation into Paradeus. Before proceeding to meet with Ulrich - planned by the Prometheans to be the friendly, familiar face to facilitate discussion with on the German situation - Samosina assured her that she should meet with them before anyone else; given the reach of Paradeus’ influence, it wouldn’t come as much of a surprise if Samosina wanted to warn her in what’s essentially a sensitive compartmented information facility (SCIF), in places unseen. After all, a number of Stasi agents, likely from the Paradeus-affiliate faction, were tailing Angelia outside the city in DR, only to be knocked out by Angelia, RPK16, and AN94, so any inkling would prove invaluable at this stage. Another confliction stems from Angelia’s knowledge about Ulrich in the first place, as in DR, Ulrich - under aforementioned Promethean directive - had sent Schwaben and “Voigt” to receive Angelia, the latter of which was entirely unaware of Ulrich’s involvement in the affair until then, unlike in the Lake, wherein Angelia had implicitly been sent to rendezvous with her, perhaps blending the early events in Bremen together.

Chosen by the unknown messenger, the Million Roses Record Shop in the Bremen Old Town - the very same meeting place between Meitner and Blackwell in early 2050s - was designated as their meeting place. Taking a detour before linking up with AK12 and AK15, the trio arrived outside the dilapidated shop, located along a sparsely-populated, run-down sidestreet, and for informational security, Angelia entered alone to speak with Samosina one-on-one, keeping her Dolls outside in case of emergency. Walking in, the dingy interior was sore on the eyes - suffocatingly dusty and dead-quiet, save for the old shopkeeper at the counter, uninterested in Angelia - rather unusual for someone whose business was likely insecure, unless it was used as common grounds for criminals or agents - chosen as a conducive, unassuming location to conduct their public affairs - just as “Samosina” was planning for her. Strolling past the shelves of records, one standout caught her eye, just out of sight of the shopkeeper. Interestingly, while considerably yellowed, the record was the same as the shop: “Million Roses”, by Alla Pugacheva; curious about the coincidence, she opened the album, finding the record in pristine condition, along with a note written by marvelous hands on the internal leaf, directed at whomever discovered the note a century later. From Meitner’s letter to Blackwell in 2058, there’s a rare glimpse into the last months of the friendship, finding solace in the old record shop in Bremen to relax and catch up, just as they’d done over sandwiches in Johns Hopkins years before. Given they must’ve come here several times, perhaps either of them were the author, lamenting the sorrowful state of the world from natural disaster, war, pollution, and radiation contamination, while envying those of the 22nd century, enthusiastically idealistic that practical solutions to these catastrophes had been solved, promoting unity and prosperity for all of mankind. The branching “realists” and “idealists” of Rossartrist ideology ultimately share the same objective, though the means differ greatly, as those among Lyons’ circle firmly recognize the impossibility of humanity’s complete unity in the new world, thus requiring checks-and-balances on world order; meanwhile, the idealists, as unattainable as their dream may seem to some, recognize the intrinsic good within us, and even if few can accept this dream with open arms, their ambitions continue burning, adherent to what’s morally right, refusing temptation, no matter the personal cost of one’s life - that is the fundamental dream of a harmonious world, upheld not by the arbitrary laws of those that rule as gods, but the principles ingrained in each man for another.

Just as she closed the album, the shop’s door swung open, in walking Agent Q, casual as any patron. Silently contacting Angelia via communicator, “Samosina” identified herself here as Agent Q, who contacting Angelia independently from either of her bosses in Lubyanka or Haus 1, forcing Angelia to immediately question where her loyalties truly lie. Having read Angelia’s file in Lubyanka, discovering her coming investigation into Paradeus, Q anonymously contacted Angelia before reaching Bremen to speak with her allegedly as an independent intelligence aide, briefing Angelia on the situation within the Stasi and the state outside their surveillance. When asked which side she was investigating Paradeus for, Q acknowledged their positions were congruent, holding vested interests for differing reasons. Before continuing, Angelia forked the bill for several snacks and drinks, a minor request from Q if Angelia was truly interested in what she had to say; once satisfied with the day’s load, paid for by her mutual acquaintance, Q proceeded with the meat and potatoes of the Stasi’s infighting. Sometime in the new Stasi’s service, there was an incident, colloquially referred to as the “Sunspot Incident”, which tanked the Stasi’s reputation, while stunting its “intelligence work on the Neo-Soviet Union back by 20 years”, embroiling into a major controversy between the GDR and NUSSR.

Next to nothing is known about the incident aside from vague references from Agent Q, Kevin “Agent J”, and Kain Schwaben “Agent K”; regardless, Sunspot must’ve remained a sore point between the ally states, souring trust within certain circles. Amid private discussion on the recently-promoted director Riefenstahl, Kevin and Schwaben reviewed strategies for dealing with the string of killings of their fellow agents by Paradeus - and tangentially, Oberstein himself; contrasting their rapidly-changing past directors, Schwaben commended Riefenstahl’s admirable, workhorse directorship, commenting just how many times they’ve changed bosses ever since the “that incident”. Whatever the Sunspot Incident was - perhaps a foreign intelligence operation by the Stasi on the NUSSR, eventually foiled by StateSec or another organization - its impact echoes today, reverberating previous Stasi directors out of their position, lowering the Stasi’s influence and image as no better than just cops of higher caliber. Theoretically, the Sunspot Incident could’ve the Weihnachtsmärkt Incident in 2052, wherein a conflict on the German-Soviet border - unclear if this is was the former FRG or the GDR - turned violent; however, with diplomat Gilda Ulrich’s intervention, bloodshed between citizens, presumably German, and Soviet troops was averted. Isomer was the only point this incident has ever been mentioned, leaving zero details or specifics beyond Lewis’ description of Ulrich’s file to Kalina and the Commander. Considering the conflict nearly escalated into bloodshed between presumed German citizens and Soviet troops, it’s theoretically emblematic of distrust, especially if the Stasi were directly implicated in the incident.

Isolation and Absolvement (October 2064)
Ambitiously seeking to reform the Stasi’s image, Q’s boss, presumably the then-yet-to-be-promoted Romy Riefenstahl, was a workaholic above the rest, keen on details to avoid any pitfalls. Evidenced by Q’s display of the “Bee Sting” real-time surveillance system, all-pervasive across all of which it connects, Riefenstahl had managed to either tap into Paradeus’ network from the Ministry of Defense’s previous cooperations with Paradeus. Likely resulting from Oberstein’s offer to introduce Galatea’s technology to Minister of Defense Schweinsteiger, two government-owned factories were established near Berlin as black-sites, overseen by “paramilitary” units with Paradeus technology, as they were unofficially under the command of the MoD and the Stasi; likewise, Anna and Ramzan encountered an English-speaking enemy force in 2051, presumed to be Paradeus’ earliest paramilitary forces before being phased out by the standard automated and Nyto units. If Paradeus was founded as a secret arm of Galatea or the former Photon Project, then black project state funding was almost surely funneled into Avernus and the confidential organization as a whole; indeed as it were, 90wish itself was originally an FRG Bundeswehr military R&D black project group, unofficially receiving state and Oberstein backing. All of this is to say, however, that Riefenstahl and Schweinsteiger were readily aware of Paradeus’ influence in the German government, even using their technology, including the Bee Sting System and their own production lines, for the Stasi and MoD, all of which were likely agreed upon by Oberstein, who offered the trap-laden deal in the first place. After evidence of arms trafficking and Oberstein’s audio log were recovered in PR, it would only be a matter of time until the fallout impacted Riefenstahl and Schweinsteiger, so the latter tasked the former with dismantling any and all links between the German government and Paradeus: window dressing for the media and public once information started leaking. Galatea was embroiled in controversy after Idunn’s countless falsified trial data was revealed, worsened by a string of disappearance and suicides of core project members, as well as fraudulent financial data submitted to the Ministry of Finance. Riefenstahl surmised that the Stasi were attacked at the MoD-Paradeus plant as an ace against the MoD’s public face, as once the story of several Stasi agents dying in a government black site, involved in the manufacturing of illegal Paradeus-Galatea technologies, hit the media, the lid on the government’s allegiances would be blown wide open, overturning the MoD - and possibly, all of Germany, amid a critical moment of geopolitics, as the Union of Rossartrism is soon to come to fruition.

Although not necessarily related to the Stasi, RPK16 led Kevin and his team into the MoD-Paradeus plant under false intel that Angelia could’ve been in the facility; at surface level, this appears as if RPK16 is leading to the Stasi investigators to their deaths, which fairly she had, yet considering Riefenstahl’s assertion that the plant attack was a ploy by Paradeus to rein in the government - in turn, razing the MoD and Stasi’s remaining reputation - it begs to ask if RPK16 was actually under Lyons’ orders, deeply undercover in Paradeus as his dangle. Entirely theoretical, it’s still a bloody gambit, but an effective one: send in an asset into Paradeus; with information on German government-involvement in Paradeus arms trafficking, use your asset as bait for your agents to discover additional information on Paradeus’ infiltration of Germany, inversely triggering your German Rossartrist allies to rid themselves of evidence of guilt; from there, your hands are entirely clean from this multi-dimensional chess game, cornering your enemies and freeing your allies from pushback. If Oberstein were responsible for the gambit at the plant, it would surely rebound on his character eventually, especially if Schweinsteiger talked; not to mention, intentionally disrupting all your classified facilities for no personal gain, let alone Oberstein’s interest in keeping Schweinsteiger on his leash, would be completely antithetical to Oberstein’s objective of a resolute, anti-Rossartrist state, unless he wished to discredit Riefenstahl and Schweinsteiger if they broke away, shifting the blame of the Paradeus cooperation squarely on them, which still would’ve returned to sender eventually. With William in Lyons’ sight, perhaps the order was given by him, simultaneously appeasing both sides by indirectly “gifting” the damning evidence to the Prometheans through RPK16 the informant, while allowing the Rossartrist sympathizers in government to seize the opportunity to erase and window-dress their connections. This is seriously speculative, easily being handwoven as nothing, yet Paradeus and RPK16 hadn’t brought Kevin’s team there for no reason; they were convinced by a probable Promethean dangle to investigate the MoD’s underbelly, forcing the hands of Schweinsteiger and Riefenstahl to act, thus pulling the duo closer to the Rossartrist-aligned side for their complacency, while personally absolving them of wrongdoing.

In addition to severing Paradeus’ tendrils in the MoD, Riefenstahl deployed Agent Q and several others after the Fireworks Incident to the Neo-Soviet Union to continue the Stasi’s cleanup work, surveilling and reporting on Paradeus’ foreign facilities, wherein she confirmed that upon the Fireworks’ completion, Paradeus’ forces were recalled to wherever their base was. The arms transfer to Carter’s ultranationalist forces - namely, unbeknownst to the Stasi, the Boxes of Iaso - was highlighted by Q, allegedly routing around the German Ministry of Construction, directed by Minister Oberstein, to traffick weapons and equipment to them. Once StateSec First Main Directorate Colonel Dupieux’s cover was blown, brought about by StateSec and Zelinsky suspecting he and his subordinates were in some way involved in the Fireworks Incident, he promptly make his exit, feigning loyalist surveillance when making a break for the German-Soviet border, rather than board the “scheduled” flight from St. Petersburg to Moscow for his “promotion” to Vice-Chairman of the Committee’s Bureau. Contacting Nemhran - codename “Evanglist”, likely a reference to her role as a “mother” or “preacher” to those created with the Evangel Axis - Dupieux requested immediate repatriation assistance, preferably outside of loyalist or Stasi awareness. The aforementioned potential Promethean acknowledgement of Avernus’ existence is of immense importance here, as right after Witkin’s intelligence network discovered the mention of an “Avernus” from the Paradeus mole network in Moscow, Riefenstahl theorized with Schwaben that the Dead Sea could’ve been the headquarters of Paradeus, with their conversation following Nemhran’s retreat from Moscow, with M16A1 under orders to follow her trail, while Witkin reported the name of the facility from their last purge of the intelligence apparatus.


Agent Q of the Stasi aiming her rifle at Colonel Dupieux, codenamed “Polar Bear”

Several hours after returning to his St. Petersburg apartment, Dupieux managed to slip surveillance, presumably with Nemhran’s aid, arriving in a frigid cabin safehouse at the German-Soviet border, possibly situated somewhere between north of Prague and Kraków. While warming up, an unusual noise caught his attention, firing several rounds from his handgun at the door, revealing nothing but fading daylight through the fresh holes. Now positioned in the center of the room, a clear sight through any door or window, his communicator burst to life with an unknown female voice, questioning the identity of “Evangelist” and his role in Paradeus, before sending an electro-shock round into his chest, blacking-out on the spot. With “Polar Bear” incapacitated, Q thought to herself how things would’ve been different had he been captured, commenting all her effort would be for naught, while staking out for Evangelist appearance. It should be noted Q is entirely oblivious to Evangelist’s identity, and she’d been assigned with trimming Paradeus’ agents overseas Had Dupieux been captured by the Soviets, however, Riefenstahl and Schweinsteiger’s plot could’ve been put into momentary jeopardy, as if he talked, there was a significant chance Soviet StateSec would extract information on the German government’s unacknowledged programs and facilities, significantly worsening relations between the two states; moreover, the revelations unveiled would’ve seriously hampered Germany’s position regarding the foundation of the Union of Rossartrism, potentially boiling tensions over in Frankfurt and the Bundestag. Essentially, if the duo failed to isolate themselves and their respective organizations from the evidence poised against Oberstein, they too would reap the whirlwind. Quoting Schweinsteiger, if Oberstein fails to accept the circumstances, forcing his hands against the Rossartrists, “then we shall spare his dignity for him”, perhaps alluding to the Stasi’s later simulations in E&S on his potential assassination by Amaris; if all Oberstein can contribute is violent rebellions, provocateurs, and hitmen, his opponents will indignantly respond in kind.

Millions Eyes of Providence (September 2064)
Serving her masters in Berlin and Moscow, Q’s supposed true loyalty upholds Riefenstahl’s bid for directorship, with the unnamed prior director still in their position at the time; furthermore, this individual, possibly a former ally of Oberstein, likely approved and oversaw the establishment of the two Paradeus/Galatea-MoD production factories on the outskirts of Berlin, though in the same vein, the director could’ve actually been “innocent”, so to speak, with Riefenstahl responsible for the initial cooperation. In Riefenstahl’s bid, Q testified her boss achieved her aims with the aid of a cutting-edge, real-time surveillance system, allowing for instantaneous analysis, organization, and dissemination of those its eye pierces; this eye, however, was not created by Riefenstahl, but Paradeus, managed from Avernus in the Dead Sea, unbeknownst to them. The all-pervasive eye supposedly motivated Q to leak the message through StateSec to Angelia before departing to Germany, as Q herself was playing double agent in Lubyanka, realizing the context of Angelia’s intelligence and upcoming deployment; Q put it best, straightforwardly describing its reach: “Anything remote, they’ll see”, for it’s impossible to bypass the surveillance once stung, forcing Q to meet with Angelia directly in an unknown, lowly record shop on a random sidestreet.

Listening to Q’s warning, Angelia was hesitant to involve herself in the Stasi’s infighting and reshuffling; even in Lyons’ anonymous message to her in Mirror Stage, he apologized for his forced intrusion into her predicament, insinuating that he was responsible for her and DEFY’s sudden release from the Stasi HQ after two days of confinement following their transfer from Bremen to Berlin, brought about by the “bad decisions the Stasi has made due to internal strife”. Angelia innately understood that Ulrich couldn’t have been responsible for their out-of-the-blue release, given the influence necessary to broker a prisoner release, breaking up Stasi infighting between the Paradeus-affiliates and loyalists, exceeded Ulrich’s reach. She may be an admired politician and pretty face for the masses, but she held no domain over the inner workings of the Stasi, let alone the capacity to intervene. Considering Riefenstahl falls squarely into the Rossartrist faction, perhaps even a blade of the Council, it’s possible the unnamed female official that extracted Angelia and DEFY from the interrogation rooms was her, as she freed them and assigned temporary housing in a nearby apartment building, with Lyons’ signing his email through RPK16 with a hope of gratitude for the apartment, implying he directly intervened in their release; moreover, while Schwaben and Light were investigating the Weser River outside Bremen for any signs of Morridow or Paradeus, someone of tremendous influence bypassed Ulrich’s authority to issue commands for the relocation of Kevin and Light to Berlin in the coming days, with a new assignment of monitoring and working with Angelia following her release - Griffin Lyons, Councilor of supreme authority and reach, the only other authority, aside from Riefenstahl, with a vested interest in Angelia’s mission.


Nyto Morridow’s cover is burned while aboard the JU-094 helicopter near Bremen.

According to Q, Schwaben was loyally working beneath the incumbent director, while Q, flexing her prior performance over him during their early training, managed to gain the slip on the others and Lubyanka with Riefenstahl’s backing. Her certainty that Riefenstahl would eventually come out on top caught Angelia’s attention, affirmed by a tenacious Q that her payments would nearly triple; not to mention, by allegedly “tapping” into the Bee Sting System, likely gaining access permissions during the Stasi and MoD’s cooperation with Paradeus-Galatea, the Stasi’s surveillance far out-paced its prior leverage, with Angelia postulating that Q’s Lubyanka boss, whoever they are, was easily observed and directed by the organization licking its wounds from the Sunspot Incident years before. Moreover, Q clarified the identity of the “sparrow by Ulrich’s side”, pointing to Ulrich’s secretary, Morridow, being a Nyto, almost certainly known by Q’s faction with Paradeus intelligence via the Bee Sting System. Ultimately, the positions and strife within the Stasi is rather abstruse when faces have yet to be revealed - such as the prior director and mother or father of Light and Shadowless, Uhrig - so it cannot be established if they or Riefenstahl were the preeminent “emissary” for the Stasi and MoD’s cooperation with Paradeus-Galatea. It may be a twist of the Lake to blame Riefenstahl for all wrongdoing, as in PR and FP, despite maintaining the system until Schweinsteiger and her statuses were jeopardized, she carried through Schweinsteiger’s order to clean house of all evidence; second - it cannot be said if Q actually revealed Morridow’s identity to Angelia, unless the latter had significant doubts that someone as casual as Morridow, who was unlike any Nyto encountered up until then, could’ve been a Nyto, becoming undeniable after her lack of reaction to the Flora Institute hallucinogens and her expertise with a concealed-carry handgun in the Refugee District; and third - Riefenstahl is an indispensable ally of Lyons, a loyalty not easily bought or replaced, as she knew Sir from some point in the past.

While perhaps unrelated, on December 13th, 2049, six prominent Warsaw Pact figures met beneath a military base in Moscow for a confidential discussion regarding Lycoris’ proposal for implementing and fielding next-generation Doll control technology into the Soviet automated divisions. Mediated by Bureau Chief Viktor Pavlovich Zelinsky, other attending members included: Soviet Prime Minister Rubik Sedrakovich Khachikyan, International Service for Military-Technical Cooperation Bureau Chief Carter Petrovich Neustadt, Marshal/Commander of the Soviet Armed Forces Ivan Aleksevich Kirnusov, Socialist Unity Party of Germany Liaison Romy Riefenstahl, and the technology provider and specialist, Lycoris. Believed to have met in 2040, a Prometheus Councilor drafted a proposal to the Council to send “weaponizable technology to Eastern Europe”, choosing this path for the fact that they were “obliged to guide the way in which it unfolds” (Confidential Files 2, Chapter 2), directing the war towards a Soviet victory even before it begun. Nine years later, the six attendees, debating Lycoris’ proposal for the next-general Doll control systems, likely voted in favor of the resolution, likely becoming a watershed moment towards a Warsaw Pact victory in Italy and southern France during Operation Tradewind the following year into 2051. At face value, this holds little credence for any statement on Riefenstahl’s position; however, there’s a non zero possibility that Promethean-affiliated technology made its way to Lycoris and Persicaria’s research group in the Leipzig University of Karl Marx or later in 90wish, and Lycoris’ technology proposal in Moscow was a means of indirectly introducing it to the Soviets and their East German allies. Furthermore, Lycoris and Persicaria were extracted in early 2049 from Germany to IOP safehouses through Witkin’s request to Kryuger, and given Lyons was a former friend of Lycoris - having met him on New Years Eve 2040 into 2041, later mentioning Persicaria to Kryuger in the significant 7.62 Bar meeting in 2052 - there’s a tenuous hypothetical that Lyons’ intelligence expertise and connections in Eastern Europe landed him on Councilor and MI6 wartime head Major General Sir Isaac’s radar, possibly working to save his old friend Lycoris and Persicaria with Kryuger in 2049. Moreover, given Witkin and Zelinsky have been high-ranking agents of the Council for decades, perhaps they were given a directive to extract the 90wish members from West Germany, so as to introduce 90wish technolgoy - led by a likely former UNRA Beaconist, mind you - into Warsaw Pact hands. Riefenstahl’s involvement in the meeting is notable too, as any single person could’ve been the GDR’s liaison to the 2049 Moscow meeting, yet she was chosen for a reason, implying she must’ve been highly-placed by December 2049, whether she be a high-ranking Stasi official or Party member.

To be clear, this is very speculative, involving stacking various theories and painting a picture of an imagined situation, yet it should spark some common discussion, even if nothing more to disprove it; not to mention, Lyons wasn’t even inducted into the Council until at least 2051, so if he was involved, it was only out of commonality to Zelinsky and Witkin, which could’ve arisen from their mutual Rossartrist positions, unless this genuinely was part of Isaac’s screening of Lyons for the Council, acting as a clandestine Rossartrist blade before officially being introduced to the powers-that-be. Nothing necessarily binds any of this together, but it would provide an answer on how Riefenstahl knows Lyons - not as a Councilor, but a mutual ally in Germany. What this doesn’t answer, however, is how the Stasi would grow so sympathetic to Paradeus-Galatea under the Prometheans’ noses, seemingly unaware of the wider picture, yet partnered closely enough to share mutual objectives, especially in regards to Paradeus. If Riefenstahl was indeed playing both sides of the street for the good of the GDR - using Paradeus’ technology while assisting the Rossartrists against volatile, destabilizing groups like Carter and Oberstein - then maybe her attempts at persuading Schweinsteiger to Lyons’ side was part of this gambit, specifically regarding the Prometheans’ desire of Paradeus’ technology for the upcoming new world order, with Riefenstahl or the other former Stasi directors possibly among the earliest beneficiaries - protecting the country and securing the pathway of the future. Yes, it’s true the Stasi and Riefenstahl were involved with Paradeus, as was the MoD, but unlike what the Lake implies, she’s squarely window dressing Germany’s image and assisting Lyons by persuading Schweinsteiger away from Oberstein, isolating the latter until he has nothing left but promising a bullet to his temple amid the austere political setting. Likewise, Riefenstahl could’ve been nothing more than a high-ranking Stasi official at the wrong position at the right time, taking over the previous director’s position, only to immediately initiate data destruction on any connection to Paradeus once in power, working alongside Schweinsteiger to appease the Rossartrists. Influence over the latter may yet still pull him closer to Oberstein, with his deafening silence to Riefenstahl after receiving Oberstein’s “gift” directly on his private jet from Berlin to Frankfurt. While not exactly a satisfactory answer, the fairest understand is that Oberstein acted as the intermediary for a cooperation between the German MoD and Galatea, with Paradeus behind its veil; thereafter, only those read-in on the black program - the creation of joint state-Paradeus production facilities, employing “paramilitary” Paradeus troops under the Stasi and MoD - knew the extent of the operation, splitting the Stasi between those innocently investigating the enigmatic cult, such as Schwaben’s case on Paradeus’ child trafficking operations in southern Germany, and those genuinely pulling the strings to maintain the status quo, perhaps even allowing for Paradeus to sink its stinger directly into the German intelligence apparatus, enabling all-domain information control and surveillance as far away as Lubyanka. Moreover, “William” managed to bypass StateSec to boldly call Zelinsky directly, offering the recently-captured Ulrich in return for the security codes for “Base 22” - whether this is OKB-167 or elsewhere is beside the point; prodding further, “William” mocked StateSec’s attempts to trace him, assuring Zelinsky these efforts would ultimately prove fruitless as his “connections and intelligence network have also extended to places where even StateSec cannot reach”, perhaps an early allusion to Paradeus’ all-pervasive surveillance system, as well as its influence within the Stasi, likely brokered by the former director before Riefenstahl who fulfilled the Galatea-MoD cooperation. And with her stern warnings about Morridow and the Bee Sting System, Q rose from her seat, grabbed the priciest record, then left as if she were never there.

Like a Moth to the Flame

Hot on William’s Trail

Angelia Viktorovna Tsoi overlooks the Bremen Refugee District amid the riots.

Although the veracity of Q’s meeting with Angelia is somewhat in question, the events following the evacuation from the Bremen Refugee District differ greatly from the core narrative, molding a hodgepodge of corrupted memories. Rather than be extracted from the JU-094 crash site near the Weser River, only AK12 was aboard, with Angelia and the rest of DEFY riding with Q in a black Porsche SUV owned by one of her superiors. While Schwaben’s faction were meticulously searching the riverside like our own, the group were flooring it to Berlin on the Autobahn, when RPK16 received the very same email that conveniently bypassed all her firewalls, as if the sender had transfer permission without a trace. In the Lake memories, Angelia promptly ignored Lyons’ request to meet him at the Athena’s Owl in Alt Berlin, instead taking the wheel straight to the Neu-Tempelhof Mansion. 

The group must’ve disembarked and rested in the Berlin apartment before heading for the mansion, given Angelia dreamt of the past again, of the watershed day in Beslan. A flash of old memory regressed, with narration speaking of the dissolution of the body to the Earth and soul into nothingness, possibly wordplay of an Old Testament verse: “And the dust returns to the ground it came from, and the spirit returns to God who gave it” (Eccleisiates 12:7, New International Version), wherein the nihilism surrounding the abrupt loss of Armin, Ramzan, and Sana continuously haunted her, even in 2062, assuming the encounter with Ganglati was factual. Rejecting this notion, Angelia stared at the young girl cowering behind the bomb safety box in the Beslan gymnasium in 2050, demanding she lift herself from that nothingness, refusing her consciousness to sink into that dreaded day. Likewise, while the physical may disappear, the existence of one’s self will be imprinted upon the scars left on others, eventually fading as time itself forgets, or their souls will be granted false deliverance into the perpetual limbo of the Lake, simultaneously the key of a quasi-eternal soul.

Hot on William’s trail in Berlin, Agent U, indirectly assigned to her by the untrustworthy Lyons, was sent as a new surveillance agent over her needs and operations in Berlin, representing the former director, aka Schwaben’s, faction of the Stasi, namely those not read-in on the innermost functions and shadowy relationships of the Ministry. Before setting out for the mansion, presumably discovered in the same manner from Morridow Voigt’s apartment after her cover was blown, Angelia linked up Q and several of her colleagues in an armory in the safehouse, laden with firearms, ammunition, IFAKs, and explosives, including an M4A1 carbine with an M203 40mm grenade launcher. Questioning why Q planned to bring along so many weapons, she assured that Morridow, having fallen over a hundred meters from the JU-094 helicopter and now-verifiably a Nyto, this armory was insurance against the inhuman. Somehow possessing forward knowledge of Paradeus VIP, callsign “Big Fish”, Q affirmed they’d arrive at the manor within an hour, leaving strictly limited time to search the manor. Essentially acting as bait, Angelia and DEFY left the safehouse for Neu-Tempelhof, arriving before the overgrown veneer concealing the decrepit townhouse of deceit; upon entering, the tall grass impeded their sightlines, as if they were tangled in the densest forests of Vietnam. A critical change in the Lake memories versus our universe is the presence of AK12, who disappeared amid the chaos of the apartment complex firefight, last seen by Light in their safehouse apartment. How exactly AK12 ended up as Koleda remains a significant mystery, a question still unanswered three years later, but there’s reason to believe AK12 had gone deep undercover, with Light as her possible sole witness.

A Secondary Infiltration
When Paradeus ambushed Angelia in the apartment, only AK12 and Light were with her, while AN94, AK15, RPK16, and other Stasi agents were preoccupied with the death squads ascending the complex; AN94 and AK15 stayed on the lower floors to fend off their attackers, RPK16 diverting to link up - and rescue, as was required - the trio if Paradeus had already infiltrated the upper floors, using the ground floor as a feint for the actual kill/capture. Notably, unlike the mansion battle, their attackers were far more dedicated to killing Angelia than purposefully attacking errantly, contrasting Paradeus facilitating capture by Gray at the end of the manor battle, wherein none of the shots directed at her were lethally aiming for center mass. Whether this be subordinate faction of Gray, deployed to assassinate Angelia for her past intervention at the Galatea Warehouse, or standard operating procedure against agent edging too close to their truth, isn’t said, yet something changed in the manor battle, mandating the Strelets to purposefully miss or shoot to incapacitate. Perhaps Lyons finally sold her out for leaving the nest one too many times, or she discovered something she shouldn’t in the manor, but something did change, evidenced by RPK16’s repeated warnings that Angelia should heed her investigation until the higher-ups - namely Lyons, Zelinsky, or Misha - brief her with additional information or objectives. Pinned down in the complex, the advancing Paradeus troops were rapidly closing the net, and for Angelia and RPK16, assigned as the Doll leader of DEFY with command permissions, to successfully escape, AK12 chose to stay behind to reduce the enemy’s pressure, diverting their attention away for her allies to escape. Light, having sustained a twisted ankle from a floor collapse, chose to stay with her, following AK12 until splitting off, so as to route the enemies in separate directions, opening a corridor for Angelia and RPK16. Firing and maneuvering down the structure, AN94 finally reestablished contact with them, as electronic communications were actively jammed, with Paradeus retreating after losing many men and track of their target, as well as the rapidly-responding Stasi and law-enforcement officers. At the ground floor, Kevin and other agents arrived to receive the wounded, discovering the nearly-faded Angelia from smoke-inhalation and exhaustion. Acting as Kevin’s protege, the absence of Light carved his core, surfacing true fear behind his eyes, and with communications still jammed, neither AK12 nor Light’s communicators were received; once restored, however, both signals were still reportedly offline. Although J assumed the worst had come to pass against Light, quite the opposite had yet to pass.

Presumably the following day, Angelia and DEFY paid Leone Michel a “visit” to the Galatea Sanatorium - escorted their from the Flora Institute after receiving a slap on the wrist from the government and a broken wrist from a Silver Fox - to discuss the contents of Gray’s research, now aware she was working for them in some way. Promising to protect Michel in return for information on Gray’s plans with Epiphyllum research and Idunn, Michel begrudgingly accepted, opening up on what little had been revealed to her in the strictly-compartmentalized informational structure. As the apparent creator or a lead researcher into the matter, Paradeus’ Boxes of Iaso were controlled-bloom Epiphyllum oxypetalum, designed to emit the absorbed Collapse Particles upon the timing of the bloom, surmised by Michel to be a limited-scale WMD to artificially contaminate the affected area then promote public support from the Gray Institute of Biotechnology’s Idunn Vaccine - all the product of the so-called Operation Cocoon, allegedly sanctioned by William himself, wherein immunes were to be filtered from those baptized by the Collapse emissions. After Gray’s disappearance, the newest-hire Cornelia Schafer began her own investigation into her former “hero”, working alongside Kevin and Schwaben’s, and with Galatea’s Third Branch Building soon to be condemned, Schafer was invited for a farewell dinner with the rest of the research members, reluctantly agreeing to attend. With access to the Institute’s database, she opened the query for a pursued lead on Paradeus’ arms trafficking operation, returning a single entry for “Umruss”, possibly derived from the German word “Umriss”, referring to a silhouette or contour of an object, perhaps referring to Franz Schrek managing the ultranationalist weapon shipments between Galatea and Berlin Airport, bound for Carter’s rebel troops internationally.


Agents J and K discover Franz Schrek is Paradeus-Galatea’s arms trafficker, Umriss.

Satisfied with this information, Schafer joined her colleagues in the workroom cafeteria, abound with discussions on future job opportunities. As former members of the Idunn Project - eponymous with the Old Norse goddess of restoration and rejuvenation - representatives of the the closest-to-success anti-ELID projects in modern times, they would naturally be welcomed anywhere, especially those desperate for talents of their caliber; as it were, Idunn’s research far surpassed any on the continent, reaching Phase III clinical trials, but never surpassing it. Disappointed by the stunted progress, Schafter mentioned that she couldn’t understand “why it (Idunn) would have resulted in brain death”, brought about by her injecting the destitute Old Pete, whose condition improved but immediately declined after a delayed period. All her colleagues fell silent, oppressively filling the air in hesitancy, only for Eicher to chime in, asking how she couldn’t have known. Buried in an NDA she hurriedly signed during her induction, the true direction of research was laid out: rather than widespread treatment, Idunn was gene selection; by “filtering” out human immune systems for the “appropriate antibodies”, discovering the core “Perfect Antibody” was paramount, wherein the successful subject’s blood will be extracted and replicated, becoming the actual saving grace. Melanie further backed this claim, firmly stating a perfect treatment for ELID was impossible without such forceful means, rather reminiscent of Meitner’s rejection of bureaucracy to achieve progress in her discipline. Indeed, Idunn’s promise to the masses was a marketing scheme in itself, enticing crowds with Galatea’s golden goose, all while truthfully used to screen for Paradeus’ perfect immune; as Professor Iverson put it, Idunn’s promise was a “Tower of Babel” in itself - an impossibly avaricious ambition that enticed the masses, only to be struck down with the almighty truth that immunity is supposedly impossible without sacrifice, pushing ethical and academic boundaries to realize this dream.

Returning to the Galatea Sanitarium, Angelia assigned RPK16, who requested the assignment, to defend Michel with the Stasi against any possible Galatea retribution against her, aiming to silence a potential informant as in-the-know as she was. Naturally, Michel panicked at her first appearance, shaking at the thoughts of RPK16’s torture in DR, then she lambasted whoever dared created an AI as devious as her, to which RPK16 assured her that she was created from something “far more precious”, presumably referring to Shaw’s objectives for “Pandora”. Terrified at RPK16’s assertions about “becoming human”, Michel pleaded for another guard, anyone but her, to watch over her, and it was Kevin who came to the door, acting as Michel’s salvation before the Silver Fox. In reality, Kevin only appeared to pass the surveillance permissions of the Sanitarium from the director, granting her direct access and control over the facility should she need it. As Kevin mulled over Michel’s complaints, growing increasingly agitated by her assertions against the Stasi, RPK16 chimed in abruptly, confirming that a Paradeus force had arrived for their attempted decapitation operation. The force Paradeus deployed was limited, but the performance of its regular troopers and the Nyto leading them outpaced the thinly-armed Stasi security and inexperienced Sanitarium Dolls; and guaranteeing Michel’s safety meant RPK16 “had” to make an escape with her, dropping her guard against the Silver Fox at the crucial moment. While RPK16 carried Leone away, Kevin rushed for the entrance, where the contingent could only be stalled by the Sanitarium’s active security forces; however, before being overwhelmed, Angelia and DEFY, along with the presumed-KIA Light, burst out from the sidelines, intercepting the enemy force before their breakthrough. Once AK15 had slammed the Nyto’s throat into ground, Light order the Stasi reinforcements to advance and encircle the entrance, closing the net on Paradeus’ avenues of escape.

With the contingent halted, the party discovered all the attackers had taken time-delayed poisons, with their features disfigured and fingerprint minutiae unrecognizable; essentially, only DNA sampling could potentially return an identity. Kevin, still processing Light’s survival, was taken aback by his apparent “resurrection”, but truthfully, Angelia confirmed that she ordered Light to keep his lips sealed, so as to mislead Paradeus’ desperate attempts at capturing or killing Angelia and trimming loose ends like Michel. As for how Light escaped, little is said before Angelia cut them off, but Light stated AK12 was involved, suggesting she escorted the injured Light out of the apartment building when splintering off from Angelia. Considering AK12 hadn’t appeared again until speaking with RPK16 in Avernus, AK12 possibly orchestrated her infiltration under deep cover, intentionally disappearing after saving Light to hack or disguise herself as the Nyto Koleda. Her introduction to Avernus suggests Paradeus hadn’t known her identity, with the exception of RPK16, who seemingly chose not to reveal Koleda’s identity, possibly collaborating to deliver Angelia from danger. 


Leone Michel’s body after attempting to escape with RPK16.

As for Michel, however, she didn’t escape the Sanitarium as well as AK12 had the apartment building, wherein a sizable gash was cut from Michel’s throat during their escape. According to RPK16’s story, she stated Michel was attacked by a White Nyto’s scythe in the facility’s tunnel, but of course, there was no way to prove the veracity of her testimony, as the cameras were destroyed beforehand; not to mention, RPK16 was the last known person with administrator permissions over the facility’s surveillance systems. Therefore, it’s more than likely that RPK16, said to the Paradeus mole at Angelia’s side, was ordered to kill Michel by Gray. One major hole remains unanswered in all this: how RPK16 was planted as Paradeus “mole” and Lyons’ dangle, seemingly playing double agent against Paradeus. Considering the time frame, RPK16 must’ve been directed to infiltrate Paradeus after visiting the Flora Institute and Michel in DR, and before the apartment attack in MS, spanning only a few days timewise. Assuming RPK16 truly is Lyons’ dangle, perhaps her backers pulled strings to place her in a suitable position to speak with Gray or another Nyto, eventually “defecting” to Paradeus during the mansion battle. But in Agent Angelia’s memories in the Lake, none of these experiences ever come to pass, instead heading straight for Neu-Tempelhof from Bremen.

Mirrored Reality
Entering the mansion with DEFY and several of Q’s colleagues, Q set up her rifle from afar, awaiting their prey to take the bait. Apart from the figures present at the mansion battle against Nyto Gray, little is changed, but the spare few new dialogues do grant additional insight into Paradeus and the Stasi’s objects. After Gray arrived, Angelia quickly opened a communication with Q - ordering AK12 and AK15 to hold off Gray in the meantime - to request target combat data for any signs of weakness, of which were none, as according to Q, nothing was returning in the Bee Sting System, suggesting that perhaps her security clearance wasn’t high enough to view the rest of the files. Realizing Q’s faction had limited access privileges, Angelia surmised their preeminent objective wasn’t taking out Gray or Paradeus, but to obtained ownership of the Bee Sting System, elevating the Stasi’s influence far beyond any modern intelligence service could dream of - total, real-time, surveillance nearly instantaneously. If Q’s faction truly wishes to obtain the Bee Sting System, and this is not some twist of the Lake or surgery, perhaps Q’s association to Riefenstahl, tangentially to the Prometheans through her to Lyons, is emblematic of Lyons’ ambitions regarding Paradeus: securing Paradeus’ technologies for the Union of Rossartrism; furthermore, with Lyons’ grand vision of a new world built upon foundations of mandated order and cooperation, maybe the path forward for this spymaster is the Bee Sting and OGAS, simultaneously automating the URNC economy and state surveillance. Q did mention, after all, that her and Angelia’s objectives aligned until Q’s faction had obtained what’s desired, granting full admin privileges, thus ownership, to the Riefenstahl’s faction after dealing with Paradeus, in a similar vein to Lyons’ own stance, wherein he sought to tear Paradeus from the roots - not for the sake of slaying the beast, but to commune with it. Riefenstahl, however, doesn’t seem to share the same sentiments as the orchestrators, at least publicly with her subordinates, so even she might be a pawn in all of this, desiring the Bee Sting for the Stasi, ultimately transferring it to Lyons’ network, given Stasi has made its way to the shared Lyons-Witkin-WAVE-Promethean intelligence network on multiple occasions, such as the miraculous discovery of the Oberstein Mansion picture in Morridow Voigt’s apartment.

After severely damaging Gray to great effect, with the original Wolf Pack directing the best of their strengths against their formidable opponent, Nyto Grig made an unexpected appearance, absent from the original MS battle. Reporting that Morridow had finished her mission, having captured Morridow and defeated the Commander and their Dolls, Gray gave the retreat order, abruptly pulling out before AK12 and AK15 could finish her off or engage Grig. Although the sequence of the event was swapped, Angelia still entered the study, discovering the yew-shaped Oberstein family true, with “William” and Lunasia’s portraits burnt, then inversely to reality, the Commander relays a message to Angelia, promising they were comrades and requesting they save Dandelion before Paradeus could escape with her. Now on the trail of Dandelion and Gray, Angelia and DEFY were about to leave when Agent “U”, Light S.,  and several of his faction’s agents had surrounded the mansion, blasting the already-mangled front door to pieces with a 40mm grenade. Retreating back into the mansion, another fight ensued that hadn’t taken place in reality, once more filling the halls with gunfire. Narrowly avoiding the agents’ shots and blows, Angelia was eventually knocked to ground by Light, while AK15 and AK12 savagely beat his men as he held his handgun to Angelia’s temple. Once communications were reestablished, Angelia knew fully well that “Agent U” before her was the agent assigned to watch over her activities in Berlin; albeit in real life, Kevin and Light’s transfer order was orchestrated by someone of great influence, likely Lyons working alongside the Riefenstahl faction to facilitate the transfer from Bremen to Berlin. Over the communicator, Schwaben stated she had crossed a line by going this far, to which she questioned why the Stasi were responding so violently to the actions of one of their own - Q wasn’t on their side, allegedly. 

Quoting Schwaben, “Q and whoever’s behind her are collaborators” and that “she is involved in arms trafficking.” He went on to state his orders: erase all information about Q, and through her, Paradeus. Slightly altered from real life, Q was Riefenstahl’s assigned agent to trim Paradeus’ tendrils to the German government, so as to window dress their position, thus absolving themselves and Schweinsteiger of wrongdoing, avoiding a substantial domestic scandal. Considering the presence of the Paradeus-Stasi-MoD production facilities outside Berlin, there’s a verifiable link between Oberstein’s alleged dealing with Schweinsteiger, acting as the intermediary of Galatea’s contract with the German MoD; however, this was only a single piece of evidence, easy enough to be falsified by amateurs, let alone a prestigious organization like Paradeus under William or Meitner. Nonetheless, in the Lake, it was Schwaben and Light sent to erase the Q and the links to Paradeus, as her faction of the Stasi were collaborating with them. Indeed, the prior administration were conducting these dealings well before Riefenstahl was installed as the director in reality; moreover, the corruption is rampant from local to federal government, so this once again calls Riefenstahl’s into question, as she ultimately wishes for the state and Stasi to blossom. When Riefenstahl assumed her position, she simultaneously wished to restore the Stasi’s prestige and influence, while immediately supporting the Commander and Schwaben’s investigations into Paradeus. Assuming what Q had said in the Million Roses was truthful, then Riefenstahl likely sought to aid the Commander’s mission, while still reaping the rewards for the Stasi, such as gaining full access to the Bee Sting System; however, despite the Bee Sting Control Center’s destruction in the fall of Avernus, the system must possess a physical component, as a data has been corrupted or lost in certain areas that mitigated the Bee Sting’s all-pervasive eye, like the deluge of seawater that drowned OKB-167.

Maybe there’s an allegory to Lyons’ position, who’ll ultimately collaborate with Paradeus - be it William or Martha - for its technology, wherein Riefenstahl’s investigation bridges the Prometheans to their desired technologies, certainly including the Bee Sting System if Q of the Lake’s words hold true. Although not necessarily mutually exclusive, the scenes depicted in the Lake could’ve merely been the reflection of Q’s mission from Riefenstahl to erase the links, including knocking out Dupieux “Polar Bear” for interrogation. Moreover, Riefenstahl and Q in real life are not read-into Paradeus to any significant degree, possessing virtually the same intelligence as the Commander on their adversary - or in the Stasi’s case, mutual business associate. Although it’s certainly true Riefenstahl knows more than she lets on, possibly even already possessing low-level privileges to the Bee Sting System, she’s oblivious to the full scale of Paradeus’ operation, apart from the aforementioned cooperative plants, so to say she’s directly implicate with them would be incorrect - rather, she and Q, possibly Schwaben as well, are more read-into Paradeus, operating from intelligence gathered from the Promethean intelligence network. Riefenstahl is an ally of Lyons - through him, the Council - but she may or may not possess similar beliefs. She may truthfully want full admin privileges to the Bee Sting System, obtained through the prior director(s)’s dealings with Paradeus, yet she’s no certainly not playing on the same field as Lyons and Witkin, the former of which is orchestrating this overarching, international investigation to acquire useful technologies for the completion of Project Prometheus, such as OGAS or the Bee Sting System. Ultimately, there are two factions in the Stasi: those read-in and those who are not, and among the former, even they lack sufficient information on the headquarters and extent of their adversary and business associate’s operations, surveillance, and infiltration of German society. If what Q had to say was genuine in the Million Roses, even someone of her caliber only heard inklings of a Nyto named Morridow. As for arms trafficking, Oberstein, with whatever sector of Paradeus he controls, backed Carter’s rebellion by trafficking Boxes of Iaso, flown out of Berlin Airport by Galatea, overseen by Schrek. Although Q in reality seemed separate from arms trafficking, even the Stasi were oblivious to Galatea’s weapon transports to the airport, becoming the foundation of Kevin and Schwaben’s investigation into “Umruss”, working from intelligence provided by Gray Institute researcher Schafer. It’s possible certain highly-placed individuals under the past director were complacent or even complicit in the arms and human trafficking across Germany, compartmentalizing the Stasi to avoid intelligence leaks between the factions. Riefenstahl knew of the Stasi and MoD’s Paradeus ties, yet she too was oblivious to the wider picture of Galatea’s black projects and the source of the Bee Sting System, assuming the Million Roses memories prove accurate.

Staring into the muzzle of Light’s handgun, Angelia was at her wit’s end when the crack of a rifle bullet whizzed through his skull, taking him down instantly. While thankful, she wasn’t so pleased that Q took her sweet time to intervene, especially since Light’s faction had the same access to weapons and ammunition as the safe house they departed from. With the situation stabilized, Angelia focused on their next steps: tracking Gray and Grig to reach Dandelion, who’d been captured by Morridow after the Paradeus facility attack on the Commander’s end. Q agreed, terminating their communication, when a voice called out replied to her mutterings about Angelia, followed thereafter by gunshot. Q’s intervention is the point of significant divergence from reality, as there’s no clear understanding why Q’s presence would be so prominent, barring the short discussion in the Million Roses, representing a temporary, off-the-record meeting between the double agent and Angelia. That is to say, why exactly would there be a detailed scene of Q eliminating an agent with the same rifle CG used to incapacitate Dupieux. In all fairness, asset reuse is a common thing in CG artwork, not to say that’s a negative, but more so that there may be nothing of true importance here but a reference - a reference to Q, allegedly affiliated with the Paradeus faction, tying loose ends for Riefenstahl, who allegedly made some use of the Bee Sting System with her limited clearance.

In the Lake scene, Q was taken out from behind by RPK16 after killing Light with the sniper rifle, while in Fixed Point, Q was last seen in FP lowering her rifle after shooting Dupieux with the electroshock round. During E&S, Q spoke to Schawben and Kein about her overseas deployment, trimming Paradeus' tendrils to isolate the German government from its connections to Paradeus-Galatea. Perhaps something could've happened to Q after knocking out Dupieux at the German-Soviet Border, as the only other time we hear from her after Dupieux’s capture was her contacting Schwaben and Kevin to pass information on Aliana’s movements in Berlin, though this could’ve just been provided to her by StateSec, having possibly reverse-engineered the Dog Tag System after she was mothballed or were actively tracking her, exploited by the double-agent Q to swap StateSec intel to her Stasi colleagues. Maybe Q did approach Angelia in the Million Roses, but her prominence in the entire Agent Angelia section is cause for debate, as there’s zero suggestion in real life of Q ever meeting Angelia so far, unless Angelia made a vow of silence not to disclose what Q outlined in the off-the-record meeting, ensuring total privacy for everyone involved, while not speaking out of suspicion that Q could’ve been gaslighting her on Paradeus’ infiltration. Generally, there’s far too little to draw any meaningful conclusions, yet Q’s association to Agent Angelia’s story was by no means coincidence, so it remains to be seen just how read-in Q is; after all, it was Riefenstahl who picked her as the agent to window dress the Stasi and MoD’s, suggesting the respect she had for Q, entrusting this mission to someone as “read-in” as her on Paradeus’ influence. Could Q herself be a Nyto? Perhaps, but evidence for that theory is virtually nonexistent, apart from possessing access privileges to the Bee Sting System; however, such connection has nothing to do with being a Nyto, given the system files can be read by anyone with sufficient clearance, VCI or physical computers.

As Angelia and DEFY left the building, they discovered an unconscious AN94, whose neural cloud had been forcibly hacked and shut down by RPK16 while waiting outside the mansion with several other of Q’s agents, all deceased. With limited time, they launched a search and capture operation on RPK16, questioning what would’ve driven her to turn her weapon on DEFY and their allies, with Angelia ordering she must be captured in one piece to understand why - whether it be hacking, a neural cloud flaw or malfunction, or actions yet understood. Still, RPK16 wasted no time in her escape in this mirrored memory, making her break while running DEFY in circles. Now alone, communications lost, and Q MIA, they had no choice but to pursue their adversary for the Commander’s sake, commandeering the Stasi Porsche SUV. When AK12 blew part of Gray’s stinger tail off, she planted a tracker just before Grig arrived as support, and the device’s last known ping was in the city, while Dandelion and Morridow were on a similar heading: a Contaminated Zone near the city, dredging up the memories of the 2051 spring operation.

Adamant as ever, Angelia assured AK12 that she’d open any door, walk any path, and glimpse anything RPK16 prevented her from doing, once again on the tumultuous road, defiant until the end, even if RPK16 ultimately had her best interests at heart. On the road to the Dead Sea, the four swapped seats and rested before the next suicide mission, with AK12’s emblematic comment on breaking traffic laws on the highway to their eventual end, defiant until the end. AK15 switched on the radio, tuning into some soothing tracks as the evening sky dimmed; with the emergence of a fog brought tranquility, and to AN94, unfamiliar nostalgia, hearing the tune of Anna, possibly referencing Pugacheva’s “Million Roses”, or a concept for a euphony of Anna’s life, a musical composition of her gnarled memories by the Lake and RPK16’s interjection. Serenity shifted to alarm when AN94 commented how long they’d been driving in a single direction, questioning why they hadn’t passed into the Quarantine Zone yet, and with a harsh, electrical disruption over the radio, RPK16 spoke to her directly.
