Remember, RPK16 injected herself in Agent Angelia’s story, assuming the role of an RPK16 who forcibly shined a mirror tragic side of her obstinacy directly against Angelia’s actions, depicting the cost, while verifying if her Commander’s decisions would ever change. Angelia “knew this would be a path of no return”, yet she continued on, forcing RPK16 to “prove my allegiance to my true master”, according to RPK16’s abrupt messages over the radio. Meitner was proud of her standout, tenacious student, likely seeing a reflection of her own values in Angelia, both of whom have made unyielding strides towards the completion of their goals, no matter how foolish or bloody at times. As for her “true master”, it’s all but confirmed RPK16 is Lyons’ informant into Paradeus, but her eventual “takeover” of Angelia’s body - seemingly not in an act of malice, but of respect and salvation - depicts RPK16’s respect for her Commander’s position, willing to carry her burdens to their promised end. The car swerved off the highway, overturning in a ditch, damaging DEFY, and ejecting Angelia into an abyss; the last she heard of subordinates was their sorrowful admittance of defeat. Amid the darkness, RPK16 came to her directly, asking the same question Meitner had posed so many times before: “If everything in life is futile, then what is the point in struggling?” Followed thereafter by one of the most evocative lines in all of Slow Shock, “I can only show my loyalty through betrayal.” For continuity discussion of RPK16’s intrusion will be withheld until the “Until We Have No Choice” section, found below.

Chapter 7 - For A World More Than Light and Shade (Angelia Viktorovna Tsoi)

Arise from Abaddon
Slaughterhouse of Souls
In the thirteen years since Operation Couatl, Avernus has stood as Paradeus’ most coveted secret, never exposed until Operation Aeneas in October 2064, wherein the megastructure - originally planned as the physical, floating symbol of mankind’s unity, towering as Babel towards Heaven - has become a bloodstained labyrinth, ceaseselly screening, processing, and refining bodies and souls. As Avernus stands today, the megastructure exists as the root of Paradeus - its central production facilities, the hub of the Bee Sting surveillance system, its training grounds, the birthplace of Nytos, and the source of its beliefs. How Nytos are created isn’t implicitly stated in order, nor are their purposes necessarily universal beyond immunity screening; nevertheless, Avernus’ Nyto technology industrial pipeline can be reasonably broken down into a few steps: first - the original Hela subject; second - the Material Screening Center; third - the production lines for Nyto modifications on surviving subjects; and lastly - the training grounds, as well as the neural pods for mental stability should the situation demand it.

While the process is uncertain, all Nytos individuals begin as synthesized replicas of a “snapshot” consciousness, transferred to the Lake of Cognition during the Holy Grail-Hela surgical procedure, a traumatic and intrusive brain surgery. Upon a successful transfer, which may or may not depend on the body’s rejection of the procedure, their consciousness, composed of memory fragments, is deposited into the Lake through unstated means, either uploaded through the Evangel Axis nodes or transcended into the Lake via the procedure itself. Regardless, these memory fragments are anchored within through the Evangel Axis mechanism, which generates an “ice sheet” between the Lake and a Nyto’s individual Virtual Cognition Image. The Evangel Axis’ core seems to exist at the bottom of the Lake, only connected to our world via the physical Evangel Axis nodes throughout Avernus; however, to maintain this Lake-Evangel System, the Evangel and the emulation of Nirvana requires tremendous bioenergy input to sustain the ice sheet, now an iceberg after thirteen years. When a new consciousness is synthesized, the original subject’s memory fragments are dissolved either into blueprint seeds, if you will, of the new consciousness through the Evangel or converted into raw energy to sustain the Evangel. Externally in our world, bioenergy from liquidated biologics is harvested across Avernus, wherein it’s piped to its intended location, whether it be the Evangel or other power facilities. Already representing cyclical death and sacrifice for others, this newly-generated consciousness is implanted into a Nyto subject body, possibly the body of the original Hela subject or a clone. 


A Paradeus cloning facility.

In the Material Screening Center, located on Level 2 of the Eastern Tower, these test subjects are dumped into a large pool for the selection process, whereupon limited quantities of Collapse Particles are injected through the pool’s inlet. Each subject must exhibit sufficient immunoresistance to the exposure, otherwise be immediately liquidated and harvested for bioenergy and raw genetic material. During Sana’s awakening, the bioenergy cost necessitated a mass-harvest from screening and production facilities, conveying the bioenergy through the pipelines to the secret laboratory on Level 35. When Nemhran order the activation of the “Gatekeeper of Hell” - Sana, the first and closest aligned with the Evangel Axis - all power was shut down to the Screening Center, followed by a gush of Collapse Particles from the pool inlet, rapidly elevating the temperature to a boil as the test subjects were blasted by high-density exposure. The water continued to churning as they thrashed for their lives, banging against the walls amid the lethal flow, but soon the pool stilled, now an immersion of boiling water, Collapse Fluid, and liquidated test subjects, with anything insoluble sinking to the floor. Any survivors in the workshop were purged thereafter by an irradiated mist that consumed the entire room, leaving nothing but the grim, still pool. Once cleared, the disposal chute beneath the pool opened, dumping materials from filtered subjects while channeling the “purified” bioenergy into the conduits up to Sana in Level 35 - or in general, anywhere in Avernus requiring energy. Tangentially, William asked Nemhran permission to activate the Gatekeeper of Hell, perhaps suggesting she held domain over the Evangel Axis System, given her codename is “Evangelist”; moreover, as Nemhran and Sana were evacuating prior to Operation Kriemhild, Sana mentioned how Meitner never treated her as her daughter, “just like how she was never his mother.”, referring to William. If we’re to believe Nemhran was a Nyto replication of the Oberstein mother, perhaps William never viewed Nyto Nemhran as his mother, rather a symbol of her, exemplified by Nemhran’s comment that both Nytos had no say in what their respective mother and son thought of them.

Within the Avernus Platform, all refuse from the disposal chutes above is dumped into a wider pool beneath the waste processing and sorting facility, congealing into a grisly mass of irradiated water, flesh, Collapse crystals, dead plants, and excess parts and components. Apart from Avernus’ waste, additional materials and luxury parts are likely imported via the subways in the subterranean shipping railyard, presumably constructed by the UNRA as the foundation of what would later become Avernus. In the waste facility, the automated sorting process collects the piling refuse onto conveyors that bring them to the sorting workbenches, wherein anything unsalvageable is dumped onto the disposal belt, conveying it into the abyss. 



Underneath the platform rests an underground fissure - completely shrouded in darkness, only accessible through the drainage pipes from the waste processing facility. Here, irradiated waste fluids, artificial humanoids, and other garbage is cast into the misty nothingness, akin to the lowest layer of the universe, Niflhel, in Norse mythology. Decayed Nyto and Isomer subject bodies and bleached bones litter the ground of the abyss, nearly imperceptible through the darkness; this is the final end for all physical things - failures and garbage alike - from Avernus, cast into the macabre abyss, never to be remembered again. All we can hope for these lost souls is for light to shine through the crevices after Avernus fell. Unfortunately, this is but one direction of the Nyto process, representing the end of any test subject of inadequate immunoresistance, while the resistant are transferred to the production lines. As the objective of this entire process is the creation or discovery of an immune, every nonimmune subject was irredeemably a failure, but partial resistance is the bare minimum for a true Nyto, progressing these “specimens” to their modification stage.

Although little is written on the actual modifications done to the subjects’ bodies, the results are self-evident: cybernetic limbs, neurostabilizers, weaponized prostheses, etc. Notably, specimens on the production lines are still subject to bioenergy harvests in the, given the conduits flow through every floor, and during Sana’s awakening, a number of specimens entered a deadly melee for warmth inside one of the specimen disintegration pods, only for their bioenergy to flow into the very same power conduit they so desperately clung to. Filtering the test subjects down to specimens, this group is further reduced after their modifications are completed, as the completed Nytos are immediately sent to Avernus’ physical and mental training grounds. Discovered by Fe56, one of the largest physical training rooms was an open area for simulated, high-intensity conflict; even Dreamer, among the Sangvis ringleader elites, only managed a “C grade” on the lowest difficulty. Moving at lightning speeds, the targets in the simulated combat far exceeded the capabilities of any recruit, and those that couldn’t keep up, nor improve, were disposed of. Alchemist, one of SF’s most agile melee fighters, was rattled by the qualification requirements, serving to explain Nytos’ exemplary dexterity, and for this, Fe56 actually downloaded the simulations under the pretenses of G&K possibly employing them in its own drills. Tucked behind the wall of the training room was a one-way window into the room, wherein the Nyto is kept under constant observation by someone they cannot be certain is or isn’t present; therefore, they must obey and never falter “under constant fear” of Schrödinger's cat. 


Chapter artworks for the major event Mirror Stage, inspired by the Rorschach inkblot test.

While specifics are not explored, it would seem the weapons chosen for higher-ranking Nytos reflect the results of their Rorschach psychological evaluation, as Morridow, Gray, and Grig perceived a spider, scorpion, and mantis, respectively. Morridow has her spider prostheses, Gray has her stinger tail, and Grig has her wrist blades and saber; furthermore, although her evaluation isn’t shown, Narciss has a wasp on her clothing, with her floating blades probably representing their stingers. Lastly, to maintain Paradeus’ influence over the Nytos, apart from anchoring their blueprint memory fragments in the Lake, any Nyto that experiences memory regression is regularly sent for brainwashing (reformatting) and review in another training room, meant to hone the intellect of Nytos after proving their physical capabilities. Considering Nytos are inherently failures of the process towards creating the perfect individual, any disloyalty to Father or Paradeus is unacceptable, immediately marking them for disposal. By Operation Aeneas in early October 2064, untold thousands have been birthed and sacrificed in this slaughterhouse, exemplified by the defilement of human souls and countless atrocities from the underground fissure to the Relic Experiment Zone. Like Meitner’s hollow heart, this place is void of all humanity. Although a considerable stretch and not directly related, when DEFY and 404 discovered the test subjects, Test Subject EOT-1 requested UMP45 refer to her as “Anna” - uniquely intriguing, given Angelia’s real name and prior connection to Paradeus through Meitner. As one of Meitner’s most commendable students, both academically and philosophically, the name Anna is one rooted in Meitner’s personality. If the 2051 mission is believed true, there is a weak, yet non zero possibility of that name having reverberated through Paradeus, with EOT-1 knowing or “sensing” the importance of that name. Even “Ganglati”, a Nyto synthesized from Ramzan’s blueprint, fought to the end to remember Anna’s name as his memories were edited from the Lake.

Only Death is Ahead

Shadowless stands before the grave of her younger brother, Light.

After RO635 and Koleda disengaged the medical catheters attached to Angelia during Operation Aeneas, Angelia gradually regained consciousness as she exited through the door of the Lake of Cognition, opened by Blackwell of the Lake. In the physiological monitoring white room - a common white torture method in which the subject is deprived of all senses, eroding their psyche into insanity or submission - RO635 barged in as Koleda supported Angelia’s feeble body. Recognizing Angelia’s serious condition, RO635 realized the purpose of the Strongarm device, meant to be delivered to Angelia, was to monitor and report Angelia’s condition through the Aeneas Conference Room. After snapping the device around her right wrist, the reported medical data were concerning, showing low hypotension and low blood-oxygen saturation. Contacting UMP45, a link was quickly established to the Conference Room so Angelia could message the Commander, whereupon she delivered the password-encrypted message, locked behind a confirmation that “The Present” is what we should strive for the most towards the future. With minimal time, she locked the critical part of the message so that she could confirm that the Commander truly was her comrade, warning them that Lyons did not seek to eradicate Paradeus, but to acquire its technologies and bring William under his wing, implying William told Angelia parts of his - and presumably, Meitner’s - plans. Knowing William and Meitner, a monster that killed her former teacher - had to be dealt with before they could open a conversation with Lyons’ faction, she described her plan as “Operation Ilya Muromets”, though part of her plan description is cut off. Ending her remarks, she quoted the inscription depicted in Russian artist and folklorist Viktor Vasnetsov’s renowned painting, Knight at the Crossroads, illustrating the sojourn of legendary Slavic folk hero, Ilya Muromets.

In the painting, Ilya rests on his horse before a stone inscribed in Cyrillic text, warning its reader against pressing forward, for the path ahead brings only death to those who “travel past, walk past, or fly past.” Resting on the Eastern European plain, bones are strewn across the ground as ravens flock the hollowed field around the ominous stone; in the sky, towards the heavens, there is light, but only darkness cast over the plains from the low-hanging sky. As a headstrong warrior of the Rus people whose committed soul always safeguarded the fatherland, refusing to falter, no better hero mirrors that of Angelia and the Commander. In the plentiful folklore legends of Ilya Muromets, retold endlessly in oral and written history, as well as the actual canonized St. Ilya Muromets of Pechersk, the man was born as Ilya of the village of Karacharovo near Murom, suffering from a spinal birth defect. Nearly unable to use his legs for the first 33 years of his life, always lounging above his family’s Russian stove for warmth; however - at the same age as Jesus upon his Crucifixion in the religious interpretation, long after the Christianization of the Kievan Rus - Ilya’s pleas, consistently wishing he could defend the father, to the Lord were answered one morning. While resting atop the stove, a couple of traveling pilgrims entered his home, seeking water and food for their travels, but with Ilya unable to move his legs to help them, they curiously stated that if he flexed his legs and believed he could walk, he could; and so he did, now healed and stronger than any man in the fields. Sometimes interpreted as disguised angels descending upon Karacharovo to aid Ilya, the realization of this miracle immediately drove Ilya to serve the fatherland: taking up the sword against highwaymen and invaders, traveling to Vladimir I’s court for his deads, or taking up arms against the Huns, depending on each folk and canonized story. In the folklorist account, Ilya rode to Vladimir I, becoming a soldier, and later, a royal-guard (“bogatyr”) of the fatherland, valiantly defending the Kievan Rus and its people from highwaymen, invaders, and great beasts. His feats and accolades were the lifeblood of his character, circulated by the people for centuries in all mediums of art, from songs and oral tales of old across Eastern Europe to film, animation, and games worldwide today. No Slavic folklore is more merited than this selfish warrior, whose tenacious valor and vigor has grown emblematic of the fortitude of the Slavic peoples for millennia, blending several warrior-knight stories together into the painting of bogatyr Ilya Muromets.


The path towards Avernus in the Dead Sea.

Correlating the followup operation against Avernus, no link can be directly drawn to a specific venture, but Angelia had quoted the inscription in Knight at the Crossroads, illustrating the bogatyr’s courage before certain death. As a retainer of Kievan Rus and the Lord in various retellings, the unbridled determination of the leader of the bogatyrs reflects that of Angelia’s lifelong tenacity and the Commander’s service, unshaken as G&K marched into the shadow of death. Foretold and elated that he would defend the fatherland, Ilya’s many stories have become embedded in Slavic culture, usually symbolized by the defense of their homeland against all its in invaders, and as it were, the operation planned by Angelia was the stake through Paradeus’ heart, driven by those unwavering few Soviets willing to sacrifice everything, including their lives, to defend humanity. Even in the canonized story of St. Muromets, the man dedicated himself wholly to his fellows, later falling in battle despite his confirmed spinal defect, discovered during the exhumation of his body in 1988. Notably, the symbol of Muromets defending the Rus hinterlands echoes today through the Russian Border Service of the FSB, obviously serving to defend Russia domestically. Although Angelia’s quote doesn’t tell us much on her specific strategy, the inscription likely holds significance to Zelinsky and Old Misha, who no doubt seek safe passage for the former’s old friend and prodigy, leading to a collaborative effort between G&K, the Soviet Air Forces, and presumably, StateSec. The followup to Operation Aeneas was twofold: Operation Ilya Muromets - a coordinated ground offensive on Avernus with two primary objectives, saving Angelia and capturing William, gathering intelligence along the way; and Operation Kriemhild - the evacuation and subsequent strategic bombing of Avernus by a flight of Tu-160s, Ruslan II among them, from the VVS, whose unnamed commander is a staunch loyalist and ally of Zelinsky and Misha. Unfortunately, the majority of the prep work leading up to Muromets and Kriemhild is withheld from the story, leaving us to our own devices, so specific details may appear exactly as they are. From what’s understood, there were three prerequisites for Chapter 3 siege: the transfer of AR18, the logistics and communications between G&K and StateSec, and an agreement to conduct Soviet sorties into Germany to facilitate Kriemhild.

How AR18 arrived in G&K after her sacrifice during LS is unexplained, but there’s strong reason to believe G&K retrieved her body, core, or both during E&S. Concluding her skirmish against Amaris on neutral terms, Aliana returned to G&K with SCR, where she was assigned as the captain of Griffin’s new Daybreak Squadron, in memoriam of Aliana’s former team and symbolic of the glimmering sheen of G&K’s blades that pierces through the darkness for the dawn of a new world. This new Daybreak was composed of Aliana, SCR, M249, M26MASS, Contender, and M60, possibly including M82A1 - all equipped with American or NATO-allied firearms. Earlier in E&S, they were sent to Berlin Hauptbahnhof under the orders of "riot control", truthfully sent to retrieve confidential cargo from an inbound transport train. Likely expedited by the Stasi and StateSec, the Commander managed to facilitate the squadron’s permissions for police work, allowing them to enter and secure the station, which was in active-lockdown following terrorist attacks, presumably carried out by Paradeus and Carter’s rebels against G&K’s mobilization during “Project Igor”. After securing the station, the team began searching through the cargo, believed to be covert arms and equipment ships from StateSec to G&K in Berlin. Following the discovery of multiple enemy explosives, Aliana rushed into the blazing car, where she confirmed the status of a specific crate, then she contacted the Commander to report the fate of "Poludnitsa", stroking the crate as if it were a “coffin”. The only thing left was the "meteorite", likely being "Poludnitsa's" body/core. 

Poludnitsa is a spirit or wraith known as the Midday/Noonday Lady who drifts along the toiled fields in various Slavic myths (in Russian: Полудница), and during Operation Eclipse, Instructor Я/Lyudmila Pavlichenko's route and team was codenamed "Noonday Star". Noonday Star was tasked with transporting the "Grand Duke" encrypted military command channel through undercover civilian pathways, culminating in the clandestine operation on the Intercontinental Train "Future". After the Future’s derailment, Noonday Star - i.e., Instructor Я/Lyudmila - valiantly sacrificed herself to guide Ruslan II's strikes using IR beacons against approaching rebel forces. The crate's codename and Aliana's solemn respect towards it all but confirm it to contain what's left of Lyudmila's (“Poludnitsa”) body, core, or both (“Meteorite”). Another small snippet comes after Aliana's team returns to base, wherein the Commander mentions that "Miss Zoya is under Griffin's protection." Zoya - i.e., A545 - is the name of one of the six Dolls who participated in Operation Eclipse; however, it's unclear what team Zoya was attached to, with LS’ first ranking map not being much help, as Lyudmila is listed as “Midnight Star” on that map. Zoya probably was assigned to Morning Star or Evening Star, which were intercepted over Kaliningrad (transport helicopter) and west of Lviv (armored convoy), respectively. Morning Star's helicopter was shot down over Kaliningrad around 19:10 local time, and Evening Star's convoy was intercepted near Lviv by Paradeus-Ultranationalist forces around 21:07; by 21:23, OPFOR confirmed the convoy was eliminated, narrowing down the search for the Grand Duke to either the Future or another train near Kraków. 


Instructor Я-Lyudmila Pavlichenko stands atop the derailed Future as
the Tu-160 Ruslan II flies over.

From the Commander's words and the mission of Aliana's team, it seems Zoya either survived Operation Eclipse or her body and core was successfully smuggled into Berlin with Instructor Я/Lyudmila; furthermore, despite Lyudmila’s memories being preserved in Erma Hume’s Summer Garden neural cloud, we cannot be sure if AR18 during Operation Ilya Muromets was a backup prior to Eclipse or if Erma managed to acquire those memories and transfer them into AR18’s new/repaired body. Given the dissolution of the Summer Garden mansion, Erma acted as if she’d need to search for those lost memories again, but this isn’t conclusive. Maggie Ponzi - whose neural cloud collapsed after the prolonged, strenuous electronic warfare battle on LVLII against Tareus - returned in SS, however, managing communications between the Muromets Conference Room with Erma prior to zero-hour, so perhaps Erma had accessed those backups and restored AR18 and Maggie, still lacking a physical body.

As for the communications between StateSec and the VVS, the unnamed VVS Commander is a known ally of the loyalist faction, coming to the aid of StateSec-sponsored-or-supported operations - Paldiski, S09, the Future, and aptly, the Dead Sea. Considering bomber support came after Witkin called Misha to inform him of Carter playing his hand against the Soviet border, it’s likely the case that Zelinsky, Misha, and the VVS Commander are closely entangled, unified in their support of G&K. To facilitate Kriemhild, however, mutual collaboration between the Soviet loyalists still wouldn’t permit a strategic bombing sortie on German soil, especially when tensions have escalated in Frankfurt between the pro- and anti-Rossartrist factions amid strife nationwide. While tenuous, something he’d likely be scrutinized by the Bundestag and German Council for, GDR Minister of Defense Heinrich Schweinsteiger has been walking a tightrope between sides, trying to preserve Germany and the MoD’s image while appealing to Oberstein’s faction. Theoretically, Schweinsteiger may have given the Soviets the greenlight to conduct the sorties, hypothetically masked as some sort of overseas training exercise in the expanse of the Contaminated Zone. This explanation feels tenuous at best, but airspace permissions must’ve been granted for Kriemhild, unless the bombers’ approach was deliberately hidden through the Contaminated Zone, circumnavigating the GDR government and military; however, such an intrusive method would surely draw the ire of some German centrists and nationalists. Furthermore, if this were an unsanctioned operation in Germany, radar likely would return their cross-section, but it’s unclear to what degree of interference the wavelength would be subjected to in the Contaminated Zone, potentially degrading into indecipherable noise in high-density regions. Nevertheless, ensuring Kriemhild’s secrecy would prove a daunting task, and Occam’s Razor suggests StateSec and the VVS collaborated with Riefenstahl of the Stasi and Schweinsteiger of the MoD, possibly a token of gratitude to the Commander for escorting him safely to Berlin Airport during FP.

In the later "Project Igor" preparations for Operation Ilya Muromets & Kriemhild, additional StateSec and Stasi support was received by the Commander in the form of air traffic control and aerial support echelons, presumably from the VVS to ensure Kriemhild’s success. From what's understood, QBU191 - codenamed “Ibis” and a likely former squadmate of No. 9 (QBZ191) - was seemingly assigned as an intermediary or liaison officer between the Commander, StateSec, and the VVS, continuously monitoring conditions and updating the Commander on the position and readiness of the bombers. During Operation Muromets, as the weather, visibility, and battlefield conditions were proved amicable, the command center informed the Commander that Kriemhild was initiated, ticking down to zero-hour from ten minutes. Tangentially, if QBU191 was No. 9’s former squadmate, then she might’ve come to her old friend’s aid, whose whereabouts remain unknown after Mona held off Nemhran while No. 9 and Rhino fled to the Western Tower. Hypothetically, No. 9 could’ve escaped or managed to request support after she and Rhino broke away, but only circumstantial evidence places QBU191, as No. 9’s possible former squadmate, as coming to her aid. Once the Commander gave the order to the Muromets squadrons to evacuate, an additional confirmation message was sent to QBU191, telling her that the cipher key will be activated upon zero-hour, to which she said her thanks for everything the Commander had done until this point to ensure the operation’s success.


Stasi-sponsored Nitrogen Squadron during Operation Aeneas (Mona, Rhino, and No. 9)

Once Angelia and William were secured, though the former was presumed KIA by the misinformed G&K, the joint operation moved into phase two: Operation Kriemhild. White swans descended into view, releasing their payload upon Avernus like Michael’s sword upon the Dragon, erupting into a volcanic, billowing inferno that shrouded the towers as they crashed into the Earth, all while the souls bound in Niflhel, like the locusts of Abaddon, were unsealed from the abyssal Lake. The Griffin Dolls boarded the jeeps to return to MBV Elmo, and the desecrated Avernus - once standing as a testament of technological Relic progress, built upon demonic foundations of sanguine ingenuity - sank below the horizon in the mirrors. Only then did the rain return to the Dead Sea, falling inside the jeeps. 


RO635 carries M4 SOPMODII away from Avernus during Operation Kriemhild - October 2064

Named after the protagonistic princess in the Middle High German epic Nibelungenlied, operational command shifted to the ATC echelons and the VVS, with QBU191 coordinating with the Commander for the bombardment of Avernus once the weather improved and the cipher key was activated. Set approximately in the 5th century, in the epic - among the most respected poems in German and Norse history, as Nordic variations exist, including within Snorri’s Prose Edda - Kriemhild was the unwed sister of the Burgundian King Gunther, left without a lover out of fear of an alleged prophecy that foretold the collapse of the family kingdom. When Siegfried - a honored warrior prince that earned his share and sword from the Nibelungen treasure for his feats, slaying a dragon (Fafnir in Norse variations) in his ventures - rode into Worms, the capital of Burgundy, he wished to win the hand of the princess, but Gunther wouldn’t accept the knight’s proposal to give his sister away until he paid something in return: Brünhild (Brynhildr in Norse), possibly a warrior princess (a Valkyrie in Norse) beyond Burgundy. For Siegfried to take Kriemhild’s hand, he had to woo Brünhild to Gunther, but after a series of tumultuous disagreements and feuds between parties over the proposals and Nibelungen hoard, Brünhild grew wary of Siegfried, working with Hagen, Gunther’s vassal, to turn the blade against Siegfried. The Burgundians, especially Kriemhild, were actually rather fond of the warrior, but Hagen’s incessancy for his king forced Gunther’s hand with Brünhild, permitting Siegfried to be slain by Hagen, who used Kriemhild’s kindness against her to reveal Siegfried’s weakness.

When Kriemhild learned of her lover’s demise, hatred of her brother festered within, slowly driving her away from the kingdom, where she later married the Hun king Etzel, knocking the first domino of prophecy over. For a time, relations were neutral between the Hun and Burgundian kings, but Kriemhild’s innocence continued eroding into darkness, eternally spiteful of Hagen for murdering Siegfried and Gunther for permitting it. And in the second act, Kriemhild, now Queen of the Huns and mother to Ortlieb, invited Gunther to Etzel’s court under the guise of mutual celebration, where she would ultimately exact her revenge years later. The masquerade fell following an exchange, possibly instigated intentionally, that turned violent between Hun and Burgundian men outside the court, where in a rage, Hagen, present with Gunther and wary of Kriemhild’s intentions in the first place, decapitated Ortlieb as revenge in front of everyone, immediately sparking a slaughter that stained the halls red. In the end, only Gunther and Hagen remained among the Burgundians, who were captured and imprisoned for a time while Kriemhild prepared her retribution, now totally possessed to avenge her former betrothed and now-descreated son. As a show of force and Kriemhild’s ruthlessness, she had Gunther decapitated by Siegfried’s sword, Balmung; thereafter, she personally presented her brother’s head to Hagen, demanding the location of the Nibelungen treasure and readying Balmung against his nape. And so too did Hagen lose his head, but the grim sight of Kriemhild’s sanguinity drove one of Etzel's surviving knights, Hildebrand, to cut down the woman, fulfilling the prophesied collapse of the Burgundian-Nibelungen line.

In the context of SS, the operation’s naming scheme could have two possible meanings: A - the final decapitation operation against Paradeus, exacting vengeance against Avernus for its atrocities over the past thirteen years as Kriemhild did to Gunther and Hagen; or B - the destruction of Avernus as Hildebrand did to Kriemhild, delivering the decisive, watershed blow against the witch. Both represent a similar theme of vengeance, but for whom the naming scheme is meant to reflect isn’t certain, perhaps simply a nod to the violent end of the Burgundian-Nibelungens through the lens of Paradeus. Still, if the operation is meant to represent Kriemhild's retribution against the wrongdoers, sacrificing her humanity in the process as Meitner and William have, who's to say Paradeus’ Hildebrand isn't waiting to return the favor against G&K? If William’s alleged plan bears fruit, this may very well be the case.

Hervör & Ráðgríðr
During Fe56’s SSE of Avernus Data Core, containing several Level 30 floors of the Eastern Tower, the group entered the monitoring and surveillance room located on Level 32, the same room the NUSSR dossier was discovered. Evidence of constant, rapid data destruction was visibly apparent: destroyed filing boxes, said to be “destroyed in the previous skirmish”, innumerable scattered files that were impossible to sort before Kriemhild, and computers with recently-wiped drives. After discovering the dossier, Dreamer attempted to access one of the computers, mentioning signs of prior electronic infiltration to the server, while most of the files were corrupt, meaning significant portions of the intelligence files - Hervör, Ráðgríðr, and an additional file depicting the conversation between Morridow and the M4A1-Lunasia entity in PR - were missing. After some time of data recovery, Dreamer was able to query some residual data from the server.

The first intelligence file, dated October 2064 - set between MS and FP - and titled “Hervör”, came from a White Nyto’s camera inside a hospital. Shot in Moscow City Hospital No. 31, the short video captured a nurse, sent by the director, jogging down the Block 12 corridor to inform Dr. Jenokov that patient 206 was ready to be cleaned and taken care of, and after the nurse departed, the Nyto seized the opportunity, stabbing Jenokov in the chest with her scythe and hiding the body. There, she gave a quick mission report, confirming her infiltration and the target’s location: Room 402, Block 12 - just down the hall. At 10AM, her operation began, darting from her hiding spot to Room 402, then stopping just short of the door. A few knocks are heard, followed by Kalina’s voice on the other side, telling her “doctor” or “nurse” to please come in, then the video ends. From this very short excerpt, it would seem Kalina was kidnapped from her hospital room recently, likely to be used as a bargaining chip against the Commander and G&K, though the terms of this bargain are anyone’s guess.

With William’s capture at the end of SS, she may end up as collateral to negotiate his release or another outcome, likely related to events soon to play out in Frankfurt. The operation must’ve occurred very recently, as news of Kalina’s kidnapping no doubt would’ve spread to G&K in Berlin and their associates in Moscow within days, hinting at a contingency formulated for William’s release, given his presence during Operation Ilya Muromets suggests he voluntarily surrendered to G&K; however, the circumstances are delicate, and barring a scenario in which either side’s lives were seriously threatened or ended, the other wouldn’t act, stonewalling any chance of negotiation. Moreover, if William’s only contingency for his release is Kalina, it’s a rather cheap shot, easily botched if G&K or their allies could gain the upper hand, and to tack onto this, the deactivation of the Evangel Axis implies the loss of authority over Nytos; therefore, assuming Kalina was held elsewhere by Nytos and that Avernus was the sole control center of Nyto Consciousness, a predicament arises in which her captors garner agency, no longer bound by the Evangel’s influence on their consciousnesses. On the other hand, if Kalina is also held by Carter’s ultranationalists, however, then the Commander is still subject to William’s leverage, but to gamble his entire life - at least, this body’s life - on Kalina’s confinement is a foolish, easily foiled effort, unless he was absolutely certain Kalina would not, under any circumstances, be found or saved before William could be handed over.

Nevertheless, the Stasi, StateSec, and the Prometheans wouldn’t accept William’s escape over a single girl’s life; bluntly said, though of course they’d want to see her safe return, Kalina isn’t collateral to dissuade G&K, nor would aforementioned parties avoid intervening to facilitate his capture - too much rides on his identity and technology. An alternative to this is the idea that Kalina isn’t William’s collateral, but leverage against the Commander to relinquish their operation and mission, orchestrated by the higher ups to ensure William’s induction among the powers that be, though this idea still suffers from the same “Is Kalina worthy enough as collateral?” question. The epiphany would no doubt ripple among G&K, but would they so easily hand over William or cease everything to save Kalina’s life? There are only a few certainties: they’d never allow Kalina to die, self-evident by her existence in GFL2, nor would the Commander falter at the 11th hour to when victory was in sight. If Paradeus, the ultranationalists, or say, the Prometheans are willing to do anything for William’s return, then Kalina alone may not be enough; it hypothetically could be enough to dissuade G&K, but the Prometheans have their sights squarely set on Paradeus’ technology, possibly even working with Meitner towards the formation of the URNC. Although Lyons and the Council do not seem this overtly malicious, though William’s capture may force their hands, perhaps Kalina’s capture was a collaborative agreement with William, Meitner, or both to avert G&K’s future intervention, reduce the Commander’s influence, and of course, save William. The last possibility, however, would seem to not necessarily be the case, especially if Meitner’s final surgery in Avernus was conducted on William.

As for the name of the file, Hervör, it’s eponymous with the warrior maiden of the same name in Snorri’s Hervarar saga ok Heidreks - a major poem within the Prose Edda, detailing the family story of the berserker king Angantýr to his great grandchildren, forever haunted by an accursed sword. Forged and enchanted by the legendary dwarves Durin and Dvalinn, who were held by King Svafrlami, Týrfingr was the universal symbol of this story - a family heirloom passed down each generation, cursed with destined bloodshed. The sword, enchanted by Dvalinn, was cursed so that when unsheathed, all were mortally wounded by its edge, no matter the severity, nor could it be resheathed until blood was spilled. The original wielder of this blade, King Svafrlami was killed by Angantýr’s father, Arngrim, who bestowed his son the blade upon his death. Later, King Angantýr and his berserker brothers fell in battle against King Hjalmar - but not before delivering a blow from Týrfingr against Hjalmar - on the real-world Danish isle of Samsø (Samsey), located in the Samsø Bælt, east of Jutland. Angantýr’s daughter, Hervör, was too young to truly know her father and family lineage when he died, instead sent to live with her maternal grandfather, Jarl Bjarmar, until she learned of her father and his fate. Laid to rest in a mound on Samsø, Hervör wished to reclaim her “birthright” from her father as heir apparent, as she never truly “fit” in with the manner in which she was raised, preferring the ways of the sword, shield, and bow. After a violent incident as a highwayman, Hervör was dragged back to the Court, where she learned from the Jarl and his men of the truth hidden from her: she was the daughter of Angantýr, wielder of Týrfingr and slayer of Hjalmar. Now driven towards Samsø, Hervör left her homeland, took up the mantle of men’s gear and weapons, and joined a band of vikings, now under the pseudonym Hervard. After some time, the captain of the viking crew died, and Hervard took his stead, sailing directly to Samsø to acquire the blade. In the Eddic Hervararkviða, part of the wider saga, Samsø was believed to be an accursed isle, and when their ship landed, none but Hervör walked ashore, discovering the mound of her ancestors. Before the mound, Angantýr’s spirit in Hel spoke to her, ordering her to cease her incessancy for the sword, as Týrfingr was in Hel where it should remain, but once her obstinacy was made clear, Angantýr reluctantly returned the blade to the mortal world, warning Hervör to treat it with utmost respect, as its properties would only shed more blood. For the rest of Hervör’s life, she did as he requested, later bearing two sons Angantýr (after her father) and Heidrekr, who became the protagonist king of the Heidreks saga. Heidrekr’s children, Hervör (after his mother), Angantýr (after his grandfather), and their Hun half-brother, Hlödr, feuded after Heidrekr’s death, spurned by Odin. Sister Hervör fell against the Hlödr’s Hun army, and in the climactic battle, Hlödr was defeated by Angantýr, cyclically wielding Týrfingr.

How exactly the Eddic saga relates to Kalina is left to the reader, and it may be as simple as the writers using a mythical Norse fitting in motif to Norse Hela; however, the importance behind naming schemes are usually significant in some manner, especially in later story arcs. As a woman who broke from tradition to pursue that which was hers by birthright, joining the likes of great men and kings, Hervör’s unwavering - at times, violent - determination towards Týrfingr, characterized etymologically by her name, may be about Kalina’s commitment and compassion for G&K and the Commander, though this reading is very much a stretch. She’s never once given up on us or the circumstances, always standing side-by-side through G&K’s darkest hours, and considering her limited experience, perhaps Hervör’s self-motivated proficiency in combat reflects through Kalina. As said, there’s no direct link one could immediately draw between Kalina and Hervör, but as resolute warrior women of strong mind who’ve stared Hell in the face and returned, perhaps some comparison can be drawn. Furthermore, as these intelligence files came from Paradeus, perhaps Kalina’s filename was named as such to demarcate her service from S09 to Paldiski. Inversely, Hervör’s reclamation of Týrfingr inadvertently ushered in an accursed chain of events in the lineage, and maybe Kalina’s capture marks the first domino to fall in a crucial scheme against G&K.

The second intelligence file, dated October 2064 - set between MS and FP - and titled “Ráðgríðr”, depicted a video file of Shadowless’ private report to an unknown party, possibly Paradeus or another intelligence service working against them. While segments were corrupted in playback, Shadowless is seen setting up her camera, then sits in a chair centered in frame to begin her report. Visibly nervous, probably hinting at hesitancy for her words, Shadowless stated that all information to and from “the TV station” - likely referring to her news agency, Deutscher Fernsehfunk and its newscast, Aktuelle Kamera, eponymous with the real-life, state-run news station in the GDR during the Cold War - was vetted for any potentially “disadvantageous information”, excluding such stories from airing. Moreover, she also established a private news channel that garnered its projected viewership, enabling “all avenues for voicing public opinion” to fall under the control of Shadowless’ bosses, perpetuating whatever narrative they wished to paint publicly. Such information control greatly aided the censorship surrounding a certain “Dr. Alecia’s” death, possibly a Galatea researcher or whistleblower, redirecting public opinion against Galatea’s alleged involvement in the incident, presumably her death. Much of the latter end of the report was corrupted, including any further information about Dr. Alecia, so little can be stated as fact. Afterwards, Shadowless explained that her private radio station’s positive listener base would only hear the reports concerning information that cannot be publicly disclosed in official channels, presumably referring to redacted stories from the state media. Resulting from the corruption, it’s unclear if Shadowless is actively complacent in Galatea’s censorship campaign or is undermining Galatea’s influence through private channels, leaking stories to the public that otherwise would’ve been scrubbed forever; however, considering Shadowless’ report was directed towards a certain group, with the video discovered in Avernus’ Data Core, the video alludes to her complacency in Paradeus-Galatea’s surveillance and propaganda programs, thus implicating her as a Paradeus asset embedded in German state media. On the other hand, Shadowless may have been forced into this position, working under orders of her bosses to redact adverse stories to Galatea’s narrative, while truthfully working clandestinely against them to investigate Light’s death; Kevin cared for the young man immensely, so there’s no doubt that his elder sister Shadowless, eponymously someone who’d dive into a nightmare to expose the truth, would dig endlessly until those responsible were brought to justice.

The title of this file possibly provides some context: mentioned briefly in the Eddic poem Grímnismál, written within Snorri’s Prose Edda, Ráðgríðr was one of the Valkyries named in Valhalla, said to pass around ale to the warriors in its halls. Other than this singular mention, there’s virtually zero information about this warrior maiden besides the etymology of her name. After almost a millennia of oral and written translations and interpretations of Snorri’s works from Old Norse to modern English, a one-to-one translation isn’t feasible, but most interpretations are unified in similar meanings. Ráðgríðr is a conjugate of the Old Norse “Ráð” (Rand/Rad), meaning peace, council(or), truce, [fair] reason, or well-thought planning - indicative of one who consuls level-headedness amid conflict; and “Gríðr” (Gird/Grith), meaning aspiration, eagerness, fervency, or determination. In short, Ráðgríðr is the ambitious Valkyrie of reason - a “headstrong advisor of truces” or “zealous councilor or planner (or dove) of peace”, if you will; however, other interpretations include Ráðgríðr’s vehemence against reason, rather than a broker of peace and reason, but having only been named in passing in the Prose Edda, remarkably little can be gleaned about this enigmatic individual. It may be simple as MICA just using a Valkyrie’s name to correlate to the motif of Norse myth throughout the event, but the series’ naming schemes are usually significant, especially in the later arcs of the story. From the two scenarios, Shadowless working for Paradeus-Galatea or her undermining their media campaign internally, two connotations of Ráðgríðr may piece this puzzle. First, if Shadowless has been compromised, occurring sometime between Light’s death in late September and before Operation Aeneas in early October, then perhaps Shadowless is ironically now casting a figurative veil over negative press, vehemently working against reason and peace. If so, perhaps Paradeus-Galatea’s operatives and objects are codenamed after Norse myth, such as Hela, Ráðgríðr, Hervör, and Iðunn. Inversely, if Shadowless is seeking the truth of Light’s death, then akin to Ráðgríðr, her zealous pursuit of the truth is symbolic of seeking peace within and justice against the guilty; that is to say, by exposing Paradeus-Galatea’s crooked work through private channels - working alongside a certain party she was delivering this report to, possibly the Stasi, StateSec, the Rossartrists, or another federal investigative agency - this disclosure gradually brings the perpetrators to the light. 

Lastly, regarding the status of the servers in the Avernus Data Core, Dreamer mentioned there were signs of prior electronic intrusion as she was attempting to recover scrubbed data. Beforehand, Fe56 mentioned the room was trashed after the last skirmish, which Occam’s Razor says it was either the Wolf Pack, Daybreak, or Taraxum responsible for the chaos, but a less likely, yet more interesting possibility is that of Black Box or RO635 and Koleda during and after Operation Aeneas. Given the Hervör, Ráðgríðr, and M4A1-Lunasia entity files were all that were recovered, the signs of intrusion put the veracity of the information presented into jeopardy, as we cannot be sure the respective events happened as they appear in playback. The whereabouts of Black Box, composing M16A1 and Beak, after Operation Aeneas are unknown, though we know the duo pulled out sometime after M16A1 encountered RPK16 in the Western Tower laboratory; as for Beak, however, there are no clues about where she went, as she wasn’t there to support M16A1 during her skirmish with M16A1, perhaps implying Beak and later M16A1 were tasked with intelligence gathering from Avernus’ Data Core for StateSec and Witkin’s faction. On the other hand, after Angelia returned to consciousness and informed the Commander of her plans against Paradeus, she issued Koleda and RO635 orders to expedite the Ilya Muromets, suggesting they were to surveil and sabotage certain sectors of the structure. Perhaps one of them - or theoretically, RPK16 - hacked into the server to muster everything possible; RPK16, after all, is implied to be Lyons’ dangle embedded in Avernus, with the Prometheans and StateSec no doubt invested in Paradeus intelligence. None of this justifies the idea of this information being deliberately left behind for G&K to find, unless they could only recover traces of expunged data, preserving it for Fe56’s SSE. Opposite to this is the idea that this information was deliberately left behind by William to mislead the Commander into a vulnerable position advantageous to him and his associates, hence uncertainty of Kalina’s predicament and Shadowless’ loyalties in media. Regardless, Dreamer’s offhand comment on electronic intrusion raises some eyebrows on the source and veracity of these intelligence files.

Olympian Emancipation

Until We Have No Choice

Angelia stares into her reflection in the White Room’s walls.

After an extended tenure in the Lake of Cognition, Angelia’s consciousness miraculously returned to her body, using 2051 Blackwell’s “key” to open the “Door” to reality, similar to Amaris’ Door of the greater Dog Tag System, created by Meitner and the Daybreak researchers, with Amaris’ Door and Aliana’s Dog Tag “Collection” embodying the earliest design of the Lake-Evangel System, wherein the memory fragments of its subjects are stored behind the sealed Door. Once Koleda and RO635 were presumably sent away by Angelia, RPK16, dressed in the same white Paradeus robes, approached her seemingly subconsciously, communicating directly between individual consciousnesses to offer an ultimatum. The longer one's mind exists in the Lake, the more it becomes gnarled into an amalgamation of memory fragments used for consciousness synthesis as the singular consciousness begins shattering. At the end of Chapter 2, the remnant of 2051 Blackwell used her final effort of existence to assist Angelia’s escape from the Lake, reemerging in her body.

Notably, when RPK16 assumed control as “her” body’s active consciousness, the reflection in the window of the White Room showed two organic arms, and when Judge of Fe56 discovered a discarded, bloody tissue, tuckered between the cracks, DNA analysis confirmed it to be Angelia’s, with additional analysis discovering trace amounts of prosthetic lubricants. Paradeus absolutely has the capacity to replace limbs or graft synthetic skin over prosthetics, such as the “human” forms of Gray, Bramedb, and Morridow, none of whom were suspected until their Nyto augmentations were unsheathed; in which case, there’s two primary possibilities: either Angelia had her left arm replaced or reconstructed, granting her an indistinguishable bionic; or a clone body was made from Angelia’s, though this is unlikely, considering she returned of her own agency to her body in the White Room, which possessed the telltale scars of her life. Furthermore, another question remains about the currently-inexplicable yellow eyes motif across virtually every high-ranking Nyto but Sana. Interestingly, if the character artworks are canonical, then the color of certain Nytos’ irises can change, with Morridow and Gray having light-brown or hazel and Bramedb with a shade of red, all reverting to yellow irises in their Nyto “forms”. Could they symbolize an innate independence from humanity, glares piercing like an owl - physical embodiments of the eponym of the “Nyto” portmanteau, representing the “Tyto”, or owl genus. Just as the Athena’s Owl name in Berlin would suggest, owls have long-since been staples of wisdom and foresight, emblematic of their fantastic piercing gaze, so perhaps the writers follow the same trend, reflecting Paradeus’ guiding wisdom and foresight towards a brave new world.

None of the subordinate Nytos shimmer with the same glare, sharing washed-out irises, but not the Abandoned Isomers, reflecting a sort of crimson shade. The exception to this, however, is Nimogen, mothballed in Tallinn after her failure in Belgrade; it may be nothing more than creative design choice for the high-ranking Nytos, but the emphasized purple-eyed girls speak volumes of importance on the relation of eye color and Paradeus. An unanswered mystery we’ll continue carrying into the future; however, there could be something to be said for Noel of the “Three Goddesses” Project, who also possesses radiant yellows, though this could easily be handwoven, for there’s no precedent for the Goddesses’ eyes. Lunasia has never been revealed, while Jefuty possesses brilliant blues, theoretically deriving from her birth mother. Although entirely speculative, the yellow irises may emerge as a “side effect”, so to speak, of consciousness synthesis into their original body or another, and further, Nyto modifications and Hela potentially involve invasive procedures to all parts of the body, with brain-specific operations possibly affecting the eyes, though eye color derives from the eye itself, not the brain. However, a significant caveat in this theory is the fact that not all Nytos have yellow eyes, such as the rank-and-file Nytos and Sana, though the latter has some justification for her eye color, given she originally was reborn in the image of Meitner’s daughter. Brilliantly radiant as they are, the yellow eyes motif may be nothing more than a stylistic choice, but the main writers have been known for their consistent use of recurring symbology and initially minor comments vastly expanded with later context. Generally, Angelia’s body in Chapter 2 is most likely her original, though the possibility of cloning cannot be entirely discounted, as there’s dozens of hours of missing time from Fixed Point to Slow Shock; however, RPK16 and Koleda remained at her side much of the time, so there would be rather little time, unless Koleda left the White Room amid the surgery, for a swap to occur. Not to mention, according to Meitner’s postoperative notes on Angelia, she was reportedly transported back to her cell after her procedure and acute symptoms of limited Hela rejection.

As for RPK16’s emergence, there’s cause for speculation on the purpose of RPK16’s Nyto-Doll modifications and Meitner’s procedure on Angelia - whether or not the emergence was a part of her wider research on collective unconsciousness and RPK16’s requests. This may be her original body but modified to harbor both minds or a cloned body created for it, though, as previously stated, the latter is significantly unlikely. Currently from what’s understood, the body now consists of two minds, that of Angelia and RPK16, and when Angelia emerged from the Lake with Blackwell’s aid, her lowly body was clinging to the edge, having its former host soul torn from its shell, narrowly avoiding biological brain death as her body withered and mind dissociated. From Blackwell’s testimony, only the consciousnesses of the recently deceased - or more specifically, biologically alive brains - can be transferred to the Lake after their Hela procedure, of which the subject expires from the procedure or has their consciousness extracted in the moment before death, as cracks spread across the foundation upholding the brain and metaphysical mind. She had already physically died, but her mind lived on, faintly returning her consciousness to this world. Just returning to the body after 12+ hours of dissociation Lake, she found herself in dire straits, and RPK16 keenly understood this as well; there was no ending in which Angelia could carry her body and mind out of Avernus, as she was still far too weak. As her mind started to slipped into darkness once more, RPK approached with a proposition: in the words of Martha Meitner, "If everything is life is pointless, then what is the point in struggling?" - Angelia, a warrior of obstinate justice, chose to struggle until she had no choice, aligning young Anna’s statement to Aliana in the Lake, “I will answer this question with my entire life.”

RPK16 rationalized her to become her, gaining her memories and thoughts, by taking control as their torchbearer to their promised land. She's quite blunt when mentioning she’ll “get Angelia to the destination" and that she should "leave the rest of the journey to me." As Angelia's mind slipped away, she used the very last of her strength - physical or mental - to reach out for RPK16's hand, wordlessly stating her acceptance. RPK16’s consciousness took control and Angelia's own slipped down to a lower level or returned to the Lake. Overall, the best answer to the overarching story of RPK-Angelia is simply “It's complicated." At the end of Chapter 2 of Slow Shock, Angelia awoke in white torture room - commonly used for sensory deprivation to induce states of confusion, madness, amnesia, and anhedonia in prisoners, potentially inflicting lifelong mental damage - that, theoretically, may have been employed by Paradeus to erode a subject’s consciousness as they dissociate or panic, possibly aiming to “degrade”, if you will, a Hela subject’s mind for their later procedure(s). After speaking with RPK/Pandora's consciousness, seemingly in her own consciousness or through a conscious link. Beforehand, Angelia's consciousness was just barely clinging to our world after escaping the Lake, given her mind had already been shattered then delivered back to her body once, recursively inducing constant strain on her mind and body. The initial stage of all of this was the Hela procedure, wherein memory fragments are extracted from the patient and implanted into the Lake as a foundational blueprint of one’s consciousness. In the past, this operation could only be performed on the recently-deceased, but newer subjects apparently can survive Hela, however, the invasive neural trauma from the surgery, including the drugs used, may kill the patient anyway if their mind or body rejects Hela. A significant percentage of individuals will likely reject Hela, expiring from the biological symptoms, brain death, etc. The exact Hela procedure is intentionally vague, but it involves direct dissection of the brain to extract memories and transfer them, somehow, to the Lake of Cognition, seemingly external to our world, with the Evangel Axis nodes as the sole physical “connection” to the central Axis, located at the bottom of the Lake.

When Angelia escaped, she was weak. She had already "died" once, and all that bound her to this world was sheer fortitude; however, that was not enough to see things through to the end. RPK16 came to Ange, forcibly revealing the criticality of Angelia’s condition, offering a radical solution for salvation - one of immense cost, yet no alternative. RPK16 understood well that Angelia was incapable of carrying her mind or body to the end, but if someone else took the reins as her body’s active consciousness, sacrificing Angelia’s autonomy of the body, there was a path to carry both to the destination. As RPK16 put it, "You've been walking in the snowy wilderness for far too long... you've forgotten your body has already collapsed from exhaustion long ago." RPK16 - who, during Operation Aeneas, was in the opposite Tower in Avernus - was previously plugged up to a mass of cables, all of which first appeared to be part of her Nyto-Doll modifications. RPK16's voice only emerged in Angelia's consciousness after she escaped the Lake, suggesting a connection to Angelia's mind was established after Angelia's Hela operation. In fact, based on the tone of Meitner’s laboratory assistant voice, it's heavily implied RPK16 was stood by Angelia while she was under the scalpel. Given that synthesized Nyto consciousnesses differ greatly from the two instances of Nyto-modified Dolls - Maggie Ponzi & RPK16, thus far, and that she was present with Meitner during Angelia's procedure, it's feasible that RPK16's “conscious link”, if you will, to Ange was part of the experiment or an exploited opportunity by her to save Angelia by "confirming" the veracity and choices of her commander. Furthermore, RPK16 mentioned that she was witness to Angelia's mind, and even if said memories were twisted by the Lake and RPK16’s projected self, Angelia was steadfast in her beliefs - in turn, proving that she was Angelia. Adding to this is RPK16's comment about Angelia's stubbornness, saying she had already long-since forgotten her fall into the snowfield, her body succumbing to the cold.

When RPK16 appeared before Angelia’s consciousness, her phrasing made it out as if she truly wishes to save Angelia from ending her life in a futile struggle, though we cannot be certain if RPK16 has an ulterior motive, such as appeasing her Promethean backers. She explained that she'd burrow herself into Angelia's flesh, into her essence of being, taking control of her body and perhaps, even her mind. She would become Angelia: all her memories - be they twisted by the Lake and RPK16 or be truthful - her mind, her thoughts - everything about her. Curiously responding to RPK16’s offer, Angelia asked if she could truly reach there, to the destination she sought. RPK16 affirmed, explaining that, even if the first steps were filled with struggle, she would carry the burden of her heavy body - always moving forward, all the way to Angelia's place of longing. In what is perhaps the most direct comment about her intentions, RPK16 adds that she will take on her likeness in full to "take Angelia to the destination.”; Angelia's self was far too tired - she must "rest and leave the rest of the journey to me." With the last of her strength, Angelia reached out to RPK16's hand, and she understood Angelia’s answer. She would be reborn, becoming her in all ways, shouldering her burdens. This scene is followed by Angelia relinquishing control while gazing into the mirror - possibly an intentional reference to Mirror Stage, emblematic of the self-perception in the true psychological “mirror stage” - to find RPK16 returning an arched smile in return. In that moment, "I am you, and you are me." 

That said, RPK16 likely wished to save Angelia, and taking control was the only way to guarantee her body and their consciousnesses could escape alive; even in Fixed Point, when Angelia awoke after a prolonged period of unconsciousness in her prison cell - before undergoing the Hela procedure, meaning this interaction took place over 12 hours before Operation Aeneas - RPK16 told Koleda that she was “counting on you” and that she should “Take good care of her”, as Angelia was “yours now”, suggesting her care was bequeathed to Koleda. Acknowledging those orders, Angelia overheard the sound of “rustling fabric” and another voice, asking RPK16 if “you’ll be forgiven for this”, to which she responded that “I don’t seek forgiveness”, insinuating she either had no interest in the opinions of her Commander or backers, or was doing this for Angelia’s preservation, delivering her from danger, thus negating any need for forgiveness for her past actions, ultimately projected on a course for Angelia’s salvation. When steadily regaining consciousness, she was met with a peculiar Nyto, unlike the technologically avante-garde atmosphere of Avernus, “dressed in tatters, like one of those abandoned Isomers.” Koleda is all but directly confirmed to be AK12, and the deliberate description of a tattered Nyto, with sounds of rustling fabric, may point to RPK16 herself being responsible for AK12’s infiltration, as AK12 relinquished transferred DEFY’s team commands to RPK16 during the Berlin apartment attack; furthermore, Angelia overheard the fabric sound, likely the rustling of Koleda’s clothing, followed by RPK16 asking if “that should put you at ease”, perhaps implying RPK16 was dressing AK12, or another Nyto that AK12 was hacking, in “Koleda’s” clothes, so as to do how Romans do for their infiltration. Considering RPK16 herself was Lyons’ dangle into Paradeus, transmitting a message to his mail from within the tower - indirectly showing her messaging could overcome the immense electromagnetic interference of the Dead Sea, unless the Prometheans had a line of contact somewhere within Avernus - one of her objectives of her confidentially-backed-infiltration into Avernus could’ve extracting Angelia; Lyons did, after all, tell Ulrich in the Athena’s Owl that Angelia had ignored his expressed orders, landing her in that predicament, though she could’ve been given up as consultation to establish communications with William and Meitner, but he wouldn’t sit idly by, implying he too sought her return. He and those around him may have never wished her circumstances to end as poorly as they did, yet a high price is always paid for foolishness, but Lyons, despite his primary objective with Paradeus, is not an overtly malicious man.

The entire ordeal plays a similar tune to the story of Cyberpunk 2077 - more specifically, the function of the Arasaka Corporation’s “Relic” engram, a biochip that contains one's consciousness written as a construct, potentially slowly corrupting and overwriting someone else's mind when the slotted in another augmented individual. Through the “Soulkiller” program -  initially developed by legendary Night City netrunner, Alt Cunningham, then repurposed by Arasaka - an individual's consciousness is corrupted, scrambled, burnt, then transferred onto the Relic engram, stored within the Arasaka neural facility and network, "Mikoshi". Adjacent to the concept of the Lake of souls, the mikoshi is an integral part of Shinto festivals, representing regal shrine litter or palanquins of Shintoism, said to contain the subject deity of worship, carried by its adherents to and from their temples. Often mikoshi are held in revelry amid festival and cultural celebrations, lauded as deific vehicles, upheld by spiritual belief and physical strength. In Cyberpunk 2077, Arasaka created Mikoshi as their shared network for a prison of souls, bound together as neural data in its indecipherable false world, formulated and edited to refine each subject’s imprint, potentially twisting the memories of specific constructs for reasons benign and pernicious; however, Mikoshi and the Relic program were not solely created as the product of sadistic scientists seeking gratification, but the decisive answer to humanity’s holy grail: immortality - rather reminiscent the purpose of the USRA Holy Grail Project. Originally designed as a gateway - for the uber-wealthy, of course - to eternal life, the Relic program first iteration was mostly a proof-of-concept, extracting subject’s souls via Soulkiller, then storing the duplicated consciousnesses on the Relic 1.0 engram and Mikoshi, though 1.0 constructs could only communicate through electronic devices until the introduction for the watershed Relic 2.0, serving as the essential plot device ingame.

As a brief warning, the following paragraphs contain spoilers for the main story of Cyberpunk 2077, so if you’ve somehow haven’t played it and wish to remain oblivious, readers may skip to the “In Betrayal, I am Loyal” section below. During the events of 2077, the biochip was damaged after V was shot in the head by Dexter DaShawn, a prominent Night City fixer who organized the heist of the biochip. Yorinobu Arasaka, heir apparent of the Arasaka emperor, Saburo Arasaka, slipped the biochip from Arasaka Laboratories, looking to sell it to NetWatch, one of the major law enforcement corporations responsible for network security and investigations of the Old Net. When the bullet entered V's head, the biochip was activated, beginning to repair the damage dealt, thus starting the doomsday clock. With the Relic's activation, the construct on the experimental engram, Johnny Silverhand, was activated as well, initiating a slow overwrite of V's consciousness. As a whole, the plot’s focus shadows V and Johnny's relationship - first hostile and alien, then confusing and cynical, and on the edge of death, apathetic or tenacious of their individuality.

Slow Shock’s story is analogous - albeit, different in many ways - to RPK16's emergence and possession of Angelia's mind. By taking control, like Johnny, she holds the immense burden, as well as capacity for defiance, to guide Angelia and herself to either salvation or death when in control of the host’s body, introducing an interesting question from Johnny's experience - RPK16’s ethics and honesty. Even in 2077, the dubious accuracy of Johnny's memories was the result of Arasaka construct editing in Mikoshi, diffusing memories into a single construct’s eroded personality. But as RPK16 said to Angelia, if she truly believed these memories, unclear as they are, to be genuine, what difference would it make to the individual? The human personality model grows from experience and memories, no different from 2nd-generation neural clouds, and if the individual was resolute in certain belief, little can be done short of intrusive methods to shake them, simultaneously arising cynicalism and pride in memories that ultimately may not be true in Mikoshi or the Lake of Cognition. The same can be said of Angelia’s Hela procedure and RPK16’s inclusion, deliberately tweaking specific memories for Meitner’s ambitions and RPK16’s raison d'etre, peering into her past, even going as far as to change certain faces or settings to “test and verify”, so to speak, Angelia’s incorrigible personality, supposedly allowing Meitner an “opportunity to understand it all” through the lens of her disciple. Nowhere else is this ideal best presented than her repeated dialogue at the end of each memory section, probing the foundation of Angelia’s self for that apparent “spark” of determination buried within her and Angelia’s hearts, ingrained in the diametrically opposite sides of the same coin through experience and principles from Johns Hopkins to Beslan.

“No matter how many times you lose your memory, no matter how the people around you present themselves, you never change your mind. I expected nothing less from my student.”
- Professor Martha aka Hela “Laplace” Meitner

Adding more to the 2077 comparison, the specific biochip implanted by V - the experimental prototype Relic 2.0 - was being tested on biological subjects. Relic 1.0 served only for consciousness to be saved on an engram as a construct, and these 1.0 constructs were only capable of communication externally through electronic devices. The development of Relic 2.0, which had only recently entered the trial phase, was headed by Anders Hellman, who aided Yorinobu Arasaka’s plot to swap the biochip from the Relic laboratory. After Soulkiller was unleashed on the subject's mind, the AI tore their consciousness apart until it could be mounted to the Relic engram. When Hela is carried out on the subject, the invasive procedure of the brain, too, brings excessively high mortality rates, with few destitute subjects “lucky” enough for their bodies to reject and survive, such as “Rosita”. With Relic 2.0, the project team progressed from simply preserving consciousness to implanting it into new bodies as well. By 2077, previous tests were filled with failures and only partial successes, mainly among those in near-death states; the greatest success, however, came in the form of the recently-deceased, just like the Holy Grail-Hela procedure. After V was "killed" by DaShawn, they found themself resurrected, so to speak, by the Relic 2.0, which had initiated a mind repair and released the construct on the chip, starting the clock. When Relic 2.0 is activated, the construct embedded in the engram is deployed into V’s organic body, specifically the neural environment, where the chip was slotted into. The construct slowly overrides the subject's mind, and in the case of V, merging Johnny Silverhand's consciousness with V's until construct Johnny either assumed control or could be isolated and removed from V’s consciousness; not unlike RPK16 and Angelia, where RPK16 burrowed herself into Angelia's body and mind, and as an equal of Johnny, her agency grants her the same potential. Who knows what RPK16 truly wants, and despite the flipped roles in Girls Frontline, Angelia's mind has experienced many twisted memories from her  operation and brief tenure in the Lake. Like Mikoshi and the 50-year gap, we don't necessarily know what Arasaka - or in Girls Frontline, the Lake of Cognition - has done to the memories, construing and molding memories to shape a narrative. It's not a one-to-one scenario, especially with certain roles flipped between them, but an adjacency can be drawn to Cyberpunk 2077’s collective struggle for individual identity in face of those seeking to uproot and wield human spirit in a dreaded conquest of quasi-immortality. To quote Silverhand, “it’s a war against the fuckin’ forces of entropy”, signifying the ultimate result of these abhorrent experiments: an inevitable erosion and enslavement of human identity - exchanging the robbery of individuality for the pseudo-consciousnessnes from Mikoshi or the Lake, abandoning the concept of “self” for “selves”.

In Betrayal, I am Loyal

RPK-Angelia stares into her reflection in the White Room’s walls.

In the final moments of the Agent Angelia memories, RPK16 approaches Angelia amidst the darkness, telling her that she can “Only show my loyalty through betrayal”, for “I am you, when I am you”, forcibly requiring her to “prove my allegiance to my true master.” There’s a plethora of connotations to unpack, but when Angelia’s obstinacy drove them to the manor outside orders, RPK16 gave her plenty of warning towards the dangers that path would follow; and considering RPK16 is all but confirmed to be Lyons’ dangle in Avernus, perhaps RPK16 was assigned a mission by Lyons, Shaw, or the other higher-ups to expedite Angelia’s extraction at any cost, even at the immense gambit RPK16 posed to Angelia as her consciousness slowly slipped away from her body, presumably back into the Lake. When RPK16 speaks of her true master, she likely speaks of Lyons and the Council, serving as an informant within Paradeus, but it's in betrayal that she simultaneously reveals dual-loyalties: connoting loyalty to her handlers who’ve supported her infiltration in Paradeus, and a loyalty to Angelia - for in betrayal, her honor towards her leader is vindicated through a will to carry them both to their promised destination, for better or worse - an independent, yet loyal soul.

Although Angelia undergoing the scalpel was unexpected, RPK16's "possession" was an apparent necessity, as Angelia could no longer carry her body to the end, so she could’ve been given this order or took the initiative to save her leader; Lyons had told Ulrich that he wouldn’t sit idly by with Angelia in captivity, so perhaps he issued that order through their communications. Tangentially, the creator of the Wolf Pack, Doctor Shaw, was a close friend of Lyons and Zelinsky who disappeared soon after RPK16 rolled off the production line, and in Mirror Stage, Lyons had contacted Angelia through RPK16’s intranet, allegedly passing through her firewalls uninterrupted. As his informant, this line of communication may have been spurred from Shaw’s relationship with Lyons and Zelinsky; theoretically, Shaw may have disappeared behind the veil to support Lyons, possibly even a Promethean herself, though little evidence of such conclusions exist. Although Lyons’ dispositions on the future of humanity is justifiably subject to scrutiny, he certainly doesn’t fall under a “malicious” umbrella - he shows respect, steadily maintains his composure, and resolves matters in calculated fashion. That said, as a friend of Shaw - both of whom seek good health for Angelia, no matter what befalls her from foolish actions - Lyons could’ve been working alongside her to gather information on Paradeus and rescue Angelia, with RPK16’s possession as a grievous necessity after Hela, aided by AK12’s infiltration.

The unique “encased” nature of RPK16’s neural cloud embodies her original namesake, Pandora: the first beautiful woman sent as divine trickery against Prometheus’ brother, Epithemeus, to punish the titans for their sin - defying the Olympians, by bestowing the graces of the divine to a timid humanity, drastically transcending consciousness and capability. As a perceived grave violation of this world’s principles, Zeus ordered a Council of Nine deities pay tribute to a “gift” for humanity; forged by the patron of crafts and the forge, Hepheastus, containing all the good and evils of the world, the infernal vessel was cast down to the world of men as a jar held by the first, magnificent woman - Pandora. Recognizing the jar’s facade, Prometheus warned Epimetheus not to fall for the woman, yet foresight failed when the jar was unsealed, unleashing the deluge of evils and sickness to a world of the arts and crafts - all that remained was hope. Although the Prometheus Council may not necessarily play the role of Prometheus in the scenario, Hephaestus crafted Pandora in the same manner as Shaw manufactured Pandora-RPK16, designed simultaneously with philosophies of the “right of defiance” and an intelligence gathering, and if Shaw, a premier weapons and technical specialist of the NUSSR, ultimately created RPK16 as an informant, perhaps her “betrayal” was the Council’s means of planting a dangle within Paradeus, whose technology - or more aptly, “fire” - they aspire is perceived as a gift cast upon Paradeus. When Shaw released “Pandora” from the production line, she was not outstanding in any way; not the raw strength of AK15, nor the calculating AK12 - she was created as an alternative partner to AK15, with a singular, unique trait of her body: an inaccessible neural cloud. Not even Paradeus managed to crack it, possibly not even Shaw herself could, but why design a Doll this way?
